지난 몇 년 동안 하나님께서 내 마음 가운데서 일하고 계신 한 영역은 복종의 문제였습니다. 잘못된 방식으로 뒤돌아보고 싶지는 않지만, 내가 하나님의 돕는 배필로서 남편에게 주신 역할에서 어떻게 실패했는지를 보게 됩니다. 제 삶을 돌아보면서 가정에서와 자녀들의 삶 가운데서 우리가 그리스도인 여성으로서 맡은 역할이 얼마나 중요한지 깨닫게 되었습니다.

우리 자녀들이 그리스도의 제자가 될지를 스스로 결정해야 한다는 것을 압니다. 그러나 나의 바람은 우리 자녀들이 하나님의 말씀에 대항하여 반역하는 이유가 내가 되지 않는 것입니다. 우리가 하나님의 말씀 안에서 가르치신 대로 남편을 존중할 때, 우리의 삶의 본은 믿지 않는 자들을 그리스도께로 이끌 것입니다. 육신으로는 우리가 하나님께 영광을 돌리게 할 방식으로 남편을 존중할 수 없지만, 그리스도 안에서 우리는 그의 뜻에 따라 모든 것을 할 수 있습니다.

최근 몇 달 동안 가정들이 영혼의 원수에게서, 또 육신과 세상을 통해 끊임없이 공격받고 있다는 것을 얼마나 많이 보았는지 때문에 이 문제에 대한 부담이 있습니다. 이 글을 쓰면서도 충분히 다루지 못할 것 같아 제 생각 일부만 적고 이 글을 읽는 모든 이들이 결혼 생활 가운데서 남편을 공경하고 존중하며 사랑하도록 격려받기를 기도합니다.

  • 그러나 아내들은 자기 남편을 존경함을 보이라 –에베소서 5:33.
  • 또 아내들이여, 자기 남편들에게 복종하라… –베드로전서 3:1.
  • 사라가 아브라함에게 순종하여 그를 주로 불렀으니: 너희는 그의 딸들이라… –베드로전서 3:6.
  • 아내들이여, 자기 남편들에게 복종하라, 주께 하듯 하라 –에베소서 5:22.
  • 그러나 나는 너희로 알게 하려니와 각 사람의 머리는 그리스도요, 여자의 머리는 남자니라; 또 그리스도의 머리는 하나님이시니라 –고린도전서 11:3.
  • 여자는 모든 복종으로 조용히 배우라. 내가 여자가 가르치거나 남자를 주장하는 것을 허락하지 아니하고 다만 조용할 것을 허락하노니 이는 먼저 아담이 지음받고 그 다음에 하와라. 아담은 속임을 받지 아니하였으나 여자가 속임을 받아 범죄하였느니라 –디모데전서 2:11-14.
  • 이와 같이 교회가 그리스도에게 복종하듯이, 아내들도 범사에 자기 남편에게 복종할지니라 –에베소서 5:24.
  • 여자들은 교회에서 잠잠할지니라: 그들에게 말하는 것이 허락되지 아니하나 오직 순종할 것을 명하였음이라 율법도 이와 같이 말하느니라 –고린도전서 14:34.

이 말씀들은 제 것이 아니라 하나님의 것입니다. 하나님은 우리가 그분의 말씀을 읽고 따라 살도록 말씀을 주셨습니다. 그것이야말로 우리가 가정에서 평화와 조화를 누릴 수 있는 유일한 길이기 때문입니다. 더 중요하게, 우리가 하나님 앞에서 깨끗한 양심을 가질 수 있는 유일한 길은 그분의 뜻의 중심에 있을 때입니다.

복종을 생각할 때 무엇이 떠오릅니까? 우리가 복종하면 이용당할 것이라고 생각합니까? 우리가 남편보다 더 지혜롭다고 생각합니까? 육신으로 들으면 이것이 다소 힘들게 들리는 것을 압니다. 그러나 우리가 남편이 앞장서 결정을 내리게 하지 않으면 남편을 무력하게 만든다는 것을 알기만 한다면 좋겠습니다. 현실은 남편이 실수하더라도 괜찮다는 것입니다. 우리 자신도 실수를 하기 때문입니다. 또한 우리가 거듭나 하나님과 동행하고 있는데 남편이 그렇지 않다면, 하나님은 여전히 우리를 돌보실 것입니다. 성경은 남편이 자기 자리 있지 않더라도, 아내가 하나님의 말씀에서 명확히 주신 가르침대로 행하면 아내의 행실을 통해(또는 삶의 처신으로) 남편이 얻을 수 있다고 가르칩니다.

우리는 결혼이라는 영역에서도 온전한 삶으로 하나님을 신뢰해야 합니다. 하나님은 질서의 하나님이십니다. 하나님이 자녀들이 부모를 공경하고 부모가 자녀를 노엽게 하지 말라 하심을 생각해 보십시오. 남편과 아내의 관계에서도 다르지 않습니다. 남편은 그리스도께서 교회를 사랑하신 것 같이 아내를 사랑할 것이요, 아내는 남편을 존경할 것입니다.

태초에 하나님은 남자와 여자를 창조하셨습니다. 하나님은 아담을 지으시고 그가 혼자 있는 것이 좋지 않다고 하시며, 아담의 갈비뼈로 여자를 지으셨습니다. 처음에 하나님의 마음은 남자와 여자가 하나 되어 함께 하나님과 동행하며 그분을 영화롭게 하는 것이었습니다. 그러나 아담과 하와가 유혹에 굴복함으로써 죄가 세상에 들어왔습니다. 우리가 결혼생활에서 어려움을 겪을 때마다 먼저 유혹에 굴복한 사람이 하와였음을 생각하게 됩니다. 아내된 우리는 우리 마음을 신속히 살펴 우리가 제자리에 있는지 확실히 해야 합니다. 상황이 생길 때, 얼마나 자주 우리가 여자로서 남편보다 더 잘 알고 상황을 더 잘 처리할 수 있다고 생각하는 유혹을 받습니까?

하나님은 우리가 그들 아래에 있을 때 남편을 우리의 보호자로 설계하셨습니다. 우리가 불완전하다는 것을 알고 있기 때문에 남편에게 복종하는 것이 더욱 어렵습니다. 그러나 우리가 성령으로 거듭날 때 그분의 사랑이 우리 안에서 우리로 하여금 남편에게 복종하도록 능하게 한다고 믿습니다. 또한 많은 가정이 깨어져 있음을 압니다. 이상적이지 못한 상황에 있는 누구에게든 내 게 드리는 격려는 진실로 기도하라는 것입니다…먼저 자신을 위해 흠 없게 행할 수 있도록, 그리고 남편이 하나님께서 그를 설계하신 그 사람이 되도록(네가 생각하는 사람이 아니라) 남편을 위해 기도하십시오. 우리는 종종 이 점에 대해 혼란스러워하여 남편에 대해 나쁜 생각을 갖게 됩니다.

디도서는 자매들에게 하나님으로부터 명확한 방향을 줍니다. 늙은 여인들도 이와 같이 하여 … 선한 일을 가르치는 자가 되게 하라. 젊은 여인들로 절제하며 자기 남편을 사랑하며 자녀를 사랑하며 이성을 지키고 가정에 충실하며 착하고 자기 남편에게 복종하여 하나님의 말씀을 욕되게 하지 않게 하라 –디도서 2:3-5.

또 다른 유혹은 우리가 다른 남자들과 남편을 비교하는 것입니다. 어쩌면 우리는 남편에게 이 다른 사람은 네가 하는 식으로 하지 않을 거라고 말할지도 모릅니다. 혹은 그 사람이 하는 방식이 네가 하는 방식보다 낫다고 말할 수도 있습니다. 이런 말들을 하지 않더라도 우리의 행동이 남편에게 많은 것을 말해 줄 수 있습니다. 하나님의 말씀은 우리에게 자기 남편에게 순종하라고 가르칩니다, 다른 사람에게가 아니라. 각 남편은 다른 방식으로 은사가 주어졌고, 그 때문에 각 아내는 자신의 남편에게 특별히 적합한 것입니다. 주 하나님이 이르시되 사람이 홀로 있는 것이 좋지 아니하니 내가 그를 위하여 돕는 배필을 지으리라 –창세기 2:18.

젊은 여인들로 절제하며 자기 남편을 사랑하며 자녀를 사랑하며 –디도서 2:4. 여기서 자기 남편을 사랑하며의 “사랑”이라는 단어는 “남편에게 애정으로 기움”을 의미하고, 자녀를 사랑하며의 “사랑”은 “자녀에 대한 어머니적 애정”을 의미합니다. 우리는 남편에게 어떤 종류의 사랑을 보이고 있습니까? 남편이 우리가 그들의 선을 바라고 있다는 것을 신뢰할 수 있습니까, 아니면 무언가를 얻기 위해 사랑하는 척 하고 있습니까? 참사랑은 실패에도 불구하고 용서할 것입니다, 우리가 고통이 너무 커서 견딜 수 없다고 생각할지라도. 참사랑은 우리가 남편과 무언가에 대해 다르게 느낄 때 우리 자신과 남편을 위해 기도하게 할 것입니다. 참사랑은 우리를 절망에 빠뜨리지 않고 오히려 하나님을 더 찾게 할 것입니다.

남편의 허물을 다른 사람에게 말하려는 유혹을 받을 때 그 유혹에 굴복하지 말고 그들을 위해 기도합시다. 우리가 다른 사람들에게 우리의 허물을 남편이 이야기하는 것을 좋아할까요? 또한 남편이 연루된 죄에 대해 누군가에게 언제 말해야 할지 분별력을 위해 기도합시다. 어려움이 생겼을 때 남편을 비방하거나 잔소리하지 맙시다. 대신 하나님께 우리의 삶 가운데서 일하도록 구하고 문제를 그분께 맡기십시오. 우리 남편도 우리처럼 너무나도 인간적입니다. 우리가 때때로 실패한다면 그들도 때때로 실패할 수 있음을 놀라워하지 말아야 합니다. 나는 우리 결혼을 온전하게 만드는 것은 우리가 서로 용서하고 하나가 되기 위해 나아가는 법을 배우는 것이라고 생각합니다.

또 아내들이여, 자기 남편들에게 복종하라. 만일 어떤 이들이 말에 순종하지 아니하면 아내들의 행실로 말 없이 얻을 수도 있으니 그들이 너희의 정결한 행실을 두려움과 함께 보고 있을 때라. 사라가 아브라함에게 순종하여 그를 주라 칭하였으니 너희는 그의 딸들이라 네가 선을 행하고 아무 두려움으로 놀라지 아니하면 그리하라. 이와 같이 남편들도 지식으로 아내와 거하고 아내를 연약한 그릇으로 깨끗이 존중하며 생명의 은혜를 함께 유업으로 받는 자로 여기라; 그리하면 너희의 기도가 막히지 아니하리라 –베드로전서 3:1-2 & 3:6-7.

이 구절이 우리에게 처음으로 실제가 되었던 때 중 하나는 첫 아이가 생후 약 다섯 달쯤 되었을 때였습니다. 우리는 집에서 꽤 멀리 있었고 아이가 큰 통증으로 울기 시작했습니다. 우리는 그를 위해 기도했지만 계속 울었습니다. 무슨 문제가 있는지 몰라 응급실로 데려갔습니다. 그들은 귀 감염이라고 말하고 약을 주었습니다. 그러나 아이는 여전히 울었습니다. 우리는 집으로 가는 데 열 시간의 여정이 있었고 그는 내내 울었습니다. 집에 돌아온 후 남편과 나는 우리 사이에 풀리지 않은 문제가 있음을 발견했습니다. 우리가 서로와 하나님 앞에서 잘못을 고백한 후 다시 우리 아들을 위해 기도했습니다. 우리가 기도하자마자 아들은 즉시 울음을 멈추었습니다. 모든 상황이 이와 같이 끝나지는 않겠지만 하나님은 우리에게 숨겨진 죄 없이 서로에게 열린 마음을 가져야 우리의 기도가 막히지 않는다는 것을 가르쳐 주셨습니다.

물어볼 수 있는 몇 가지 질문들: 우리 자녀들은 가정에서 무엇을 보고 있습니까? 그들이 아버지를 기쁨으로 존경하는 어머니를 보고 있습니까, 아니면 두려움으로 보고 있습니까? 어머니가 남편에게 적절히 애정을 표현하는 것을 보고 있습니까, 예를 들어 친절한 말, 그가 좋아하는 것을 함께 사랑하려는 시도, 손을 잡는 행동 등(우리 사이에 무언가 있으면 남편과 손을 잡기 어렵다는 것을 깨달았습니다). 어머니가 아버지의 행위를 질문하고 도전하거나 비판합니까?

우리 자녀들이 성장하여 청소년기에 이르렀을 때 이 원칙들이 가정에서 실행되는 것이 얼마나 중요한지 봅니다. 우리가 공개적으로 남편의 권위를 의심하면 자녀들에게도 아버지의 권위를 의심하도록 씨를 뿌리고 있다고 믿습니다. 궁극적으로 우리가 사는 시대에 우리는 하나님의 창조 질서에 대해 모든 것을 의심하는 세대를 보고 있습니다—성별 혼란, 진화론, 그리고 전반적인 권위에 대한 반역이 있습니다. 나는 평범한 교회들에서 이렇게 많은 반역을 보는 이유가 가정에서 하나님의 질서가 실천되지 않았기 때문인지 종종 궁금해했습니다.

우리의 한 친구는 가정에 가장 큰 영향을 미칠 단 하나의 기독교 원칙을 꼽으라면 머리의 권위 원칙이라고 말했습니다. 우리가 아는 사랑하는 친구 중 한 명은 남편보다 먼저 그리스도인이 되었습니다. 그녀는 많은 어려움을 겪었지만 계속해서 남편을 사랑하고 존경했습니다. 그녀는 여러 해 동안 금식하며 남편을 위해 기도했습니다. 오늘날 그녀의 남편은 아내의 경건한 행실이 그를 회개와 그리스도 안의 믿음으로 이끌었다고 증언할 것입니다.

다른 결과의 예도 있습니다… 나는 견고한 결혼이 아니었던 한 부부를 압니다. 남편이 그의 자리에 있지 않았고 아내는 쓰라리게 되었습니다. 그녀는 너무나도 쓰라려서 무덤에 묻힐 때 남편 옆에 묻히고 싶지 않다고 말하기까지 했습니다. 이런 깊은 쓰라림은 자녀들에게 끔찍한 영향을 미쳤습니다. 내가 생각하기에 그녀가 그렇게 쓰라리지 않았다면 적어도 자녀들이 겪은 많은 마음의 상처를 면하게 할 수 있지 않았을까 싶습니다.

또 다른 부부는 가까운 가족에게 심하게 학대받았지만 쓰라림을 택하지 않았습니다. 그들은 그 골짜기를 통해 하나님과 서로에게 더 가까워졌고 오늘날까지 그 선택의 열매를 거두고 있습니다.

더 개인적인 이야기로… 저는 비기독교 가정에서 자랐습니다. 부모님 두 분 다 거듭나신 분들이 아니었습니다. 그분들이 하나님께 마음을 열기 시작하셨을 때 나는 그것을 볼 수 있었습니다. 나는 모임에서 돌아와 아버지가 성경을 읽으며 울고 있는 것을 보곤 했습니다. 또한 어느 저녁에 집에 돌아왔을 때 부모님이 식탁에 앉아 함께 찬양을 부르고 계셨습니다. 나는 이것이 내 삶에 엄청난 영향을 미쳤음을 증언합니다. 또한 어머니가 하나님의 설계대로 자기 자리에 있기를 원하시는 모습을 볼 수 있었습니다. 우리가 이 생을 떠날 때 우리 가족은 우리에 대해 무엇이라고 말할 것입니까? 그들이 우리의 죽을 육신 가운데 하나님의 사랑이 다스렸다고 증언할까요?

실용적인 면에서, 남편을 말뿐이 아니라 행동으로 사랑하고 있음을 보여줄 수 있는 몇 가지 방법을 적어 보겠습니다.

  • 그들에게 조언을 구하기(단지 우리가 생각하는 대로만 하지 않기)
  • 그가 좋아하는 음식을 만들어 주기
  • 집을 정돈되고 깔끔하게 유지하기
  • 남편이 필요로 하는 어떤 일이든 돕기 위해 우리의 계획을 기꺼이 포기할 준비와 의지 가지기
  • 문에서 미소로 맞이하기(아무리 힘든 날을 보냈더라도)
  • 그가 쉬거나 공부하려 할 때(어린 아이들이 있더라도) 집을 조용히 유지하기
  • 가정에서 서로를 대할 때 자녀들에게 올바른 예절을 가르치기
  • 아버지가 항상 완벽하지 않더라도 자녀들에게 아버지를 사랑하고 존경하도록 가르치기

또 한 가지 각 기혼 자매에게 드리고 싶은 도전은 남편에게 그와 함께 있음으로 축복받았다고 말할 수 있는 것을 생각해 보라는 것입니다. 2주 동안 매일 이것을 시도해 보십시오. 친절이 결혼에 미치는 영향이 얼마나 놀라운지 보게 될 것입니다. 어떤 이들에게는 이것이 단조롭게 보일 수도 있지만 그렇지 않습니다. 우리가 나이가 들수록 얼마나 생각이 닮아 가는지, 때로는 서로의 문장을 완성하기까지 하는지 놀랍습니다. 더 많이 쓸 수 있었지만 하나님을 구할 때 우리에게 계속해서 그의 말씀을 열어 주실 것을 신뢰합니다.

편집자 주:

저는 복종하는 법을 몰라 몇 년 동안 크게 고심했던 사람 중 하나였습니다. 아래는 하나님께서 저에게 가르쳐 오신 것을 나누려는 제 시도입니다.

많은 사람이 “복종”으로 고심하는 주요한 이유 중 하나는 그들이 하나님이 그 주제로 의미하시는 바, 즉 성경적 복종의 실체를 제대로 이해하지 못하기 때문입니다. 보통 사람은 어떤 주제에 대해 자신이 무엇을 믿는지 알고 있으므로, 그들이 그 관점에서 “복종”하라는 요청을 받을 때 자신의 개인적 신념을 타협하거나 양심에 반하는 일을 하라는 요청을 받고 있다고 생각합니다.

답은 이중적입니다.

첫째, 두 사람이 어떤 문제에 대해 동의하면 누구도 복종할 필요가 없습니다. 그러므로 복종한다는 것은 복종하는 사람이 반드시 마음을 바꾸는 것을 의미하지 않습니다. 오히려 그들은 하나님께서 한 사람을 그 당사자—부부, 가정, 학교, 교회 등—의 결정에 대해 책임을 지우신 사람으로 보신다는 사실에 근거하여 다른 사람의 결정을 지지하기로 선택하는 것입니다.

둘째, 하나님은 여러 사람이 어떤 결정을 논의할 때 그 중 한 사람이 결국 다른 사람에게 복종하게 될 것을 아셨습니다. 그러므로 책임의 명확성을 제공하기 위해 그분은 각 종류의 상황에서 누구를 책임 있는 사람(영적 권위)으로 보시는지에 대해 명확한 방향을 주십니다—결혼에서는 남편, 가정에서는 아버지, 가정에서는 남자(머리), 교회에서는 안수된 지도자들, 학교 환경에서는 교사/교장 등. 그렇게 함으로써 누구든지 어떤 실수가 있을 때 하나님이 누구를 책임으로 보시는지 알 수 있게 됩니다.

에덴동산에서 하와가 먼저 그 열매를 따서 먹고 남편에게도 주었음에도 불구하고, 하나님은 그 실패(죄)에 대해 누구를 책임으로 보시는지에 대해 명확성을 주십니다. 그러므로 한 사람(한 여자가 아니라)으로 말미암아 죄가 세상에 들어가고 죄로 말미암아 사망이 왔나니 이와 같이 사망이 모든 사람에게 이르렀나니 이는 모든 사람이 죄를 범하였음이라 … 그러나 사망이 아담으로 말미암아 왕 노릇하였느니라 (여하와가 아니라) 모세까지도, 아담의 범죄의 모양을 따르지 아니한 자들에게까지도 –로마서 5:12-14.

그러므로 우리는 권위 아래에 있는 모든 사람에게 그 권위 아래에 머물면 하나님께서 보호와 안전을 제공하심을 봅니다. 각 관계에서 하나님이 분명히 권위자로 규정하신 사람은 그 집단의 결정에 대해 항상 책임을 지는 사람입니다. 에덴동산의 타락 때처럼 각 가정 내에서의 누락된 죄와 행한 죄는 주로 아버지에게 물을 것입니다. 아버지가 가정에 잘못된 방향을 주었든 전혀 방향을 주지 않았든 상관없이, 하나님은 남자를 그의 가정의 머리로 보시기 때문에 그에게 책임을 물으실 것입니다. (고린도전서 11:3 및 로마서 13:12 참조)

And there arose a great storm of wind, and the waves beat into the ship, so that it was now full. And he was in the hinder part of the ship, asleep on a pillow: and they awake him, and say unto him, Master, carest thou not that we perish? And he arose, and rebuked the wind, and said unto the sea, Peace, be still. And the wind ceased, and there was a great calm. And he said unto them, Why are ye so fearful? how is it that ye have no faith? And they feared exceedingly, and said one to another, What manner of man is this, that even the wind and the sea obey him? Mark 4:37-41

Many times, I have read this passage and wondered what we are to derive from it. It seems to be a story that generates more questions than it solves. We often like to think of Jesus as the relational form of the Godhead; a sort of go-between, between us and the Almighty God. But here, in our scriptural passage, His behavior is almost unthinkable in human terms. How could Christ sleep in such a storm, much less in a boat filling with water? We can believe that He is Master of the wind and seas, and they must bow at His command, but does He expect us to do the same? Would our compassionate Christ expect us to be calm and fearless in such dire straits? Is all exhibition of fear the fruit of our lack of faith? These probing questions are disturbing, for we all would hope that our faith in Him is strong enough to secure our salvation, yet experience has taught us that our own walk through the troublesome pastures of life has produced nothing more noble than the harrowing bleating of the disciples.

Why are ye so fearful? How is it that ye have no faith? The questions seem almost out of place coming from our Saviour, almost as though He is not as patient and longsuffering as we had hoped. But Christ has placed a definitive expectation upon His disciples that is not beyond their attainment. Was He calling on them to rebuke the storm themselves? Should they have awakened Him sooner? Did he expect them to quietly row on in confident assurance? The Scripture here supplies us with few answers, but we do know that there is an abiding lesson here concerning fear and faith.

Storms are a common part of life, and no major dilemma is pleasant. While Paul sailed toward Rome, they experienced a time …when neither sun nor stars in many days appeared, and no small tempest lay on us, all hope that we should be saved was then taken away –Acts 27:20. In the midst of a cloudy and hopeless situation there is one bell that continues to toll clear and bright: There is a peace that can be apprehended even in the most dreadful circumstances. Paul had spent a precarious …night and a day I have been in the deep –2 Corinthians 11:25, yet he did not demand the wind and sea to submit to his authority. Rather, he states that in the midst of the storm …there stood by me this night the angel of God, whose I am, and whom I serve, Saying, Fear not, Paul… –Acts 27:23-24. This is a scene similar to the peril being endured by the disciples (in our text for today) yet we see a different outcome. Paul was comforted and commended while the disciples received rebuke.

While bobbing about in the clutches of a potential watery grave, the disciples cried out: …Master, carest thou not that we perish? –Mark 4:38. How natural it is for us all to thrust our frustration and blame upon another. To think that some apathetic person is shirking their responsibility is very disheartening. In like fashion …the shipmaster came to him [Jonah], and said unto him, What meanest thou, O sleeper? arise, call upon thy God, if so be that God will think upon us, that we perish not –Jonah 1:6.

There seems to be an edge to the shipmaster’s rebuke very similar to the disciple’s response to the sleeping Jesus. Christ finds no pleasure in allowing trouble to visit us, but there seems to be no other veritable vehicle of grace wherewith His peace can flood our souls. If there first be no valley, how shall we value the mountaintop? If there be no thorns, how shall we enjoy the rose? If there first be no storm, how shall we appreciate the calm? Paul suffered the same despair being …pressed out of measure, above strength, insomuch that we despaired even of life –2 Corinthians 1:8. Yet he carried within his breast a visionary anchor for his soul.

For he commandeth, and raiseth the stormy wind, which lifteth up the waves thereof. They mount up to the heaven, they go down again to the depths: their soul is melted because of trouble. They reel to and fro, and stagger like a drunken man, and are at their wits’ end. Then they cry unto the LORD in their trouble, and he bringeth them out of their distresses. He maketh the storm a calm, so that the waves thereof are still. Then are they glad because they be quiet; so he bringeth them unto their desired haven –Psalm 107:25-30.

The Desired Haven…

Somehow, we have embraced the thought that the desired haven of rest is an earthly euphoric utopia void of any storms. The shipmaster in charge of guiding the vessel en route to Rome thought that …the haven was not commodious to winter in … supposing that they had obtained their purpose… –Acts 27:12-13, so he set sail at the first hint of approval from the soft south wind. But the haven Christ promotes is a harbor that is free from fretful fear and fledgling faith. This is a peace … not as the world giveth, give I unto you. Let not your heart be troubled, neither let it be afraid –John 14:27. This rest is ours to be had just by sailing with Christ and trusting Him to guide us through each storm.

The tenacious storms of adversity can arise without warning as quickly as …a tempestuous wind, called Euroclydon –Acts 27:14. These tempestuous winds carry an amazing audacity to jolt any relationship. To feel tense and alert in the midst of stressful situations is but human nature. Our central medulla gland unleashes a powerful hormone called adrenaline into our system, our muscles become tense, our mind focuses, so that we are aroused and prepared for fight or flight. This is not necessarily anxiety but a natural response. As humans, we have a divine capacity to reason in the midst of extreme passion and pressure. The disciples did not know what Jesus would do. They only knew that this situation was out of control. Here is where they made their major mistake. Christ knew Who was in control. Paul knew Who was in control. Even Jonah knew why the tempest had arisen. Our faith is bound to fail when anxiety escalates, and we think we must control the raging trials about us. We may have a noble agenda and a sincere heart and still find our faltering faith frazzled. We mistakenly marvel that God sits in heaven and does nothing. We faithfully launch our prayers upward, but the heavens seem brazenly silent. We would expect that from worshippers of Baal, Buddha, and from backsliders. But it is not supposed to happen to people with strong convictions—people who are born again, attend church regularly, read their Bible, and pray on a daily basis. We must reconsider that God is not so concerned about our environmental peace, but rather that our inner soul arrives safe and sound at His haven of rest.

When we are happy, we jubilantly claim that rest, even though we have no sense of truly needing Him. His insertions into our lives often seem like interruptions. But when times get desperate and we have exhausted all our resources, we lean hard upon Him. In that excruciating hour, He often tests our sincerity and offers us nothing … nothing but silence. Christ, sleeping in our boat. Sleeping… right when we need him the most. And then the question, Why are ye so fearful? How is it that ye have no faith? Frankly, this seems hard to me—even harsh—and entirely out of character with what I would normally expect from Jesus. But the question must be answered, for it is necessary if we wish to enter His haven of rest. The winds obey Him, but they don’t obey us … or do they? We obviously cannot control the weather, our environment, our situations, or the people around us. Yet these externals are not the root cause of our anxiety. It is our own faulty premonitions that pound our soul and prevent us from entering the portal of peace. The winds that whip our vessel into a fearful frenzy are not driven from without but unleashed from within. This anxiety rides on the waves of unbelief, while Christ continues in His divine slumber, waiting until we recognize the source of our anxiety and call out in faith. These four strong winds are roused at the slightest provocation when we are…

…Preserving our Person

If we are healthy, and if things are going well in our family and finances, we may be prone to misinterpret our circumstances. It is a mistake to believe that easy sailing is a mark of God’s favor, and that trouble is a sign of His displeasure. All good and perfect gifts come from God, but a debilitating storm can fall under that category as well. Our personal surroundings are temporal while our soul is eternal. God will frequently expend our personal comforts in order to expand our faith. But great fear arises when our person is demoted. Many of our phobias arise in the absence of actual danger.

  1. The acrophobic person has a fear of heights and is afraid he will fall from the heights of any platform though it is secure and guarded well. Even if countless others have successfully stood there, he is miserably trapped in this fear, not because he is in danger, but because he has grossly overestimated his likelihood of falling and refuses to believe the truth.
  2. The zoophobic lives in fear of animals, creating images in his mind of being clawed to death or disemboweled.
  3. The claustrophobic is afraid of small, tight places, while the agoraphobic fears open places.
  4. Arachibutyrophobia is the fear of getting peanut butter stuck to the roof of your mouth.

In the face of his fear, the phobic may experience a racing heart, heavy breathing, dry mouth, perspiration, dizziness, or light-headedness. Thus, their phobias become real to them. While most will excuse their personal glitch, the truth remains that this anxiety is unfounded. When we excuse and cater to the preservation of our person, fear is inevitable. The disciples feared that they were perishing, and Christ asked them why. Is it not better …to depart, and to be with Christ; which is far better –Philippians 1:23. If we can trust Christ with our life, can we not trust him with our death?

For whosoever will save his life shall lose it; but whosoever shall lose his life for my sake and the gospel’s, the same shall save it –Mark 8:35.

…Protecting our Property

Outwardly, the life of Christ was one of the most troubled lives that was ever lived. Foxes had their dens and the birds had their nests while He lay His pillow in the back of a rocking boat groaning under tempest and tumult of the incessant waves breaking over it. But His inner haven was a sea of glass. This was partially due to the fact that He had no property to protect. Even the boat was borrowed. “Much coin, much care” states the ancient proverb, and anxiety rises when wealth falls. And one of the company said unto him, Master, speak to my brother, that he divide the inheritance with me –Luke 12:13. Jesus refused to side with him. Instead, He spoke to the covetous heart that was causing the anxiety. If Christ gives us wealth, we do not need to feel guilty. If He takes it, we do not need to feel anxiety. In the midst of the storm, we are exhorted …to be of good cheer: for there shall be no loss of any man’s life among you, but of the ship –Acts 27:22. This was ministered as healing balm to the bedraggled sailors, but to those who feel inclined to protect their property it is a sordid saga. When the rich young ruler was offered salvation in exchange for his earthly collection of trinkets, …he went away sorrowful: for he had great possessions –Matthew 19:22. Those of us who become anxious at the loss of our wealth are no less foolish.

…Perfecting our Plan

We set out on a course. Maybe we change jobs, enter into a relationship, or embark upon some new avenue of ministry. We have launched out in faith and before we know it, we are struggling. The winds and waves of ordinary life seem to be working against us. We have expectations that are not being met and it seems that Christ is not doing His part. It is not Christ, but rather it is our expectation that is the cause of our anxiety. We expect much from our investments and it is discouraging to see our efforts go for naught. Martha’s pulse quickened at the lack of help she was receiving in the kitchen. Her frustration rose while her well-planned meal remained unfinished. Her complaint is no less accusing than the disciples’ while rowing in the sea. …Lord, dost thou not care that my sister hath left me to serve alone? bid her therefore that she help me –Luke 10:40. Her anxiety was not caused by Mary’s neglect nor Christ’s indifference. Her sister was docked at the haven of rest while Martha battled the tumultuous emotions within her heart. So does the perfectionist create his own storm when his unfulfilled vision falls short of his expectations. But Christ is more concerned about faith-filled bosoms than water-filled boats.

…Pleasing all People

The Scriptures have taught us well to love our neighbor as ourselves, but that does not insinuate that we must strive and aim for their approval. It feels wonderful to be liked. It is painful to be rejected. Thus, many souls spend their waking hours seeking the approval of others. They must dress like, act like, talk like, and live like their peers. These live a life laden with stressful waves of anxiety. A flurry of “what ifs” arrive with each new acquaintance. There is no ship more fragile than a relationship. No matter how great a sacrifice we make to be loved, we will eventually encounter a disappointing squall sucking us down to the depths of despair. When our best efforts fail us and our best friends derail us, we must bring our battered vessel to the haven of rest. Inconvenient, unfortunate, unpleasant, and annoying relationships will always exist. We shall do much better to make excuses for others’ poor behavior than for our own. When we can rebuke the winds that arise within our own minds, we will immediately find ourselves at the desired haven.

There remaineth therefore a rest to the people of God. For he that is entered into his rest, he also hath ceased from his own works, as God did from his. Let us labour therefore to enter into that rest… –Hebrews 4:9-11.

এবং হঠাৎ এক প্রবল ঝড় উঠল, এবং ঢেউগুলি জাহাজে ধাক্কা দিল এমনভাবে যে এখন এটি পুরোটাই জল ভর্তি হয়ে গেল। আর তিনি নৌকাটির পশ্চাৎভাগে একটা বালিশে মাথা রেখে ঘুমিয়ে ছিলেন; তখন তাঁরা তাঁকে জাগিয়ে বলল, আরস্য, আমাদের কি তুমি পরিত্যাগ করতে চাও—আমরা কি নাশ হব?। তিনি উঠলেন, এবং সেই ঝড়কে তিরস্কার করলেন, এবং সমুদ্রকে বললেন, শান্ত হয়ে যাও। আর ঝড় থমকে গেল, এবং বড়ই শান্তি হল। তখন তিনি তাদেরকে বললেন, তোমরা কেন এত ভয়গ্রস্ত? কিভাবে তোমাদের বিশ্বাস নেই? তখন তাঁরা অত্যন্ত ভয় পেল, এবং একে অপরকে বলল, এই ব্যক্তি কী রকম— যে এমনকি বায়ুও ও সমুদ্রও তাঁর আজ্ঞা মানে? — মার্ক 4:37-41

অনেকবার আমি এই পদ্যাংশ পড়েছি এবং বিস্ময় করেছি এতে থেকে আমাদের কী শিক্ষা গ্রহণ করা উচিত। এটা এমন এক কাহিনী বলে মনে হয় যা সমাধানের চেয়ে বেশি প্রশ্ন উত্পন্ন করে। আমরা প্রায়ই যীশুকে ঈশ্বরত্বের সম্পর্কগত রূপ হিসেবে ভাবতে পছন্দ করি; আমাদের এবং সর্বশক্তিমান ঈশ্বরের মধ্যবর্তী এক ধরণের মাঝামাঝি হিসেবে। কিন্তু এখানে, আমাদের বাইবেলের অংশে, তাঁর আচরণ মানবিক পরিভাষায় প্রায় অবিশ্বাস্য। এমন ঝড়ের মধ্যে কিভাবে খ্রিস্ট এমনভাবে ঘুমাতে পারতেন, তাতে তো নৌকাটিও জল ভর্তি হচ্ছে? আমরা বিশ্বাস করতে পারি যে তিনি বাতাস ও সাগরের অধিপতি, এবং তারা তাঁর আজ্ঞায় মাথা নত করে, কিন্তু তিনি কি আমাদেরকেও একই প্রত্যাশা রাখেন? আমাদের সহানুভূতিশীল খ্রিস্ট কি এত ভয়াবহ পরিস্থিতিতে আমাদের শান্ত ও নির্ভীক থাকার প্রত্যাশা করতেন? সব ভয়ের প্রকাশ কি আমাদের বিশ্বাসের অভাবের ফল? এসব খুঁত Sik প্রশ্ন সবচেয়ে বিরক্তিকর, কারণ আমরা সবাই আশা করবো যে তাঁর প্রতি আমাদের বিশ্বাস আমাদের উদ্ধার নিশ্চিত করতে যথেষ্ট শক্ত—তবে অভিজ্ঞতা আমাদের শিখিয়েছে যে জীবনের বিপৎসম চারণভূমি অতিক্রান্ত করার আমাদের পথ প্রায়ই শিষ্যদের ভীত কণ্ঠস্বর ছাড়া আর কিছু দেয়নি।

তোমরা কেন এত ভয়গ্রস্ত? কিভাবে তোমাদের বিশ্বাস নেই? আমাদের পরিত্রাতার তরফ থেকে এ ধরণের প্রশ্ন ত্যাগ করা প্রায় অনুপযুক্ত মনে হয়, যেন তিনি এত ধৈর্যশীল ও সহিষ্ণু নন যতটা আমরা আশা করেছিলাম। কিন্তু খ্রিস্ট তাঁর শিষ্যদের উপর একটি নির্দিষ্ট প্রত্যাশা স্থাপন করেছেন যা তাদের অর্জনের বাইরে নয়। তিনি কি তাদেরকে নিজে ঝড়কে তিরস্কার করার আহ্বান করছিলেন? তাঁরা কি তাঁকে দ্রুত জাগাতে পারতেন? তিনি কি প্রত্যাশা করতেন যে তারা নির্ভয়ে নিশ্চিন্তভাবে নৌকা চালিয়ে যাবে? এখানে শাস্ত্র আমাদেরকে অল্প উত্তর দেয়, তবে আমরা জানি যে ভয় ও বিশ্বাস সম্পর্কে এখানে একটি স্থায়ী শিক্ষা আছে।

ঝড় জীবনেই সাধারণ, এবং কোনো বড় সংকটই আনন্দদায়ক নয়। পল রোমের উদ্দেশ্যে যাত্রা করে গিয়ে একটি সময় অভিজ্ঞ হয়েছিলেন …যখন বহু দিন হইতে সূর্য না তবু নক্ষত্রই দৃশ্যমান হইলো না, এবং আমাদের উপর একটি ছোট্ট ঝড়ও ছিল না, তখন আমাদের বাঁচবার সমস্ত আশাই এবার কেড়ে নেওয়া হল—প্রেরিতদের কাজ 27:20। মেঘলা ও নিঃসত্ত্ব পরিস্থিতির মাঝখানে একটি ঘণ্টা পরিষ্কার ও উজ্জ্বলভাবে বাজতে থাকে: এমন একটি শান্তি আছে যা সবচেয়ে ভয়ঙ্কর পরিস্থিতিতেও ধরবার যোগ্য। পল একটি ঝুঁকিপূর্ণ …রাত এবং একটি দিন আমি গভীরে ছিলাম—2 করিন্থীয় 11:25 অতিবাহিত করেছিলেন, তবু তিনি বাতাস ও সমুদ্রকে তাঁর কর্তৃত্বে আনতে দাবি করেননি। বরং তিনি বলেন যে ঝড়ের মধ্যেই …এই রাত্রে আমার পাশে ছিলেন ঈশ্বরের দূত, যাঁর আমি, এবং যাঁকে আমি দাসত্ব করি, বলিয়া, ভয় পিও না, পল…—প্রেরিতদের কাজ 27:23-24। এটি এমন এক দৃশ্য যা আমাদের পাঠ্যের শিষ্যদের পার হওয়া বিপদের সঙ্গে সদৃশ, তবু আমরা ভিন্ন ফলাফল দেখি। পল সান্ত্বনা ও প্রশংসিত হন, অপরদিকে শিষ্যরা তিরস্কার পায়।

সম্ভবত একটি জলের কবরের হুড়োহুড়ি ভোগ করতে থাকা অবস্থায়, শিষ্যরা চিৎকার করে বলল: …আরস্য, তুমি কি আমরা নাশ পাই বলে উদ্বেগ করো না?—মার্ক 4:38। আমাদের সকলের জন্য নিজের হতাশা ও দোষ আরেকের ওপর চাপানো কত প্রাকৃতিক। মনে করা যে কোনো উদাসীন ব্যক্তি তাঁর দায় এড়িয়ে যাচ্ছে খুবই হতাশাজনক। অনুরূপভাবে …জাহাজের প্রধান তাঁর কাছে এহেন বলিল, তুমি ঘুমন্ত লোক, তুই কী করিতেছিস? উঠ, তোর ঈশ্বরকে আহ্বান কর, হইবে তো ঈশ্বর আমাদের চিন্তা করিবেন, আমরা নষ্ট না হইবার জন্য—যোনাহ 1:6।

জাহাজের প্রধানের তিরস্কারে একটি ধার দেখা যায় যা শিষ্যদের ঘুমন্ত যীশুর প্রতি সাড়া দেওয়ার সঙ্গে খুব সদৃশ। খ্রীষ্টে কষ্টের আগমনকে অনুমোদন করায় কোনো আনন্দ নেই, কিন্তু মনে হয় তাঁর শান্তি আমাদের আত্মায় প্রবাহিত হওয়ার আর কোনো প্রকৃত মাধ্যম নেই। যদি প্রথমে কোনো উপত্যকা না থাকে, তবে আমরা কীভাবে শৃঙ্গের মূল্য জানব? যদি প্রথমে বিষোদগার না থাকে, আমরা কীভাবে গোলাপের আনন্দ উপভোগ করব? যদি প্রথমে কোন ঝড় না থাকে, আমরা কীভাবে শান্তিকে কদর করব? পল একই হতাশা ভোগ করেছিলেন যখন তিনি …পরিমাপে চাপিত, শক্তির ওপরে, এমন যে আমরা জীবন পর্যন্তই হতাশ হলাম—2 করিন্থীয় 1:8। তবু তিনি তাঁর হৃদয়ে একটি দ্যৈব_anchor ধারণ করতেন।

কারণ তিনি আজ্ঞা দেন, এবং ঝড়ো বাতাস উত্থাপন করেন, যে তাহার ঢেউগুলোকে উত্তোলন করে। সেগুলো তারা আকাশে উঠে যায়, আবার গভীরে নামে: তন্মধ্যে তেওঁলোকের আত্মা দুঃখে গলে যায়। তাঁরা দোলায় আর ফিরে যায়, এবং মাতাল মানুষের মতো দাঁড়ায়, এবং তাঁদের বিবেচনার শেষ হয়। তখন তাঁরা তাদের কষ্টে প্রভুকে ডাকায়, এবং তিনি তাদের কষ্ট হতে তোলা করান। তিনি ঝড়কে শান্ত করেন, যাতে তাহার ঢেউ নীরব হয়। তখন তারা আনন্দ করে, কারণ তিনি তাদের নির্ঝঞ্ঝাট করেন; তিনি তাদেরকে তাদের কাঙ্খিত আশ্রয়ে নিয়ে যান—নিয়ামক 107:25-30।

কাঙ্খিত আশ্রয়…

কখনো না কখনো আমরা এমন ধারণা গ্রহণ করে নিয়েছি যে বিশ্রামের কাঙ্খিত আশ্র্য একটি ভৌত উভোরিয়ান ইউটোপিয়া যেখানে কোনো ঝড় নেই। রোমের পথে জাহাজটি পরিচালনার দায়িত্বে থাকা জাহাজক্রমিক মনে করেছিলেন …এই আশ্রয় শীতকালে বসবাসের উপযোগী নয় … ধারনা করিয়া যে তারা তাদের উদ্দেশ্য লাভ করিয়াছে…—প্রেরিতদের কাজ 27:12-13, তাই তিনি দক্ষিণের নরম বায়ুর প্রথম ইঙ্গিতেই যাত্রা শুরু করলেন। কিন্তু খ্রিষ্ট যে আশ্রয় প্রচার করেন তা এমন এক খানঘর যেখানে উদ্বিগ্ন ভয় ও দোলাখরা বিশ্বাস নেই। এটি এমন একটি শান্তি যা …যে শান্তি পৃথিবী দেয় না, তুমি আমি দিই। তোমার হৃদয় উদ্বিগ্ন হউক না, ন কী ভয় পাও—ইওহান্ন 14:27। এই বিশ্রামটি আমাদের পাওয়ার জিনিস, শুধুমাত্র খ্রিস্টের সঙ্গে ভ্রমণ করে এবং প্রত্যেক ঝড়ে তাঁকে আমাদের পথপ্রদর্শক হিসেবে বিশ্বাস করে।

দুর্যোগের অনমনীয় ঝড়গুলি ঝটিতভাবে উঠতে পারে যেমনটি …একটি ঝড়ো বাতাস, যাকে ইউরোক্লাইডন বলা হয়—প্রেরিতদের কাজ 27:14। এই ঝড়ো বাতাসের একটা আশ্চর্য সাহস রয়েছে যে যে কোনো সম্পর্ককে ঝট করে ঝলসে দিতে পারে। চাপযুক্ত পরিস্থিতিতে উদ্ভুত হয় সত্যিই উত্তেজিত ও সতর্ক বোধ করা—এটা মানব প্রকৃতি। আমাদের মস্তিষ্কের কেন্দ্রীয় গ্রন্থি একটি শক্তিশালী হরমোন অ্যাড্রেনালিন মুক্তি করে, আমাদের পেশী টান, মন কেন্দ্রীভূত হয়, যাতে আমরা লড়াই কিংবা পালানোর জন্য প্রস্তুত হই। এটা অবশ্যই উদ্বেগ নয়, বরং একটি স্বাভাবিক প্রতিক্রিয়া। মানুষ হিসেবে চরম আবেগ ও চাপের মাঝেও আমরা যুক্তি কষার ঐশ্বরিক ক্ষমতা রাখি। শিষ্যরা জানত না যীশু কী করবেন। তারা কেবল জানত এই পরিস্থিতি নিয়ন্ত্রণহীন। এখানেই তাদের বড় ভুল। খ্রিস্ট জানতেন কে নিয়ন্ত্রণে। পল জানতেন কে নিয়ন্ত্রণে। এমনকি যোনাহও জানতেন ক্যান ঝড় উঠল। যখন উদ্বেগ বাড়ে, তখন আমাদের বিশ্বাস ব্যর্থ হওয়ার পাথরে বাঁধা পড়ে, এবং আমরা ভাবি যে আমাদেরই নিয়ন্ত্রণ করতে হবে আমাদের চারপাশের প্রবল পরীক্ষাগুলোকে। আমাদের উঠেপড়ে একটি মহৎ কর্মসূচি ও সত্যিকার হৃদয় থাকতে পারে এবং তবু আমরা দেখতে পাই আমাদের দমবন্ধ করা বিশ্বাস শুন্য হয়ে যায়। আমরা ভুলভাবে বিস্ময় করি যে ঈশ্বর স্বর্গে বসে কিছুই করে না। আমরা আন্তরিকভাবে উপাসনার কাছে আমাদের প্রার্থনা প্রেরণ করি, কিন্তু স্বর্গ উদারভাবে নীরব। আমরা কেবল বায়াল, বুদ্ধ বা পশ্চাদপদদের কাছ থেকে এই আচরণ আশা করতাম। কিন্তু এটা সেইসব মানুষের সাথে হওয়া উচিত নয় যাদের দৃঢ় বিশ্বাস আছে—পুনর্জন্মা প্রাপ্ত, নিয়মিত উপাসনায় যাওয়া, বাইবেল পড়া, আর প্রতিদিন প্রার্থনা করা। আমাদের পুনর্বিবেচনা করা উচিত যে ঈশ্বর আমাদের পরিবেশগত শান্তি সম্পর্কে অতটা উদ্বিগ্ন নন, বরং তিনি আমাদের আভ্যন্তরীন আত্মা যেন তাঁর বিশ্রামের আশ্রয়ে নিরাপদে পৌঁছে যায় তাতে অধিকতর উদ্বিগ্ন।

যখন আমরা সুখী, আমরা আনন্দের সঙ্গে সেই বিশ্রাম দাবি করি, যদিও আমরা প্রকৃতপক্ষে তাঁর প্রতি প্রয়োজন কিছুটা অনুভব করি না। তাঁর আমাদের জীবনে হস্তক্ষেপ প্রায়ই বিকর্ষণ মনে হয়। কিন্তু যখন সময় বিবর্ণ হয়ে যায় এবং আমরা আমাদের সমস্ত সম্পদ খরচ করে ফেলেছি, আমরা তাঁকে উপরিভরীভাবে নির্ভর করি। সেই মর্মান্তিক কালে তিনি প্রায়শই আমাদের আন্তরিকতা পরীক্ষা করেন এবং কিছুই অফার করেন না…কিছুই ছাড়া চুপচাপতা। খ্রীস্ট, আমাদের নৌকায় ঘুমাচ্ছেন। ঘুমিয়ে আছেন… ঠিক তখন যখন আমরা সবচেয়ে বেশি তাঁকে প্রয়োজন। এবং তারপরেই প্রশ্ন, তোমরা কেন এত ভয়গ্রস্ত? কিভাবে তোমাদের বিশ্বাস নেই? খোলাখুলি বলতে গেলে, এই প্রশ্ন আমার কাছে কঠিন—এমনকি কঠোর—এবং সম্পূর্ণরূপে সে চরিত্রের বিরুদ্ধে যার আমি সাধারণত যীশু থেকে প্রত্যাশা করতাম। কিন্তু এই প্রশ্নের উত্তর দিতে হবে, কারণ এটি প্রয়োজন যদি আমরা তাঁর বিশ্রামের আশ্রয়ে প্রবেশ করতে চাই। বাতাস তাঁকে মানে, কিন্তু তারা আমাদের মানে না… নাকি মানে? আমরা স্পষ্টতই আবহাওয়া, আমাদের পরিবেশ, আমাদের পরিস্থিতি, বা আমাদের চারপাশের মানুষকে নিয়ন্ত্রণ করতে পারি না। তবু এই বহিঃপ্রক্রিয়াগুলোই আমাদের উদ্বেগের মূল কারণ নয়। আমাদের নিজের ত্রুটিপূর্ণ পূর্বাভাসই আমাদের আত্মাকে পিটিয়ে দেয় এবং শান্তির দ্বারে ঢুকতে বাধা দেয়। আমাদের জাহাজকে ভয়ানক উত্তেজনায় ঠেলে দেওয়া বাতাসগুলি বাহির থেকে চালিত নয় বরং অন্তর থেকে উদ্দীপ্ত। এই উদ্বেগ অবিশ্বাসের ঢেউতে চড়ে যায়, যেখানে খ্রিস্ট তাঁর ঐশ্বরিক নিদ্রায় অব্যাহত রয়েছেন, অপেক্ষা করছেন যতক্ষণ না আমরা আমাদের উদ্বেগের উৎস চিনতে পারি এবং বিশ্বাসে চিৎকার করে ওঠি। এই চারটি শক্তিশালী বাতাস সবচেয়ে সামান্য উত্তেজনাতেই জাগ্রত হয় যখন আমরা…

…আমাদের ব্যক্তিকে রক্ষা করি

যদি আমরা সুস্থ থাকি, এবং যদি আমাদের পরিবার ও আর্থিক অবস্থায় সব ঠিকঠাক থাকে, আমরা হয়তো আমাদের পরিস্থিতি ভুলভাবে ব্যাখ্যা করতে প্রবণ। সহজ পথে চলা ঈশ্বরের অনুগ্রহের লক্ষণ এবং কষ্ট তাঁর অপ্রীতির চিহ্ন হিসেবে বিশ্বাস করা একটি ভুল। সব ভালো ও পরিপূর্ণ দান ঈশ্বরের পক্ষ থেকে আসে, কিন্তু একটি পরাজয়জনক ঝড়ও সেই শ্রেণীর মধ্যে পড়তে পারে। আমাদের ব্যক্তিগত পরিবেশ সাময়িক, যেখানে আমাদের আত্মা চিরস্থায়ী। ঈশ্বর প্রায়ই আমাদের ব্যক্তিগত স্বাচ্ছন্দ্য ব্যয় করে আমাদের বিশ্বাস বাড়ান। কিন্তু যখন আমাদের ব্যক্তি মর্যাদা নামান তখন যথেষ্ট ভয় উদ্ভব হয়। আমাদের বেশিরভাগ ভীতি প্রকৃত বিপদের অভাবে উদ্ভূত।

  1. উচ্চতাভীতি রোগী ব্যক্তির উচ্চতার ভয় আছে এবং তিনি ভয় পান যে তিনি যে কোনও মঞ্চের উচ্চতা থেকে পড়ে যাবেন যদিও তা সুরক্ষিত ও ভালোভাবে পাহারা দেওয়া। অনেকে সেখানে সফলভাবে দাঁড়িয়েছে বলেও 그는 ভীষণভাবে এই ভয়ে বন্দী থাকেন, কারণ তিনি তাঁর পড়ে যাওয়ার সম্ভাবনাকে অত্যাধিক অনুমান করেছেন এবং সত্যে বিশ্বাস করতে অস্বীকার করেন।
  2. পশুপ্রীতি-ভীতি লোক পশুর ভয়ে জীবিত, তিনি মনের মধ্যে এমন চিত্র সৃষ্টি করেন যে তিনি চামড়া ছিঁড়ে মেরে মারা হবে বা তাঁর পেট থেকে অভ্যন্তরীণ অঙ্গ বের করে ফেলা হবে।
  3. ক্লস্ট্রোফোবিক ছোট, শক্ত জায়গা ভয় পান, যেখানে আগোরাফোবিক খোলা জায়গা ভয় পায়।
  4. আরাচিবুটিরোফোবিয়া হলো মাড়ির ছাদে মাখন আটকে যাওয়ার ভয়—পিনাট বাটার ঠেকে যাওয়া ভয়।

তাদের ভয়ের সম্মুখীন হতে গিয়ে, ফোবিক ব্যক্তির হৃদস্পন্দন দ্রুত ত্বরান্বিত হতে পারে, শ্বাসকষ্ট, মুখ শুকিয়ে যাওয়া, ঘাম, মিনিটিক বা হালকা মাথাব্যাথা অনুভব করতে পারেন। সুতরাং, তাদের ভয় তাদের কাছে বাস্তব হয়ে উঠবে। অধিকাংশ মানুষ তাদের ব্যক্তিগত ত্রুটিকে ক্ষমা করে দিলেও, সত্য হলো এই উদ্বেগটি ভিত্তিহীন। যখন আমরা আমাদের ব্যক্তির রক্ষণাবেক্ষণের জন্য ক্ষমা ও মুসাদ করি, তখন ভয় অনিবার্য। শিষ্যরা ভয় পেয়েছিল যে তারা বিনষ্ট হয়ে যাবে, এবং খ্রিস্ট তাদের জিজ্ঞেস করলেন কেন। কি ভাল নয় …চলিয়া যাওয়া, আর খ্রীষ্টের সাথে থাকা; যা বহুত উত্তম—ফিলিপীয় 1:23. যদি আমরা আমাদের জীবন খ্রীষ্টের উপর বিশ্বাস করতে পারি, তবে আমাদের মৃত্যুতে কি আমরা তাঁকে বিশ্বাস করতে পারব না?

যে কেউ তার জীবন রক্ষা করতে চায় সে তা হারাবে; কিন্তু যে কেউ আমার এবং সুসমাচারের জন্য তার জীবন হারায়, সে তাহাই রক্ষা করিবে—মার্ক 8:35।

…আমাদের সম্পদ রক্ষা করা

বহিরঙ্গভাবে, খ্রিস্টের জীবন ছিল সবচেয়ে অশান্ত জীবনগুলোর মধ্যে একটি। শিয়ালের আস্তানাও আছে এবং পাখিদের বাসা আছে, আর তিনি তাঁর বালিশ পেছনের অংশে একটি দুলতে থাকা নৌকায় রাখতেন যা অনবরত ঢেউ ভেঙে গিয়ে কাঁপছিল। কিন্তু তাঁর অভ্যন্তরীন আশ্রয় কাচের সমুদ্রের মতো শান্ত ছিল। এর কিছু অংশ কারণ ছিল যে তাঁর রক্ষার জন্য কোনো সম্পদ ছিল না। এমনকি নৌকাটিও ধার নেয়া ছিল। “অধিক মুদ্রা, অধিক চিন্তা” বলে প্রাচীন প্রবাদ, এবং ধন কমলে উদ্বেগ বেড়ে যায়। এবং একজন জনের মধ্যে কেহ তাঁকে বলিল, আরস্য, আমার ভাইকে বল যে আমার সাথে ঐ উত্তরাধিকার ভাগ করুক—লূক 12:13। যীশু তার পাশ নেননি। পরিবর্তে তিনি ঈর্ষাপরায়ণ হৃদয়কে উপদেশ দিলেন যা উদ্বেগ সৃষ্টি করছিল। যদি খ্রিস্ট আমাদেরকে ধন প্রদান করেন, তবে আমাদের অপরাধবোধ হওয়ার দরকার নেই। যদি তিনি তা নেন, আমাদের উদ্বেগের দরকার নেই। ঝড়ের মাঝেও আমরা উপদেশ পাই …উত্তেজিত হইও না: কারণ তোমাদের মধ্যে কেহে প্রাণহানী হইবে না, কিন্তু জাহাজের হানি হইবে—প্রেরিতদের কাজ 27:22। এটি ক্লান্ত নাবিকদের প্রতি আরোগ্য বালি রূপে উৎসর্গ করা হল, কিন্তু যে তাদের সম্পদ রক্ষায় প্রবণ তাদের জন্য এটি একটি কৌতুককর কাহিনী। যখন ধনী যুবরাজকে তাঁর ভৌত সংগ্রহ ত্যাগ করে উদ্ধার প্রস্তাব করা হল, …সে দুঃখে কেঁদে গেল: কারণ তাঁর অনেক সম্পদ ছিল—মাথিউ 19:22। আমাদের মধ্য যারা আমাদের ধনের ক্ষয়ে উদ্বিগ্ন হন তাঁরা কম নয় বোকা।

…আমাদের পরিকল্পনা পরিপূর্ণ করা

আমরা একটি পথ নির্ধারণ করি। হতে পারে আমরা চাকরি পরিবর্তন করি, কোনো সম্পর্ক শুরু করি, বা কোনও নতুন মন্ত্রণালয়ে প্রবেশ করি। আমরা বিশ্বাস নিয়ে যাত্রা শুরু করেছি এবং অচিরেই আমরা সংগ্রাম শুরু করি। দৈনন্দিন জীবনের বাতাস ও ঢেউ যেন আমাদের বিরুদ্ধে কাজ করে। আমাদের প্রত্যাশা পূরণ হচ্ছে না এবং মনে হয় খ্রিস্ট তাঁর অংশ করছেন না। এটা খ্রীষ্ট নয়, বরং আমাদের প্রত্যাশাই আমাদের উদ্বেগের কারণ। আমরা আমাদের বিনিয়োগ থেকে অনেক আশা করি এবং আমাদের চেষ্টা বিফল হলে হতাশাজনক হয়। মারথার কোলিপ করা রুটি-পাকশালায় সাহায্যের অভাবে তাঁর স্পন্দন দ্রুত হয়। তাঁর কষ্ট বেড়ে যায় যখন তাঁর সুচারু পরিকল্পিত খাবার অসম্পূর্ণ থাকে। তাঁর অভিযোগ শিষ্যদের চিৎকারের কম নয় যখন তারা সমুদ্রে চেপে থাকে। …প্রভু, তুমি কি দেখছ না যে আমার বোন আমাকে একা সেবায় রেখে গেল? বলে তাকে বল যে সে আমাকে সহায় করুক—লূক 10:40। তাঁর উদ্বেগ মেরির অনীহা বা খ্রীষ্টের উদাসীনতার কারণে হয়নি। তাঁর বোন বিশ্রামের আশ্রয়ে ডক করেছে যখন মারথা হৃদয়ের উত্থিত আবেগের বিরুদ্ধে লড়াই করছিল। তাই পারফেকশানিস্ট তাঁর অসম্পূর্ণ দৃষ্টিভঙ্গি যখন প্রত্যাশার তুলনায় ছিন্ন হয় তখন নিজেই ঝড় সৃষ্টি করে। কিন্তু খ্রীষ্ট জলের ভর্তি নৌকার চেয়ে বিশ্বাসে ভর করা বুকে অধিক উদ্বিগ্ন।

…সকলকে সন্তুষ্ট করা

শাস্ত্র আমাদের ভালভাবে শেখিয়েছে আমাদের প্রতিবেশীকে নিজের মতো করে ভালোবাসতে, কিন্তু তা নির্দেশ করে না যে আমাদের তাদের অনুমোদনের জন্য লড়াই করা উচিত। পছন্দ করা হওয়া আনন্দদায়ক। প্রত্যাখ্যাত হওয়া বেদনাদায়ক। ফলে অনেক আত্মা জাগরণঘন্টা অন্যান্যদের অনুমোদন পাওয়ার সন্ধানেই কাটায়। তাদেরকে তাদের সহপাঠী সব রকমের পোশাক পরতে, যেমন আচরণ করতে, যেমন কথা বলতে, এবং যেমন জীবন যাপন করতে হবে। এরা উদ্বেগের ঢেউয়ে ভরা জীবন যাপন করে। প্রতিটি নতুন পরিচিতির সাথে “কি হইলে” ধরণের প্রশ্নের ঝড় ওঠে। কোনো সম্পর্কই জাহাজের চেয়েও নাজুক নয়। আমরা যত বড় ত্যাগ করব ভালোবাসা পেতে, শেষে আমরা এমন এক অসন্তোষজনক ঝড়ের মুখোমুখি হব যা আমাদের হতাশার গভীরে টেনে নেবে। যখন আমাদের সেরা প্রচেষ্টা আমাদের বঞ্চিত করে এবং আমাদের সেরা বন্ধুরাই আমাদের পথভ্রষ্ট করে, তখন আমাদের আহত নৌকাকে বিশ্রামের আশ্র্যে আনতে হবে। অস্বস্তিকর, দুর্ভাগ্যজনক, অপ্রিয় এবং বিরক্তিকর সম্পর্ক সবসময় বিদ্যমান থাকবে। আমাদের অনেক ভালো হবে যদি আমরা অন্যদের খারাপ আচরণের জন্য অজুহাত দেব নিজের জন্য নয়। যখন আমরা আমাদের নিজের মনেই উদ্ভূত বাতাসকে তিরস্কার করতে পারি, তখন আমরা তত্ক্ষণই কাঙ্খিত আশ্রয়ে পৌঁছাব।

অতএব, ঈশ্বরের লোকদের জন্য একটি বিশ্রাম রয়ে যায়। কারণ যে ব্যক্তি তাঁর বিশ্রামে প্রবেশ করেছিল, সে নিজের কাজ থেকেও বিশ্রাম লাভ করেছে, যেমন ঈশ্বরও তাঁর কাজ থেকে বিশ্রাম লাভ করেছিলেন। অতএব আমরা পরিশ্রম করিতে থাকি, যেন আমরা সেই বিশ্রামে প্রবেশ করি…—হেব্রুই 4:9-11।

Humanity is defined by its search for truth. Some people search for this truth through personal power, as they attempt to hold sway over their fellow man. Some search for truth in pleasure, seeing self-gratification as the greatest achievement in life. Others seek enlightenment through their own thoughts and reasonings, ever learning, and never able to come to the knowledge of the truth –2 Timothy 3:7. Yet others believe a life of service will be a reward unto itself, so they try to make a name for themselves through the publicity of their acts of service and charity.

Time and time again, throughout history, the collective thought of man has turned to something greater than themselves. Religions rise, and religions fall, empires are founded and crumble, philosophies develop and fall apart.

Against this background of intellectual undulation, a movement which most of my readers will recognize, took root in a small, mountainous region of the globe. Zurich, Switzerland, in the year 1525 AD, was to be its given birthplace and birthdate, but its roots had been established a full 1500 years earlier, in Galilee, where One taught and lived the final answers to all of man’s questions.

The beginnings of this more recent movement are well documented. In short, it was founded by a small group of assorted students, clergy, and commoners who sought after truth in its purest form. The stories of Conrad Grebel, Felix Manz, and George Blaurock are well known to many of us. They endeavored to separate from the spiritual corruption that surrounded them, as they established the beginnings of what would become known as the Anabaptist movement.

These three soon faced the scrutiny of the civil and spiritual authorities of their time, enduring hardship and suffering for their faith. Two of them eventually gave their lives for the truth they so esteemed. Felix Manz was the first Anabaptist to be martyred. On January 5th, 1527, not two years after his courageous re-baptism, he was drowned in the River Limmat which flowed through Zurich. His last words were: “Into thy hands, O God, I commend my spirit.”

The Anabaptist movement lived beyond these three men.

It spread and grew throughout Moravia, the Netherlands, Switzerland, and the Palatinate region of Germany. Almost one hundred years later there was another prominent leader in the Zurich hills; this one was an elderly farmer. He was well-seasoned in leading his flock through the ebb and flow of the challenges facing the believers of that time. His name is Hans Landis.

The year was 1613, January 26 to be exact. Converging on the small castle, Wadenswil, on the shore of Lake Zurich, was an elderly Hans Landis, along with fourteen of his church members. Most notably among these was Galli Fuchs, a schoolteacher and recent convert, as well as Bachman, a smith and well-known troublemaker, who had also been recently converted. There to meet with them were nine church and state officials, including the mayor of Zurich, Rudolf Rhan; his chief of police, Conrad Grebel (apparently a namesake of the original re-baptizer of nearly a century prior); and numerous local ministers from Zurich’s Protestant church. The reason for this meeting was that Hans’ spiritual work had been blessed, and his small congregation was rapidly growing, causing ripples in the attendance of rural parishes belonging to the Protestant church. Dropping attendance presented several difficulties to this combined church and state government.

First, the Protestant Church drew vast funds from its parishioners. Thus, another church drawing away and converting its members was seen not only as a spiritual threat, but also a financial one. The cantons of the area were often engaged in religion-fueled hostilities, ranging from angry debates to full-blown military campaigns. Second, deviant spiritual doctrines that disagreed with the government’s official religions were often introduced in times of civil unrest, and the peasant uprisings of nearby cantons were still fresh in the minds of local nobility and clergy. Events such as the Muensterites and their violent interpretations of Scripture remained a clear warning of religious zeal gone awry. These uprisings had taken place as the Catholic church collapsed in the area, which presented opportunities for new and sometimes extreme beliefs to take root. Now, the activities of Hans and his church seemed to these officials a matter bordering on rebellion and treachery.

This meeting was not the first encounter Hans Landis and his flock had had with the local authorities. An earlier investigation had been conducted, nearly four years prior. This report gave their meeting places as the forests, barns, and even Hans Landis’ home. However, no list of members was included, as even the Protestant neighbors of the church refused to name any of the Anabaptists. Not only did the local populace refuse to cooperate in naming any of those in Hans’ congregation, but it was also rumored that the Taufer held a general fund, in charge of Deacon Jacob Isler, from which they provided for needs within their community. To the officials, this appeared to be nothing more than another trick to persuade the poor of the community to forsake their church and join Hans and his group.

Mayor Rhan opened the meeting, addressing those of his company as “Reverend, high and well-learned, pious, noble, intelligent, wise, (and) dear lords.” Next, he spoke to Hans and the brethren with him, giving them a cordial greeting of “Honorable, dear and good friends” before reminding them of their positions by referring to them as “subjects”. Following these none-too-subtle maneuverings, he questioned them, asking for an explanation on “the reasons [why] you separated from our church and … started a separate sect.” Following this question, he assured them that the council wished to be tolerant but that the separatists should “not misuse the patience and graciousness of the lords.”

Meeting this introduction, Hans asked permission for him and his brethren to rise and address their “Gracious Lords”. Given it, he rose, thanking the mayor for his kind words of greeting before questioning their interest in the Anabaptists’ beliefs, as he maintained they had oft heard them before. He adjoined this by stating that all their doctrine was “nothing else than what Christ taught and what the apostles wrote.” As before, the Anabaptists asked simply to be allowed to hold onto this, supporting their government in matters not relating to conscience. They would also continue to pray for the government and their leaders.

Mayor Rhan did not take kindly to this answer, taking it as being implied that he and the Protestant church did not obey the commands of Christ. Hans, upon hearing this rebuttal, asked leave to take his group outside of the room for a short while. Upon returning, Galli Fuchs was presented and gave a testimony to the lords, outlining his spiritual journey through both the Protestant and Catholic churches, observing that while both preached well across the pulpit, both also denied this teaching by their godless living. Upon studying the Anabaptist faith and application, Galli was converted.

The officials were skeptical, arguing that Galli’s points had “still shown no reason for your separation.” Upon this rejoinder, another convert was brought forward, this one was the blacksmith Bachman. Bachman was immediately recognized by Conrad Grebel (not the Anabaptist founder), the Zurich chief of police, as having been known as one of the local rowdies—“It’s true, you were godless [and] there is no one in the entire area with whom I had more trouble than you.”

Bachman’s testimony echoed many of Galli’s points, especially on the purity and separateness of the true church, ending with this quote from Sirach: “Whoever stirs in pitch will be smudged.”

The debates continued, with contention flaring around communion, the examples of church leaders, and knowledge of salvation. As the meeting ended, Galli Fuchs could not resist a final remark: “If you would give us the church at Hirzel, … you would see … who would have the larger crowd!” This brought a round of laughter from the room, and Hans seized a final opportunity to speak, pleading: “Oh, dear sirs, let us remain by what we believe.”

Following this plea, the mayor deliberated, finally deciding that the brothers were to be given leave to go without arrest, who, upon exiting, were heard to speak in agreement: “We would also give life, body, property, and blood.” They were soon to have the opportunity to live this commitment.

Fifteen months passed. Hans was locked up in the Wellenberg tower in Zurich, along with Galli Fuchs, Deacon Jacob Isler, Hans Meili, Stephen Zehnder, and Paul Degia (a native of Milan, Italy). There they were held for fourteen weeks, and repeatedly cajoled, interrogated, and threatened. An order was finally handed down that they should leave the canton of Zurich, but Hans refused, to which the council responded with a threat often considered worse than death. The council maintained that because of these men’s civil disobedience, not their beliefs, they were to be sentenced as galley slaves to row aboard the ships of France in the Mediterranean.

Jacob Isler pleaded with the lords, asking them how they could do such a thing, knowing that the Taufer (Anabaptists) could not bear to leave their families. Stephen Zhender added: “We would not fear to go over sea and water since they [are] also the creation of God.” Despite these entreaties, the council made good on its threats, sentencing all six to the galleys.

The sentencing sent shock rippling through the community. The life expectancy for a young, healthy galley slave was no more than three years, and those three years would be filled with starvation, exposure, beatings, and exhaustion. Even in the harsher Catholic cantons, this sentence was severe. In the more lenient Protestant community, it brought public outrage.

The prisoners were all given one last chance to leave the canton, whereupon three of them relented. But Galli Fuchs, Stephen Zehnder, and Hans Landis steadfastly refused to change their mind. They were subsequently led under guard westward to a French ambassador in Solothurn, a town in the canton of Bern. Bern reacted in much the same way as Zurich had, with a ransom being offered for the prisoners’ release. When that failed, a file was secretly slipped into their cell in Solothurn. The prisoners’ chains were swiftly cut through, and they escaped the city, fleeing back to their homes. Once there, the populace, still outraged by their treatment, refused to report them to the authorities.

News of the escape spread and grew, and Hans was soon at work, baptizing the new converts, and even overseeing several marriages. The Anabaptists prospered, helping the poor of the community through food and no-interest loans from their alms fund. This renewed activity angered and frightened the authorities, who finally decided that the efforts of its elderly leader would need to be neutralized.

Hans was promptly arrested upon this decision and once again locked up in the Wellenberg. Here the threats and admonishments from the authorities were scaled up. If he would not recant or at least leave the canton, they would need to kill him.

Threats such as these did not sway Hans. He, instead, admonished the rulers not to commit sin in their treatment of him, affirming his resolve that he had “given himself to God” and “was ready to await what God would let come upon him.”

This brave stand by Hans brought a similar realization to the authorities: they would need to make good on their threats. Regarding Hans as a rebel, they maintained that he “wanted to be his own lord and master regardless of the honorable authorities,” and that he displayed the “stubborn, seditious resistance of wicked people.” Despite these allegations in conjunction with their threats, the magistrates realized that an execution would be an unpopular undertaking. Hans was well respected by the local populace, and even had connections in Amsterdam, where his daughter lived, being married to a Dutch Mennonite.

Officer Grebel, the Protestant clergy, and various others spent much time in discussion with Hans in his prison cell, but to no avail. By Thursday, September 29, 1614, they realized that he was completely immovable in his faith, unwilling either to recant or to leave the canton. This report, presented to the lords, sent them into deep deliberation. Some argued for publicly cutting off Hans’ ear and exiling him, while others deemed life imprisonment a more appropriate sentence. The matter was put to a vote at noon, and a majority decision was quickly reached. Hans Landis would be publicly beheaded at once.

Hans, upon hearing the decision, thought it only another ploy to persuade him to recant. However, upon approaching the well-known public execution site in Zurich, his face turned ashen, and his hands flew to his head. However, he swiftly composed himself, smiling and admonishing the crowd not to weep, as he trusted in his good hope. Noticing his wife and children present, he asked them to leave so that his resolve would not be weakened.

The sentence was read; Hans stood silent. Not a word of criticism had been raised against his personal morals. Instead, the issue was his refusal to disband his church. He remained steadfast, and so the executioner, Paul Vollmar, led Hans to the execution site. Some observers claimed that Vollmar let go of Hans, seemingly giving him a way of escape. When Hans did not, Vollmar raised his hands to God, asking forgiveness for what the law required him to perform. Hans, smiling, forgave the man, while various church ministers admonished him to recant, but Hans answered that he had seen no repentance in them.

Vollmar, having reached the site of the execution, gave Hans an opportunity to speak unimpeded, and Hans spoke but briefly: “I do not know what more I should say than that I wish everyone would come to a knowledge of their sins and repent, that they might be saved; this I would wish for everyone.”

Then, within sight of the place where Feliz Manz had given his life nearly a century prior, he knelt and bowed his head. The sword flashed downward, then Paul Vollmar asked the ritual question: “Have I executed this man rightly?”

“Yes,” came the reply, “you have executed this poor man.”

The immediate impact of the elderly Hans’ sacrifice was a ripple of support and outrage throughout the non-Anabaptist community. Rhudlof Rhan and Conrad Grebel continued to pressure the remaining Anabaptists, committing Margaretha Landis, Hans’s widow, to solitary confinement in the city hospital after her refusal to comply with their demands. Hans’s children would likewise remain strong, refusing to recant, but several of his grandchildren began attending the city church shortly after their grandfather’s execution.

The local Anabaptist congregation remained strong as well. Its spiritual descendants would carry the word of Christ with them when, a century later, a great emigration landed them on the wild shores of the New World. Here, in the religious freedom of Pennsylvania, they would establish new communities where the faith that had cost Hans Landis his life was to flourish through future generations. Today, there are believers throughout America who are endeavoring to live out their faith according to their conscience, who are where they are as a result of the life lived by Hans some 400 years ago. Some are his descendants, and some are friends of his descendants. May we be inspired to walk as Jesus walked, just like Hans.

Die Menschheit wird durch ihre Suche nach Wahrheit definiert. Manche Menschen suchen diese Wahrheit durch persönliche Macht, indem sie versuchen, über ihre Mitmenschen zu herrschen. Manche suchen die Wahrheit im Vergnügen und sehen Selbstbefriedigung als die größte Errungenschaft im Leben an. Andere streben nach Erleuchtung durch ihr eigenes Denken und ihre Überlegungen, immer lernend und niemals zur Erkenntnis der Wahrheit gelangend – 2. Timotheus 3:7. Wieder andere glauben, ein Leben im Dienst sei Lohn genug, und versuchen daher, sich durch die Öffentlichkeit ihrer Werke des Dienstes und der Nächstenliebe einen Namen zu machen.

Immer wieder hat sich im Lauf der Geschichte das kollektive Denken der Menschen etwas Größerem zugewandt als sich selbst. Religionen entstehen und vergehen, Reiche werden gegründet und zerfallen, Philosophien entwickeln sich und zerbrechen.

Vor diesem Hintergrund intellektueller Schwankungen nahm eine Bewegung Wurzeln, die den meisten meiner Leser bekannt sein dürfte, und zwar in einer kleinen, gebirgigen Region der Erde. Zürich, Schweiz, im Jahre 1525 n. Chr. sollte als Geburtsort und Geburtsjahr gelten, doch ihre Wurzeln waren bereits volle 1500 Jahre früher in Galiläa gelegt worden, wo Einer lehrte und lebte, was die endgültigen Antworten auf alle Fragen des Menschen sein sollten.

Die Anfänge dieser jüngeren Bewegung sind gut dokumentiert. Kurz gesagt wurde sie von einer kleinen Gruppe verschiedener Schüler, Geistlicher und Laien gegründet, die nach Wahrheit in ihrer reinsten Form suchten. Die Geschichten von Conrad Grebel, Felix Manz und George Blaurock sind vielen von uns wohlbekannt. Sie bemühten sich, sich von der geistlichen Korruption, die sie umgab, zu trennen und legten damit den Grundstein für das, was als Täuferbewegung bekannt werden sollte.

Diese drei standen bald unter der Beobachtung der weltlichen und geistlichen Autoritäten ihrer Zeit und erduldeten Leid und Verfolgung um ihres Glaubens willen. Zwei von ihnen gaben schließlich ihr Leben für die Wahrheit, die sie so hochschätzten. Felix Manz war der erste Täufer, der gemartert wurde. Am 5. Januar 1527, nicht einmal zwei Jahre nach seiner mutigen Wiederestaufe, wurde er in der Limmat, die durch Zürich floss, ertränkt. Seine letzten Worte waren: „In deine Hände, o Gott, befehle ich meinen Geist.“

Die täuferische Bewegung überdauerte diese drei Männer.

Sie verbreitete sich und wuchs in Mähren, den Niederlanden, der Schweiz und der Pfalz in Deutschland. Fast hundert Jahre später gab es einen weiteren prominenten Führer in den Zürcher Hügeln; dieser war ein älterer Bauer. Er war erfahren darin, seine Herde durch die Ebbe und Flut der Herausforderungen jener Zeit zu leiten. Sein Name ist Hans Landis.

Das Jahr war 1613, genauer der 26. Januar. Auf dem kleinen Schloss Wädenswil am Ufer des Zürichsees versammelten sich der alte Hans Landis mit vierzehn Mitgliedern seiner Gemeinde. Besonders nennenswert waren darunter Galli Fuchs, ein Schulmeister und kürzlich Konvertierter, sowie Bachman, ein Schmied und bekannter Unruhestifter, der ebenfalls erst kürzlich zum Glauben gekommen war. Ihnen gegenüber saßen neun Kirchen- und Staatsbeamte, darunter der Bürgermeister von Zürich, Rudolf Rhan; sein Polizeichef, Conrad Grebel (anscheinend Namensvetter des ursprünglichen Wiederestaufers knapp ein Jahrhundert zuvor); und zahlreiche lokale Pfarrer der Zürcher protestantischen Kirche. Der Grund für dieses Treffen war, dass Hans’ geistliche Arbeit gesegnet worden war und seine kleine Gemeinde schnell wuchs, was Auswirkungen auf die Besucherzahlen der ländlichen Pfarreien der Protestantischen Kirche hatte. Rückläufige Besuche stellten für diese verbundene Kirchen- und Staatsherrschaft mehrere Probleme dar.

Erstens zog die protestantische Kirche erhebliche Gelder von ihren Gemeindegliedern ein. Daher wurde eine andere Kirche, die Mitglieder abwirbt und bekehrt, nicht nur als geistliche, sondern auch als finanzielle Bedrohung gesehen. Die Kantone der Gegend waren oft in religionsbegründete Feindschaften verwickelt, die von hitzigen Debatten bis zu offenen militärischen Unternehmungen reichten. Zweitens wurden abweichende geistliche Lehren, die mit den offiziellen Religionen der Regierung nicht übereinstimmten, häufig in Zeiten zivilen Aufruhrs eingeführt, und die Bauernaufstände benachbarter Kantone waren den lokalen Adligen und Geistlichen noch gegenwärtig. Ereignisse wie die Münsterischen und ihre gewalttätigen Auslegungen der Schrift blieben eine deutliche Warnung vor religiösem Eifer, der aus dem Ruder läuft. Diese Aufstände hatten stattgefunden, als die katholische Kirche in der Gegend zusammenbrach, was neuen und manchmal extremen Überzeugungen Gelegenheit zum Wachsen gab. Nun erschienen die Aktivitäten von Hans und seiner Gemeinde den Beamten als eine Angelegenheit, die an Rebellion und Verrat grenzte.

Dieses Treffen war nicht die erste Begegnung, die Hans Landis und seine Gemeinde mit den örtlichen Behörden gehabt hatten. Fast vier Jahre zuvor war bereits eine Untersuchung durchgeführt worden. In diesem Bericht wurden ihre Zusammenkünfte in Wäldern, Scheunen und sogar in Hans Landis’ Haus genannt. Allerdings war keine Mitgliederliste beigefügt, da selbst die protestantischen Nachbarn der Gemeinde sich weigerten, irgendwelche Täufer zu benennen. Die lokale Bevölkerung weigerte sich nicht nur, Namen aus Hans’ Gemeinde preiszugeben, es wurde auch gemunkelt, dass die Taufer einen gemeinsamen Fonds unter der Verwaltung des Diakons Jacob Isler führten, aus dem sie für Bedürfnisse innerhalb ihrer Gemeinschaft sorgten. Für die Beamten schien dies nichts anderes als ein weiterer Trick, um die Armen der Gemeinde dazu zu bringen, ihre Kirche zu verlassen und sich Hans und seiner Gruppe anzuschließen.

Bürgermeister Rhan eröffnete die Versammlung und sprach die Anwesenden als „Verehrte, hohe und wohlgelehrte, fromme, edle, verständige, weise, (und) liebe Herren“ an. Dann wandte er sich an Hans und die Brüder bei ihm und grüßte sie freundlich mit „Ehrliche, liebe und gute Freunde“, bevor er sie mit dem Hinweis auf ihre Stellung als „Untertanen“ an ihre Positionen erinnerte. Nach diesen wenig subtilen Manövern befragte er sie und forderte eine Erklärung für „die Gründe [warum] ihr euch von unserer Kirche getrennt und … eine eigene Sekte gegründet habt.“ Im Anschluss versicherte er ihnen, der Rat wolle tolerant sein, doch die Separatisten sollten „die Geduld und Gnade der Herren nicht mißbrauchen.“

Auf diese Einführung hin bat Hans um Erlaubnis, er und seine Brüder möchten aufstehen und vor ihren „Gnädigen Herren“ sprechen. Diese wurde ihnen gewährt, und er erhob sich, dankte dem Bürgermeister für seine freundlichen Begrüßungsworte und fragte dann nach ihrem Interesse an den Überzeugungen der Täufer, wobei er meinte, sie hätten diese Lehren schon oft gehört. Er fügte hinzu, dass all ihre Lehre „nichts anderes sei als das, was Christus gelehrt und was die Apostel geschrieben hätten.“ Wie zuvor baten die Täufer schlicht darum, dies behalten zu dürfen, die Regierung in Fragen, die nicht das Gewissen betrafen, zu unterstützen. Sie würden auch weiterhin für Regierung und Obrigkeit beten.

Bürgermeister Rhan nahm diese Antwort nicht gut auf und wertete sie als Unterstellung, er und die protestantische Kirche gehorchten nicht den Geboten Christi. Hans bat daraufhin um Erlaubnis, seine Gruppe kurz aus dem Raum zu führen. Nach ihrer Rückkehr wurde Galli Fuchs vorgestellt, der den Herren ein Zeugnis gab und seinen geistlichen Weg durch die protestantische und die katholische Kirche schilderte, wobei er feststellte, dass beide zwar gut von der Kanzel predigten, aber durch ihr gottloses Leben diese Lehre leugneten. Beim Studium des täuferischen Glaubens und seiner praktischen Anwendung bekehrte sich Galli.

Die Beamten blieben skeptisch und argumentierten, Gallis Ausführungen hätten „immer noch keinen Grund für eure Trennung gezeigt.” Als Antwort darauf wurde ein weiterer Bekehrter vorgeführt, diesmal der Schmied Bachman. Bachman wurde sofort von Conrad Grebel (nicht der täuferische Gründer), dem Zürcher Polizeichef, als einer der örtlichen Raufbolde erkannt – „Es ist wahr, du warst gottlos [und] es gibt niemanden in der ganzen Gegend, mit dem ich mehr Ärger hatte als mit dir.”

Bachmans Zeugnis spiegelte viele von Gallis Punkten wider, besonders hinsichtlich der Reinheit und Trennung der wahren Kirche, und endete mit diesem Zitat aus Sirach: „Wer sich in Pech rührt, wird beschmiert werden.”

Die Debatten dauerten an, die Auseinandersetzungen drehten sich um Abendmahl, das Vorbild der Kirchenführer und die Erkenntnis des Heils. Als die Versammlung endete, konnte Galli Fuchs einen letzten Kommentar nicht unterlassen: „Wenn ihr uns die Kirche in Hirzel geben würdet, … würdet ihr sehen … wer die größere Menge hätte!” Das löste Gelächter im Raum aus, und Hans ergriff die letzte Chance zu sprechen und flehte: „O, liebe Herren, laßt uns bei dem bleiben, was wir glauben.”

Auf diese Bitte hin beriet der Bürgermeister und entschied schließlich, den Brüdern die Erlaubnis zu geben, ohne Verhaftung zu gehen; beim Verlassen des Saales waren sie zu hören, wie sie übereinstimmend sprachen: „Wir würden auch Leben, Leib, Gut und Blut geben.” Bald sollten sie Gelegenheit haben, dieses Versprechen zu leben.

Fünfzehn Monate vergingen. Hans wurde zusammen mit Galli Fuchs, Diakon Jacob Isler, Hans Meili, Stephen Zehnder und Paul Degia (ein gebürtiger Mailänder, Italien) im Wellenberg-Turm in Zürich eingekerkert. Dort wurden sie vierzehn Wochen lang festgehalten, wiederholt beschwatzt, verhört und bedroht. Schließlich wurde ihnen befohlen, den Kanton Zürich zu verlassen, doch Hans verweigerte dies, worauf der Rat mit einer Drohung reagierte, die oft schlimmer als der Tod selbst angesehen wurde. Der Rat erklärte, dass diese Männer wegen ihrer zivilen Ungehorsamkeit, nicht wegen ihres Glaubens, dazu verurteilt würden, als Galeerensklaven an Bord französischer Schiffe im Mittelmeer zu rudern.

Jacob Isler flehte die Herren an und fragte, wie sie so etwas tun könnten, da die Taufer nicht ertragen könnten, ihre Familien zu verlassen. Stephen Zehnder fügte hinzu: „Wir würden uns nicht fürchten, über Meer und Wasser zu gehen, da auch sie Gottes Schöpfung sind.” Trotz dieser Bitten machten die Herren ihre Drohung wahr und verurteilten alle sechs zu den Galeeren.

Das Urteil löste in der Gemeinschaft Erschütterung aus. Die Lebenserwartung eines jungen, gesunden Galeerensklaven betrug nicht mehr als drei Jahre, und diese Jahre wären gefüllt mit Hunger, Entbehrung, Prügeln und Erschöpfung. Selbst in den härteren katholischen Kantonen galt dieses Urteil als hart. In der milderen protestantischen Gemeinschaft führte es zu öffentlichem Aufschrei.

Den Gefangenen wurde noch einmal die Chance gegeben, den Kanton zu verlassen; drei von ihnen gaben daraufhin nach. Doch Galli Fuchs, Stephen Zehnder und Hans Landis weigerten sich standhaft, ihre Meinung zu ändern. Sie wurden unter Bewachung westwärts zu einem französischen Gesandten in Solothurn, einer Stadt im Kanton Bern, gebracht. Bern reagierte ähnlich wie Zürich und bot ein Lösegeld für die Freilassung der Gefangenen an. Als das scheiterte, wurde heimlich eine Feile in ihre Zelle in Solothurn geschmuggelt. Die Ketten der Gefangenen wurden schnell durchgesägt, und sie flohen aus der Stadt zurück in ihre Heimatorte. Dort weigerte sich die Bevölkerung, immer noch entrüstet über ihre Behandlung, sie den Behörden zu melden.

Die Nachricht von der Flucht verbreitete sich und wuchs, und Hans war bald wieder tätig, taufte die neuen Bekehrten und vollzog sogar mehrere Eheschließungen. Die Täufer gediehen und halfen den Armen der Gemeinde durch Lebensmittel und zinsfreie Darlehen aus ihrer Armenkasse. Diese erneute Aktivität verärgerte und beunruhigte die Behörden, die schließlich entschieden, die Einwirkung ihres alten Führers müsse gebrochen werden.

Hans wurde nach dieser Entscheidung umgehend verhaftet und erneut im Wellenberg eingesperrt. Hier wurden die Drohungen und Ermahnungen der Behörden verschärft. Wenn er nicht widerrufe oder zumindest den Kanton verlasse, so würden sie ihn töten müssen.

Solche Drohungen ließen Hans unbeeindruckt. Stattdessen ermahnte er die Obrigkeit, kein Unrecht an ihm zu verüben, und bekräftigte seine Entschlossenheit, sich „Gott hingegeben“ zu haben und „bereit zu sein, abzuwarten, was Gott über ihn kommen lassen würde.”

Dieser mutige Stand brachte bei den Behörden die Erkenntnis, dass sie ihre Drohungen wahrmachen müssten. Sie betrachteten Hans als Aufrührer und behaupteten, er „wolle sein eigener Herr und Meister sein, ungeachtet der ehrbaren Obrigkeiten,“ und zeige den „sturköpfigen, aufrührerischen Widerstand böser Leute.” Trotz dieser Anschuldigungen und Drohungen erkannten die Richter, dass eine Hinrichtung unpopulär wäre. Hans war bei der lokalen Bevölkerung hoch angesehen und hatte sogar Verbindungen nach Amsterdam, wo seine Tochter lebte und mit einem niederländischen Mennoniten verheiratet war.

Officer Grebel, die protestantischen Geistlichen und mehrere andere suchten Hans in seiner Zelle immer wieder zum Gespräch auf, jedoch ohne Erfolg. Am Donnerstag, dem 29. September 1614, erkannten sie, dass er in seinem Glauben völlig unbeweglich war, weder bereit zu widerrufen noch den Kanton zu verlassen. Dieser Bericht, den sie den Herren vorlegten, führte zu einer intensiven Beratung. Einige plädierten dafür, Hans öffentlich ein Ohr abzuschneiden und zu verbannen, während andere Lebenslanges Zuchthaus für angemessener hielten. Die Angelegenheit wurde am Mittag zur Abstimmung gebracht, und schnell fiel eine Mehrheitsentscheidung. Hans Landis sollte sofort öffentlich geköpft werden.

Als Hans die Entscheidung hörte, hielt er sie zunächst für einen weiteren Versuch, ihn zum Widerruf zu bewegen. Doch als er sich dem bekannten Hinrichtungsplatz in Zürich näherte, wurde sein Gesicht bleich, und die Hände fuhren ihm an den Kopf. Schnell jedoch beherrschte er sich, lächelte und ermahnte die Menge, nicht zu weinen, da er auf seine gute Hoffnung vertraute. Als er seine Frau und Kinder sah, bat er sie zu gehen, damit sein Entschluss nicht geschwächt werde.

Das Urteil wurde verlesen; Hans blieb schweigend. Kein Wort der Kritik war gegen seine persönlichen Sitten erhoben worden. Stattdessen ging es um seine Weigerung, seine Gemeinde aufzulösen. Er blieb standhaft, und so führte der Henker, Paul Vollmar, Hans zum Richtplatz. Einige Beobachter meinten, Vollmar habe Hans einen Moment losgelassen, scheinbar um ihm eine Fluchtmöglichkeit zu geben. Als Hans diese nicht ergriff, hob Vollmar die Hände gen Himmel und bat Gott um Vergebung für das, was das Gesetz von ihm verlangte. Hans vergab dem Mann mit einem Lächeln, während verschiedene kirchliche Amtspersonen ihn zum Widerruf ermahnten; Hans entgegnete, er habe bei ihnen keine Reue gesehen.

Vollmar, am Ort der Hinrichtung angekommen, gab Hans die Gelegenheit, ungestört zu sprechen, und Hans sprach nur kurz: „Ich weiß nicht, was ich mehr sagen sollte, als daß ich wünsche, alle mögen zur Erkenntnis ihrer Sünden kommen und Buße tun, damit sie gerettet werden; das wünsche ich für jeden.”

Dann kniete er, in Sichtweite der Stelle, an der fast ein Jahrhundert zuvor Felix Manz sein Leben gelassen hatte, und neigte sein Haupt. Das Schwert blitzte nieder, und Paul Vollmar stellte die rituelle Frage: „Habe ich diesen Mann rechtmäßig getötet?”

„Ja,” lautete die Antwort, „du hast diesen armen Mann hingerichtet.”

Die unmittelbare Wirkung des Opfers des alten Hans war eine Welle von Unterstützung und Entrüstung in der nicht-täuferischen Gemeinschaft. Rhudlof Rhan und Conrad Grebel setzten die Verfolgung der verbliebenen Täufer fort und ließen Margaretha Landis, Hans’ Witwe, nach ihrer Weigerung, ihren Forderungen nachzukommen, in der städtischen Hospitalirung in Einzelhaft halten. Hans’ Kinder blieben ebenfalls standhaft und weigerten sich, zu widerrufen, doch mehrere seiner Enkel begannen kurz nach der Hinrichtung ihres Großvaters, die Stadtkirche zu besuchen.

Auch die lokale täuferische Gemeinde blieb stark. Ihre geistlichen Nachfolger trugen das Wort Christi mit sich, als sie ein Jahrhundert später in großer Auswanderung an die wilden Ufer der Neuen Welt gelangten. Hier, in der Religionsfreiheit Pennsylvanias, gründeten sie neue Gemeinden, in denen der Glaube, der Hans Landis das Leben kostete, über kommende Generationen hinweg aufblühte.
