“왜 아직까지 암 치료제가 없는 거죠?” 내 환자가 나에게 물었다.

나는 어깨를 으쓱했다. “암에는 여러 종류가 있습니다.”라고 말했다. “어떤 암은 치료법이 있지만, 다른 암들은 아직 어떻게 가장 잘 치료할지 배우는 중입니다.”

“제 생각에는,” 내 환자는 자신이 일급 비밀 이론을 전하는 것 같은 확신을 가지고 말했다. “사실 암에 대한 치료법이 있는데 제약회사들이 우리에게 알리고 싶어하지 않는 것 같아요.”

나는 머리를 저었다. “우리는 최선을 다하고 있다고 생각합니다.”라고 그에게 말했다. “암 치료에 관해서는 많은 진전이 있었지만, 아직도 갈 길이 멉니다.”

암은 무서운 병이다. 한 기독교 남성은 죽는 것을 두려워하지는 않지만, 만약 선택권이 있다면 암으로 죽는 것보다는 거의 어떤 다른 방식으로 죽는 편을 택하겠다고 말했다.

그보다 더한 것은 암이 신비롭게 보인다는 점이다. 암에 걸리는 사람이 더 많은 것처럼 보이지만, 아무도 정확히 이유를 모르는 것 같다.

이 글에서는 암이 무엇인지, 그리고 암 선별검사에 관해 살펴보려고 한다. 다음 호에서(주님이 허락하신다면) 암에 대해 사용 가능한 치료법들 가운데 몇 가지를 논의하겠다.

여기에서 밝히자면 나는 가정의학과 의사다. 나는 암 환자들을 많이 돌보아 왔지만, 결코 종양학자(온콜로지스트)는 아니며 암에 대해 모든 것을 아는 것도 아니다. 내가 이해하는 바를 기꺼이 나누겠다.

암이란 무엇인가?

많은 것들과 마찬가지로, 우리는 암의 기원을 에덴 동산에서 인간의 타락으로 거슬러 올라가 설명할 수 있다. 하나님은 사람을 완전하게 창조하셨음을 우리는 안다. 원래 창조된 상태에서는 암이 없었을 뿐만 아니라 암에 걸리지도 않았을 것이다.

암이 무엇인지 이해하려면 정상 조직과 세포가 어떻게 행동하는지를 이해해야 한다.

정상 세포는 일정 기간 살아 있다가 죽는다. 이 과정을 세포자멸사(apoptosis)라고 한다. 이것은 세포가 지속적으로 교체되도록 보장한다. 또한 하나의 세포 유형이 “선을 넘어” 제자리에 있지 않은 곳에서 증식하는 것을 막는다.

세포가 분열할 때마다 DNA를 딸세포에게 복사한다. 보통은 오류 없이 이루어지지만 가끔 복사 과정에서 오류가 발생한다. 우리는 이러한 오류를 돌연변이라고 부른다.

암세포는 정상적인 행동에 대한 제동을 잃은 세포들이다. DNA의 돌연변이 때문에 이들은 더 이상 한정된 수명을 갖지 않으며 자신이 몸의 어디에 있어야 하는지의 경계를 지키지 않는다. 대신 주변 조직을 침범하기 시작하고 그 과정에서 추가적인 혈액 공급과 영양분을 끌어들인다.

암세포는 국소적으로 커질 수 있고, 림프계나 순환계를 통해 몸의 먼 부위로 퍼질 수 있다. 암세포가 원래 발생한 장소가 아닌 다른 위치로 옮겨간 경우 우리는 그것을 전이(metastases)라고 부른다.

암의 유형은 통제 불능으로 증식하는 세포의 종류에 의해 결정된다. 의사들은 일반적으로 “피부암”이라고만 말하지 않는다. 피부 세포에서 시작하는 암들이 있긴 하지만, 대신 이러한 암들을 기저세포암(basal cell carcinoma), 편평세포암(squamous cell carcinoma), 흑색종(melanoma)으로 분류한다—각각이 다른 종류의 피부 세포를 가리킨다. 이들 각 피부암은 서로 다르게 행동한다. 기저세포암과 편평세포암은 국소 부위에서 커지고 거의 다른 곳으로 퍼지지 않는 반면, 흑색종은 다른 부위로 전이될 가능성이 매우 높다.

또한, 암이 치료에 어떻게 반응하는지는 단순히 발생한 장기에 의해서가 아니라 그것이 유래한 세포 유형에 의해 좌우된다.

돌연변이의 원인…

홍수 이전 시대에 암이 얼마나 흔했는지는 알 수 없다. 나는 비교적 드물었을 것이라고 추측한다.

우리는 홍수 이전에 사람들이 매우 오래 살았다는 것을 안다—종종 900년대까지 살았다. 돌연변이는 드물었음에 틀림없다. 그들의 DNA는 원래 인류의 유전적 표본(따라서 완전성)에 더 가까웠으며, 우리 21st세기(서기) 사람들보다 더 완전에 가까웠다. 따라서 유전자가 돌연변이로 변하고 비정상적인 유전자가 생겨날 확률은 지금보다 훨씬 적었다.

…환경적 요인

그보다 더하여, 홍수 무렵에 돌연변이율을 증가시킨 무언가가 있었을 것이다. 어쩌면 방사선 수치가 증가했을 수도 있다. 아마도 암이 점차 나타나도록 하는 유전적 변화들이 있었을지도 모른다.

성경에는 암이 직접적으로 언급되어 있지 않지만, 히스기야의 “종기”가 어떤 종류의 암성 성장일 가능성도 있다. 또한 언약궤가 블레셋 땅에 있을 때 블레셋 사람들에게 영향을 미쳤던 어떤 질병들이 암성 종양이었을 가능성도 있다.

사람들은 홍수 이후 더 젊은 나이에 죽기 시작했고, 아브라함 시대 직후에는 거의 백세를 넘기지 못했다.

오늘날 우리는 세포의 복제 기계와 DNA를 손상시키는 것들이 암 위험을 증가시킨다는 것을 알고 있다. 그중 가장 잘 알려진 것은 방사선이다.

히로시마와 나가사키에 원자폭탄이 투하된 후 생존자들에게서 특정 종류의 암이 크게 증가한 것이 관찰되었다. 백혈병(혈액의 암)이 가장 흔한 유형이었고, 그 다음으로 위암, 폐암, 간암, 유방암이 뒤를 이었다.

방사선은 대부분의 사람들이 일상적으로 접하는 것은 아니다. 그러나 엑스레이 부서에서 일하거나 어떤 종류의 암을 치료하기 위해 방사선 치료를 받았던 경우, 일반 대중보다 훨씬 높은 수준의 방사선에 노출되었을 가능성이 있다.

암 증가와 관련된 다른 요인들도 많이 있다. 자외선 노출은 피부암 위험을 높이며, 그래서 의사들이 햇볕을 즐길 때 자외선 노출을 제한하기 위해 자외선 차단제와 보호복을 권장하는 큰 이유 중 하나다.

마지막으로, 다양한 작업 환경에서 존재하는 많은 화학물질들이 암 위험을 증가시킬 수 있다.

…건강에 해로운 음식

질산염(nitrites)이 많이 함유된 음식은 장(腸) 암의 위험을 증가시킨다. 질산염은 일반적으로 훈제 및 가공육에 존재한다. 따라서 건강을 위해 사람들은 이러한 음식의 섭취를 전혀 하지 않거나 적어도 전체 식단에서 매우 제한된 비율로 제한해야 한다.

…특정한 이전 질병들

또 한 가지 언급할 것은 특정 유형의 감염이 암 위험을 증가시킬 수 있다는 점이다. 전염성 단핵구증을 일으키는 엡스타인-바 바이러스는 특정 종류의 림프종과 관련이 있다. B형 및 C형 간염은 간세포암(간암)의 위험을 높인다. 위의 헬리코박터 파일로리 감염은 위암과 연관되어 있다.

이러한 바이러스 중 하나를 가지고 있었다고 해서 반드시 그 감염으로 인해 암에 걸리는 것은 아니라는 점을 기억하는 것이 중요하다. 오히려 단지 그 사람에게 미래 어느 시점에 암이 발생할 위험을 높일 뿐이다.

…건강에 해로운 습관

마지막으로 언급할 것은 특정 독소들이 암 위험을 극적으로 증가시킨다는 것이다. 명백한 예는 담배 사용으로, 폐암, 인후암, 심지어 방광암의 위험을 강하게 증가시킨다. 알코올도 또 다른 위험 요인이다. 알코올은 구강 및 인후암, 위장관 암, 간암의 위험을 높인다. 이러한 독성 물질에 대한 안전한 노출량은 사실상 없지만, 확실히 노출 정도가 높을수록 더 나쁘다.

암 선별검사

다양한 암을 선별할 수 있다고 주장하는 많은 검사들이 있다. 이들 대부분은 적어도 암을 조기 발견하는 데 어느 정도 효과가 있다. 그러나 일부 검사에는 특정 문제가 있어 그 검사가 실제로 선별 과정에 도움이 되지 못함을 시사한다.

좋은 출발점은 완벽한 선별검사가 어떤 모습일지를 생각해 보는 것이다. 이는 어떤 검사가 유익할지 또는 그렇지 않을지를 판단하는 데 도움이 된다.

완벽한 선별검사는 여러 특징을 갖는다. 첫째, 위양성(false positive)이나 위음성(false negative) 결과가 전혀 없어야 한다. 다시 말해, 검사에서 양성인 모든 사람은 암이 있어야 하고 음성인 사람은 암이 없어야 한다. 다음으로, 검사는 암이 치료하기 쉬운 단계에서 이를 식별해야 한다. 검사는 저렴하고 최소한의 침습적이어야 하며 방사선 노출도 최소화해야 한다.

불행히도 우리가 현재 선별용으로 시행하는 어떤 검사도 이러한 기준을 완전히 충족하지는 못한다.

한 가지 이유는 많은 검사들이 위양성과 위음성 결과를 모두 산출한다는 점이다. 이 둘은 모두 문제다. 위음성 검사의 문제는 명백하다—실제로 암이 있는데도 암이 없다고 생각하게 만든다. 반면 위양성 검사는 더 높은 불안 수준과 환자에게 암이 실제로 없다는 것을 확인하기 위해 필요한 추가 검사들의 비용과 위험을 초래한다.

이와 관련해 나쁜 예의 하나는 CEA-125이다. CEA-125는 일부 유형의 암이 만들어내는 화학물질이다. 종양학자들은 화학요법에 대한 환자의 반응을 추적하기 위해 이 수치를 사용한다.

이것을 이러한 암들에 대한 선별검사로 사용할 수 있을 것 같지만, 단순히 작동하지 않는다. 암이 없음에도 불구하고 CEA 수치가 상승해 있는 사람이 많고 반대로 많은 위장관(GI) 암은 전혀 이 화학물질을 만들지 않는다. 많은 사람들을 대상으로 CEA-125 검사를 하면 스캔과 생검이 더 많이 이루어지겠지만, 암으로 인한 사망률에 상당한 영향을 미칠지는 의문이다.

또 다른 문제는 특정 암 자체와 관련이 있다. 검사가 도움이 되려면 암이 전암 단계들(precancerous stages)을 거치며 오랜 기간에 걸쳐 진행되어야 한다.

예로 대장암이 있다. 대장암이 발생하는 대부분의 사람들은 암이 생기기 수년 전에 전암성 용종을 가지고 있다. 이 때문에 대장내시경은 대장암으로의 진행을 예방하는 데 효과적일 수 있다.

환자가 대장내시경을 받으면 의사는 용종의 존재를 감지할 수 있다. 더 나아가, 내시경을 통해 용종을 제거할 수 있어 암으로의 진행을 멈출 수 있다.

마지막으로 관련된 점은 조기 발견에 이득이 있어야 한다는 것이다. 만약 새로운 검사가 기존 검사보다 암을 6개월 더 일찍 발견할 수 있다면, 다른 것이 변하지 않더라도 사람들은 평균적으로 암과 함께 6개월 더 오래 살게 된다.

문제는 암을 더 일찍 진단하는 것이 더 효과적인 치료로 이어지는가이다. 림프절로 퍼지기 전에 암을 제거할 수 있어 화학요법의 필요를 완전히 피할 수 있는가?

치료와 반응률이 암을 진단하는 단계에 관계없이 동일하다면, 선별검사는 실제로 의미가 없다.

미국예방서비스 태스크포스(United States Preventive Services Task Force)는 다양한 검사에 관한 문헌을 검토한 전문가 자원봉사 패널이다. 이용 가능한 검사들에 대해 수행된 연구들을 바탕으로 이들은 다양한 검사와 검사 시행 빈도에 대한 권고를 제시한다.

이 패널은 많은 암 학회들보다 권고에서 더 보수적인 경향이 있다. 예를 들어, 이들은 50세에서 75세 사이의 여성에게 유방촬영술(맘모그램)을 격년(2년마다) 권장하는 반면 다른 단체들은 매년 선별을 권장한다.

각 권고에는 특정 권고를 뒷받침하는 연구들의 수준에 대한 등급과 그 연구들에 대한 링크가 있다. 그들의 권고는 잘 조사되어 있다. 이것은 저위험군 사람이 어떤 검사를 할지 결정하는 데 도움이 된다. 가족력이나 노출 때문에 고위험군인 사람에게는 이들의 권고가 덜 도움이 된다.

암이 주는 도전들

사람들은 종종 암을 하나의 실체인 것처럼 논의한다. 앞서 언급했듯이 암은 단 하나의 것이 아니다. 피부암은 림프종과 다르게 행동하고, 림프종은 결합조직암(sarcoma)과 또 다르게 행동한다. 사람들이 말하는 “암에 대한 단 하나의 치료(암 치료제)”가 언젠가 나올 가능성은 낮다.

암세포를 다루는 데 있어 더 큰 도전은 이들이 정상 세포와 매우 유사하다는 점이다. 기본적으로 우리는 정상 조직보다 암을 조금 더 독살하려고 시도하고 있다. 현재 사용 가능한 다양한 치료법들이 존재한다. 2부에서는 오늘날 이용 가능한 몇 가지 선택지와 미래에 나올 수 있는 다른 선택지들을 다루겠다.

마지막 생각들

암이라는 주제를 생각할 때 몇 가지 떠오르는 점이 있다.

우리는 두려움 속에 살거나 두려움 때문에 선택을 내릴 필요가 없다. 두려워하지 말라 내가 너와 함께 함이라 놀라지 말라 나는 네 하나님이 됨이라 내가 너를 굳세게 하리라 참으로 내가 너를 도우리라 참으로 나의 의로운 오른손으로 너를 붙들리라—이사야 41:10.

나는 우리가 단순히 ‘하나님의 뜻’이니 해서 어떤 일이 일어나도록 운명론적으로 내버려 두어야 한다고 생각하지 않는다. 우리는 지혜로운 선택을 해야 하고, 그러고 나서는 불안 상태에 살지 않아야 한다.

그러므로 무엇을 먹을까 무엇을 마실까 무엇을 입을까 염려하지 말라(저희는 다 이방인들이 구하는 것들이니라) 너희 하늘 아버지께서는 너희가 이 모든 것이 있어야 할 줄을 아시느니라 오직 너희는 먼저 그의 나라와 그의 의를 구하라 그리하면 이 모든 것을 너희에게 더하시리라 그러므로 내일 일을 위하여 염려하지 말라 내일 일은 내일 염려할 것이요 각 날의 괴로움은 그 날에 족하니라—마태복음 6:31-34.

마지막으로, 우리가 지혜로운 결정으로 특정 암이 형성되거나 퍼지는 것을 예방할 수 있다면, 그것은 합리적인 목표처럼 보인다. 우리 누구도 이 몸 안에서 영원히 살지는 못하겠지만, 만약 우리가 암이 아닌 다른 무엇으로 죽을 수 있다면 그것도 좋은 목표인 것 같다. 하나님께서 우리에게 주신 몸을 돌보는 지혜를 우리에게 주시기를 바란다.

Glancing up at the sun, Beto (a made-up name) quickened his already hurried pace as he approached the forest. He knew that he would need to hurry if he wanted to make it through the forest before dark. Large wildcats were known to roam in the surrounding mountains, and many were the terrifying stories of these cats attacking people in this very forest!

Entering the cool shade of the forest, Beto paused just long enough for a refreshing drink of water from the creek that meandered across the footpath.

Several hours later, as he pushed wearily onward, Beto rounded a bend in the trail and, thinking he saw a movement in the bushes ahead, stopped abruptly. In the gathering darkness Beto watched as, not thirty paces before him, the dreaded beast he so tremendously feared crept out of the bushes and turned to face him! Turning, Beto fled for his life! Hearing the padding of the wildcat’s enormous paws on the forest floor behind him, Beto tried to pump his tired legs even faster. Suddenly, not being able to see the path clearly in the darkness of the forest, Beto tripped on a vine and sprawled helplessly onto the ground. Weeping bitterly, Beto concluded that it was useless to continue trying, so he lay on the ground, waiting for the inevitable. As he waited, he imagined that he could hear the sound of the wildcat moving in closer, closer, closer…

* * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * *

Are you feeling a bit like Beto? Is there a big “something” inflicting pain in your life and you’re trying to get away from it? Maybe your friends have forsaken you or a brother or sister has slandered you. Maybe someone you highly respected has trampled over you or you are experiencing difficult situations in your family. Maybe you are experiencing something painful that no one else knows about and all that others see is your “smiling” exterior, never realizing the pain you’re feeling inside. Whatever it is that you’re dealing with, have you, like Beto, concluded that it’s useless to keep trying?

At times we experience painful situations that cause us to feel like giving up. We naturally hate pain and do our best to avoid it. Still, we meet up with some of those hard things of life. We don’t want to nurse an attitude of self-pity, going through life with an “I am a victim” mentality. It would be foolish, however, to assume that there is no such thing as a victim. Sometimes people commit sins against each other. There are times when we find ourselves victims of circumstances over which we have no control.

Situations like this are painful and confusing, sometimes causing us to feel like just throwing up our hands in despair. How do we go from feeling like poor victims to being …more than conquerors through him that loved us –Romans 8:37?

Let’s take a look at a few things that we must understand if we are to overcome these battles and continue to thrive spiritually…

…Unreserved surrender

We must understand the importance of unreserved surrender to the Lord Jesus Christ. This means that we are willing to serve Him for the rest of our life, no matter what the cost. We need to be aware that we will face difficulties in life (1 Peter 4:12,13). Being Christians does not give us a trial-free life. Living the life of a Christian does in fact, often bring hardships of its own. Why, then, does Jesus teach that His yoke is easy and His burden light?—…For my yoke is easy, and my burden is light –Matthew 11:28-30. The answer… Because He is willing to help us bear our burdens, we don’t need to do it alone! If we are willing to serve the Lord only in good times, then we will soon feel like giving up when we meet hardship.

…Forgiveness

Usually, when we experience a difficult situation, other people are involved in some way. Sometimes hot words are exchanged, or evil action is taken, and people end up hurting each other. When we’ve been wronged, we know that we should forgive the person who wronged us, yet we hesitate, because we’d really like to see justice carried out. We fear that if we forgive the other person, then we will set him or her free before they realize how wrong they were, so we choose unforgiveness!

Unforgiveness always leads to bitterness; bitterness always shackles us. Always! Bitterness often brings with it a host of other sins and causes much trouble for us and for others. (Hebrews 12:14-17) However, when we choose to forgive others, God will also forgive us (Mark 11:25,26), setting us free from the awful mess that bitterness creates in our lives. We no longer need to worry about holding the offender captive. After all, he or she is not in bondage to us. We cannot choose whether or not they will be set free. Only the Lord has the power to set someone free.

We must understand what forgiveness is or else we will find ourselves wondering whether or not we have forgiven. Following are three points that will help us understand what it really means to forgive:

1. Accept it

Sometimes we face difficulties as the result of our own choices and sometimes as the result of other people’s choices. When other people make choices that cause pain in our life we have a hard time accepting it. We may try to fight this pain in an effort to remove it from our life, or we may try to run away from it in an effort to escape its dreadful reality. We may put up a “tough” facade to try to make others believe it’s really not so bad when in reality it just plain hurts! While these reactions come naturally, we won’t find relief until we’ve come to a place of acceptance. To accept it doesn’t mean to do nothing about it but, rather, to realize that sometimes God allows painful situations in life to help us grow. (James 1:2-4) It means to trust the Lord instead of trying to figure things out on our own. (Proverbs 3:4,5) It also means to admit that we’ve been hurt and that we need God to help us heal.

2. Let it go

What’s the quickest way to get rid of something you no longer want? Give it away! That’s exactly what we must do with those painful burdens we sometimes find ourselves carrying. Give them to God. (1 Peter 5:6,7) It is very important, when we give our burdens to God, that we leave them there. We would feel very foolish taking a load of garbage to the local landfill, and then turning around and taking it all back home without dumping it! None of us would even consider doing such a thing. Yet, when we bring a burden to the Lord, we sometimes go through a formal ritual of telling God about it but never letting it go.

How do you let go of something that has become so much a part of you and is so painful that you can think of little else? A good place to start is to find a stable believer with whom you can comfortably converse and talk with about it. Even more importantly, talk with God about it. (Hebrews 4:14-16) It doesn’t matter if you find a place to be alone with God or if you find someone to pray with you. What really matters is to find a place where you can get on your knees and tell the Lord exactly how you are feeling. You can tell Him that you feel you were treated unjustly. You can tell Him all about the pain, the confusion and the feelings of hatred and revenge that you are feeling. Make a point of telling God that you choose to forgive the offender. Be specific, mentioning the name of the offender and specific situations. This can be very painful because it brings fresh memories of difficult situations. It is a time of soul searching, forgiving, and letting go. Stay on your knees until you are at peace about the situation. It doesn’t matter how long it takes as long as you get rid of that awful burden—try to not be mindful of the time. Be assured that God never ignores a plea for help! (1Peter 3:12)

3. Love your enemies

Jesus commands us to love our enemies. (Matthew 5:43-48) When we have forgiven, we will genuinely love the offender the way that God loves them. According to human reasoning, this isn’t possible. It’s the miracle of a changed heart that causes us to love someone we once hated.

…Worship the Lord

Often, we don’t feel like worshiping the Lord in the middle of a trial but why should we quit worshiping Him when we need Him the most? (Philippians 4:4-7) We ought to at least think of some things for which to be thankful, then thank God for them. In Acts 16, we read an account of Paul and Silas preaching in Philippi. After they had healed a demon-possessed girl they were severely beaten by the local authorities, secured in stocks, and locked in prison. Their situation must surely have felt hopeless. They were in pain, they couldn’t move, and it was night. It probably felt like a dark time in their lives. In spite of all this, they prayed and sang praises to God! They were living lives of unreserved surrender to a God Whom they loved and trusted. In the end, God chose to miraculously deliver them.

Praising God in the middle of trials is only possible when Christ is reigning in our lives.

…Move forward

When we experience difficulties there are always things we can learn. We learn the importance of complete dependence on and unconditional surrender to the Lord. We experience, at a personal level, the comfort of God and we are called to reach out to other troubled souls with this comfort. (2 Corinthians 1:1-7)

Dear friends, remember, the next time the cares of life make you feel like giving up, bring your burden to the Lord, put it all in His hands, and let it go!

En levant les yeux vers le soleil, Beto (un nom inventé) accéléra le pas déjà rapide en approchant de la forêt. Il savait qu’il devrait se hâter s’il voulait traverser la forêt avant la nuit. De grands félins sauvages étaient connus pour rôder dans les montagnes environnantes, et nombreuses étaient les terrifiantes histoires de ces chats attaquant des gens dans cette même forêt !

Entrant dans la fraîcheur de l’ombre de la forêt, Beto s’arrêta juste assez longtemps pour boire de l’eau rafraîchissante dans le ruisseau qui serpentait sur le sentier.

Plusieurs heures plus tard, alors qu’il avançait péniblement, Beto contourna un virage du sentier et, croyant avoir vu un mouvement dans les buissons devant lui, s’arrêta net. Dans l’obscurité qui tombait, Beto regarda, à moins de trente pas devant lui, la bête redoutée qu’il craignait tant sortir des buissons et se tourner pour lui faire face ! Se retournant, Beto s’enfuit pour sauver sa vie ! Entendant le bruit des énormes pattes du félin sur le sol de la forêt derrière lui, Beto tenta de presser encore davantage ses jambes fatiguées. Soudain, ne voyant plus clairement le chemin dans l’obscurité de la forêt, Beto trébucha sur une liane et s’étala, impuissant, sur le sol. Pleurant amèrement, Beto en conclut qu’il était inutile de continuer d’essayer, alors il resta allongé sur le sol, attendant l’inévitable. Pendant qu’il attendait, il s’imaginait entendre le bruit du félin qui s’approchait, de plus en plus près…

* * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * *

Vous sentez-vous un peu comme Beto ? Y a-t-il un grand « quelque chose » qui vous inflige de la douleur et dont vous essayez de vous éloigner ? Peut-être que vos amis vous ont abandonné ou qu’un frère ou une sœur vous a calomnié. Peut-être que quelqu’un que vous respectiez beaucoup vous a piétiné ou que vous traversez des situations difficiles dans votre famille. Peut-être vivez-vous quelque chose de douloureux que personne d’autre ne connaît et que tout ce que les autres voient est votre extérieur « souriant », sans jamais se douter de la douleur que vous ressentez à l’intérieur. Quelle que soit la chose à laquelle vous êtes confronté, avez-vous, comme Beto, conclu qu’il est inutile de continuer d’essayer ?

Parfois nous affrontons des situations pénibles qui nous donnent envie d’abandonner. Nous détestons naturellement la souffrance et faisons de notre mieux pour l’éviter. Pourtant, nous rencontrons certaines de ces épreuves de la vie. Nous ne voulons pas nourrir une attitude d’apitoiement sur nous-mêmes, vivre en répétant « je suis une victime ». Il serait toutefois insensé de prétendre qu’il n’existe pas de victimes. Parfois les gens commettent des péchés les uns contre les autres. Il y a des moments où nous nous retrouvons victimes de circonstances sur lesquelles nous n’avons aucun contrôle.

Des situations comme celles-ci sont douloureuses et confuses, et parfois nous donnent l’impression de lever les mains en désespoir. Comment passer du sentiment d’être de pauvres victimes à être …plus que vainqueurs par celui qui nous a aimés – Romains 8:37?

Voyons quelques éléments que nous devons comprendre si nous voulons vaincre ces combats et continuer à prospérer spirituellement…

…abandon sans réserves

Nous devons comprendre l’importance de l’abandon sans réserves au Seigneur Jésus-Christ. Cela signifie que nous sommes prêts à Le servir pour le reste de notre vie, quel qu’en soit le coût. Nous devons être conscients que nous ferons face à des difficultés dans la vie (1 Pierre 4:12,13). Être chrétien ne nous donne pas une vie sans épreuves. Vivre la vie chrétienne apporte en effet souvent ses propres difficultés. Alors pourquoi Jésus enseigne-t-Il que son joug est facile et que son fardeau est léger ? —…Car mon joug est facile, et mon fardeau léger – Matthieu 11:28-30. La réponse… Parce qu’il est disposé à nous aider à porter nos fardeaux, nous n’avons pas à le faire seuls ! Si nous sommes prêts à servir le Seigneur seulement dans les bons moments, nous nous sentirons bientôt prêts à abandonner quand nous rencontrerons des épreuves.

…le pardon

La plupart du temps, quand nous vivons une situation difficile, d’autres personnes sont d’une manière ou d’une autre impliquées. Parfois des paroles dures sont échangées, ou des actions mauvaises sont commises, et des gens finissent par se blesser mutuellement. Quand nous avons été lésés, nous savons que nous devrions pardonner à la personne qui nous a fait tort, pourtant nous hésitons, parce que nous aimerions vraiment voir la justice s’accomplir. Nous craignons que si nous pardonnons à l’autre personne, nous la libérerons avant qu’elle ne réalise à quel point elle avait tort, alors nous choisissons le refus de pardonner !

Le refus de pardonner mène toujours à l’amertume ; l’amertume nous enchaîne toujours. Toujours ! L’amertume entraîne souvent avec elle une foule d’autres péchés et cause beaucoup de problèmes pour nous et pour les autres. (Hébreux 12:14-17) Cependant, lorsque nous choisissons de pardonner aux autres, Dieu nous pardonnera aussi (Marc 11:25,26), nous libérant du terrible chaos que l’amertume crée dans nos vies. Nous n’avons plus besoin de nous inquiéter de maintenir l’offenseur captif. Après tout, il ou elle n’est pas enchaîné(e) à nous. Nous ne pouvons pas décider s’il/elle sera libéré(e) ou non. Seul le Seigneur a le pouvoir de libérer quelqu’un.

Nous devons comprendre ce qu’est le pardon sinon nous nous retrouverons à nous demander si nous avons pardonné ou non. Voici trois points qui nous aideront à comprendre ce que signifie réellement pardonner :

1. L’accepter

Parfois nous faisons face à des difficultés à la suite de nos propres choix et parfois à la suite des choix d’autrui. Quand d’autres personnes font des choix qui causent de la douleur dans notre vie, nous avons du mal à l’accepter. Nous pouvons essayer de lutter contre cette douleur pour la supprimer de notre vie, ou nous pouvons tenter de l’éviter pour échapper à sa cruelle réalité. Nous pouvons afficher une façade « dure » pour faire croire aux autres que ce n’est pas si grave alors qu’en réalité cela fait très mal ! Bien que ces réactions soient naturelles, nous ne trouverons pas de soulagement tant que nous ne serons pas parvenus à un lieu d’acceptation. L’accepter ne signifie pas ne rien faire à ce sujet, mais plutôt réaliser que parfois Dieu permet des situations douloureuses dans la vie pour nous aider à grandir. (Jacques 1:2-4) Cela signifie faire confiance au Seigneur au lieu d’essayer de tout comprendre par nous-mêmes. (Proverbes 3:4,5) Cela signifie aussi admettre que nous avons été blessés et que nous avons besoin de l’aide de Dieu pour guérir.

2. Lâcher prise

Quelle est la façon la plus rapide de se débarrasser de quelque chose que vous ne voulez plus ? Le donner ! C’est exactement ce que nous devons faire avec ces fardeaux douloureux que nous portons parfois. Donnez-les à Dieu. (1 Pierre 5:6,7) Il est très important, quand nous remettons nos fardeaux à Dieu, de les laisser là. Nous nous sentirions très bêtes d’apporter un sac d’ordures à la décharge locale, puis de faire demi-tour pour tout ramener à la maison sans rien déverser ! Aucun de nous ne considérerait même faire une telle chose. Pourtant, quand nous apportons un fardeau au Seigneur, nous passons parfois par un rituel formel de lui en parler sans jamais le lâcher.

Comment lâcher prise de quelque chose qui est devenu si intégré en vous et si douloureux que vous ne pouvez penser à presque rien d’autre ? Un bon point de départ est de trouver un croyant stable avec qui vous pouvez converser confortablement à ce sujet. Plus important encore, parlez-en à Dieu. (Hébreux 4:14-16) Peu importe si vous trouvez un endroit pour être seul avec Dieu ou si vous trouvez quelqu’un pour prier avec vous. Ce qui compte vraiment, c’est de trouver un lieu où vous pouvez vous mettre à genoux et dire au Seigneur exactement ce que vous ressentez. Vous pouvez Lui dire que vous estimez avoir été traité injustement. Vous pouvez Lui raconter toute la douleur, la confusion et les sentiments de haine et de vengeance que vous éprouvez. Prenez la décision de dire à Dieu que vous choisissez de pardonner à l’offenseur. Soyez précis, en mentionnant le nom de l’offenseur et des situations spécifiques. Cela peut être très douloureux parce que cela réveille de nouveaux souvenirs de situations difficiles. C’est un temps d’examen de conscience, de pardon et de lâcher-prise. Restez à genoux jusqu’à ce que vous soyez en paix au sujet de la situation. Peu importe combien de temps cela prend, tant que vous vous débarrassez de ce fardeau affreux — essayez de ne pas regarder l’heure. Soyez assuré que Dieu n’ignore jamais une supplication de secours ! (1 Pierre 3:12)

3. Aimez vos ennemis

Jésus nous commande d’aimer nos ennemis. (Matthieu 5:43-48) Quand nous avons pardonné, nous aimerons sincèrement l’offenseur de la manière dont Dieu l’aime. Selon le raisonnement humain, cela n’est pas possible. C’est le miracle d’un cœur changé qui nous pousse à aimer quelqu’un que nous avons autrefois haï.

…Adorez le Seigneur

Souvent, nous n’avons pas envie d’adorer le Seigneur au milieu d’une épreuve, mais pourquoi cesserions-nous de L’adorer quand nous avons le plus besoin de Lui ? (Philippiens 4:4-7) Nous devrions au moins penser à quelques choses pour lesquelles être reconnaissants, puis remercier Dieu pour elles. Dans Actes 16, nous lisons le récit de Paul et Silas prêchant à Philippes. Après avoir guéri une jeune fille possédée d’un démon, ils furent sévèrement battus par les autorités locales, entravés et jetés en prison. Leur situation devait sûrement paraître sans espoir. Ils souffraient, ils ne pouvaient pas bouger, et c’était la nuit. Cela a probablement paru être une période sombre de leur vie. Malgré tout cela, ils prièrent et chantèrent des louanges à Dieu ! Ils menaient des vies d’abandon sans réserves envers un Dieu qu’ils aimaient et en qui ils avaient confiance. Finalement, Dieu choisit de les délivrer miraculeusement.

Louer Dieu au milieu des épreuves n’est possible que lorsque Christ règne dans nos vies.

…Allez de l’avant

Lorsque nous vivons des difficultés, il y a toujours des choses que nous pouvons apprendre. Nous apprenons l’importance d’une dépendance complète et d’un abandon inconditionnel au Seigneur. Nous faisons l’expérience, à un niveau personnel, de la consolation de Dieu et nous sommes appelés à tendre cette consolation à d’autres âmes troublées. (2 Corinthiens 1:1-7)

Chers amis, souvenez-vous, la prochaine fois que les soucis de la vie vous donnent envie d’abandonner, apportez votre fardeau au Seigneur, mettez-le entièrement entre Ses mains, et lâchez-le !

In the last couple of years, something that God has been working on in my heart is the area of submission. I don’t want to look back in a wrong way, but I see where I have failed my husband in the role that God has given for me to function as his helper, one that is meet for him. As I have been thinking about my own life, I have come to realize how important our role is as Christian women, in our homes and in the lives of our children.

I realize that our children are going to need to make their own decision when it comes to being a disciple of Christ, but my desire is that I am not the reason that our children rebel against the Word of God. When we honor our husbands the way that God has taught in His Word, the example of our lives will draw the unbelieving to Christ. In the flesh, we will not be able to honor our husbands in a way that will bring glory to God, but with Christ we can do all things according to His will.

I have a burden about this because in the last couple of months I have noticed how much our homes are under constant attack from the enemy of our souls, as he tries to use our flesh and the world. As I write on this, I don’t feel that I will do justice to it, so I will just write some of my thoughts and pray that all who read this article will be encouraged in their marriages to honor, respect, and love their husbands.

  • Nevertheless let … the wife see that she reverence her husband –Ephesians 5:33.
  • Likewise, ye wives, be in subjection to your own husbands… –1 Peter 3:1.
  • Even as Sara obeyed Abraham, calling him lord: whose daughters ye are… –1 Peter 3:6.
  • Wives, submit yourselves unto your own husbands, as unto the Lord –Ephesians 5:22.
  • But I would have you know, that the head of every man is Christ; and the head of the woman is the man; and the head of Christ is God –1 Corinthians 11:3.
  • Let the woman learn in silence with all subjection. But I suffer not a woman to teach, nor to usurp authority over the man, but to be in silence. For Adam was first formed, then Eve. And Adam was not deceived, but the woman being deceived was in the transgression –1 Timothy 2:11-14.
  • Therefore as the church is subject unto Christ, so let the wives be [subject] to their own husbands in every thing –Ephesians 5:24.
  • Let your women keep silence in the churches: for it is not permitted unto them to speak; but they are commanded to be under obedience, as also saith the law –1 Corinthians 14:34.

These Scriptures are not my own, but God’s. He gives us His Word to read and to live by because that is the only way we will be able to have peace and harmony in our homes. Even more importantly, the ONLY way that we can have a clear conscience before God is when we are in the center of His will.

When we think of submission, what comes to mind? Do we think that if we submit, we will be taken advantage of? Do we think that we are wiser than our husbands? I know to the flesh this sounds kind of hard, but if we could only realize that if we don’t allow our husbands to lead out and make decisions, we are only crippling them. The reality is that if our husbands make mistakes, it is okay because we ourselves make mistakes as well. Also, if we are born again, and we are walking with God, but our husbands are not, God will still take care of us. The Scriptures teach that if our husband is not in his place, then through the wife walking according to the clear teaching that God has given her in His Word, the husband can be won through her conversation (or by the way she conducts her life).

We need to trust God with our whole lives, even in the area of our marriage. God is a God of order. Think of how God desires the children to honor the parents and the parents to not provoke their children to anger; it’s no different in the husband-and-wife relationship. The husband is to love his wife as Christ loves the church, and the wife is to reverence her husband.

In the beginning, God created male and female. He created Adam and said that it was not good for man to be alone; then He created woman from the rib of Adam’s side. God’s heart in the beginning was that man and woman would be one, and together they would walk with God and glorify Him. Then through Adam and Eve yielding to temptation, sin was brought into the world. Whenever we are struggling in our marriage, I am reminded how it was Eve that first yielded to the serpent’s temptation. Let us as wives be quick to examine our own hearts to be sure that we are in our place. When situations arise, how often are we as women tempted to think that we know better and could handle the situation better than our husbands.

God has designed our husbands to be our protector if we stay under them. I realize that we are imperfect, and that makes it more challenging to submit to our husbands. However, I believe that when we are born again by the Spirit of God, His love in us enables us to submit to our husbands. I also realize that there are a lot of broken homes. My encouragement to anyone who is in a less than ideal situation is to sincerely pray…first for yourself that you can walk in a blameless way and also for your husband that he would be what God has designed him to be—not what you think he should be. Many times, we get confused about this and it causes us to have bad thoughts about our husbands.

Titus gives us sisters clear direction from God. The aged women likewise, that they be … teachers of good things; That they may teach the young women to be sober, to love their husbands, to love their children, To be discreet, chaste, keepers at home, good, obedient to their own husbands, that the word of God be not blasphemed –Titus 2:3-5.

Another temptation that we women face is to compare our husbands with other men. Perhaps we tell our husbands that this other man wouldn’t do such and such the way you do, or the way he does something is better than the way you do. Maybe we don’t even say these words, but our actions can tell our husbands a lot. God’s Word teaches us to be obedient to our own husbands, and not another. Each husband is gifted in a different way, and that is why each wife is especially suited for their husband. And the LORD God said, It is not good that the man should be alone; I will make him an help [helper, aid, supporter] meet [suitable, appropriate, complementary] for him –Genesis 2:18.

That they may teach the young women to be sober, to love their husbands, to love their children –Titus 2:4. The word “love,” in to love their husbands means “to be affectionately fond of their man” as compared to the word “love” in to love their children which means “to have a maternal fondness for one’s children”. What kind of love are we showing our husbands? Can our husbands trust us that we only have their good in mind, or do we pretend to love in order to get something in return? True love will forgive in spite of failures, even when we think the pain is too great to bear. True love will cause us to pray for ourselves and our husbands when we feel differently about something than they do. True love will not cause us to despair, rather it will cause us to seek God even more.

When we are tempted to speak about our husbands’ faults to others, let us not yield to that temptation but let’s pray for them. Would we appreciate our husbands talking about our faults to other people? Also, pray for discernment to know if, and when, to speak to someone about a sin that your husband may be involved in. Let us not rail on or nag our husbands when difficulties arise. Instead, let us ask God to work in our lives and give the problem to Him and let it there. Our husbands are only too human, just as we are. If we fail at times, then we must not be surprised that they too might fail at times as well. I think what makes our marriages perfect is that we learn to forgive one another and press on to be one together.

Likewise, ye wives, be in subjection to your own husbands; that, if any obey not the word, they also may without the word be won by the conversation [conduct] of the wives; While they behold your chaste [modest, innocent, perfect, pure] conversation coupled with fear. Even as Sara obeyed Abraham, calling him lord: whose daughters ye are, as long as ye do well, and are not afraid with any amazement [terror]. Likewise, ye husbands, dwell with them according to knowledge, giving honour unto the wife, as unto the weaker vessel, and as being heirs together of the grace of life; that your prayers be not hindered –1 Peter 3:1-2 & 3:6-7.

One of the first times that this verse became real to us was when our first child was around five months old. We were quite a ways from home and he started crying with a lot of pain. We prayed for him, but he still cried. We could not figure out what was wrong, so we took him into the ER. They told us that he had an ear infection and gave us medication. However, he still cried. We had a ten-hour journey home, and he cried the whole way. After we had gotten home, my husband and I discovered that there were some unresolved things between us. After we confessed our wrongs to each other and to God, we prayed again for our son. Immediately after we prayed, our son quit crying. I know not every situation turns out like this one did, but God taught us that we need to be open with each other with no hidden sin, that our prayers be not hindered.

Some questions that could be asked are: What are our children seeing in our homes? Do they see Mom reverencing their dad with joy or with fear? Do they see Mom being appropriately affectionate with her husband, such as through kind words, seeking to love the things that he loves, holding hands, etc. (I have come to realize that it is difficult to hold hands with my husband if there is something between us.) Does Mom question, challenge, or criticize what Dad does?

As our own children are growing older and into their youth years, I see how important it is that these principles are lived out in our homes. If we openly question our husband’s authority, I believe we are sowing a seed in our children that they too will question their dad’s authority. Ultimately, in the time that we live, we are seeing a generation that is questioning everything about God’s created order—there is gender confusion, evolution, and rebellion against authority in general. I have often wondered if perhaps the reason that we see so much rebellion in our plain churches is because of God’s order not being lived out in our homes.

There was a friend of ours who told us that if there would be one Christian principle that he thought would have the most impact on the home, it would be the principle of the headship order. We have a dear friend who had become a Christian before her husband. She went through a lot of difficult times, but she continued to love and reverence her husband. She fasted and prayed for many years for her husband. Today her husband will testify that it was because of his wife’s godly conduct that drew him to repentance and faith in Christ.

Another example with a different outcome… I know of a couple that didn’t have a solid marriage. The husband was not in his place and the wife became bitter, so bitter in fact, that she said that when she is buried in the grave, she doesn’t want to be buried beside her husband. This much bitterness has had a terrible effect on their children. I wondered if she had not become bitter, if she could have at least spared her children from the many heartaches that they have suffered.

I also know of another couple where both of them were badly mistreated by close family, but they chose not to become bitter. They drew closer to God and to each other through those valleys and they are reaping the benefits of the fruit of their choices to this day.

Even closer to home… I grew up in a home that was not a Christian home. Neither of my parents were born again. When they began to allow God to work in their hearts, I could see it. I would come home from gatherings and see my dad weeping as he was reading his Bible. Also, on one particular evening I came home and saw my parents sitting at the table and they were singing together. I will testify that this had a tremendous effect on my life. I could also see my own mother desiring to be in her place as God had designed her to be. When we pass from this life, what will our family say about us? Will they testify that the love of God reigned in our mortal bodies?

On a practical note, I thought I would write a few ways that we can show that we love our husbands in deed and not just in word.

  • Asking them for advice (not just going on what we think)
  • Fixing their favorite foods
  • Keeping the house orderly and neat
  • Being ready and willing to drop our plans to help our husbands with whatever they need
  • Meeting them at the door with a smile (no matter how bad of day we may have had)
  • Keeping the house quiet, even with little children, when he’s trying to rest or study
  • Teaching our children proper manners in relating to each other in the home
  • Teaching our children to love and respect their father, even if he isn’t always perfect

Another challenge I wish to give to each married sister is to think of something that you can tell your husband that you are blessed about with him, Try doing this every day for two weeks. It’s amazing what effect kindness can have on a marriage. Maybe to some this would seem like drudgery, but it’s not. I am amazed that as we get older, how much we think alike, even sometimes finishing each other’s sentences. I realize there is so much more that could have been written. I trust that God will continue to open His Word to us as we seek Him.

I was one who struggled majorly and for years with not knowing how to submit and yet wanting to. Following is my attempt to share what God has been teaching me.

One of the main reasons that many people struggle with “submission” is that they don’t really understand what God means with the subject—they don’t understand the reality of biblical submission. Usually, a person knows what they believe on a certain subject, so in their mind when they are being asked to “submit” on that point, they think they are being asked to compromise their personal belief—or sin against their conscience.

The answer is two-fold.

First, if two people agree on an issue, then there is no need for anyone to submit. Thus, to submit does not mean that the person submitting is necessarily changing their mind, rather they are choosing to support the other person’s decision based on the fact that God says that that person is the one He is holding responsible for the decisions of that party—whether it be a couple, the home, a school, a church, etc.

Second, God knew that whenever there would be more than one person discussing a decision that needs to be made, that it would always mean that the one would end up submitting to the other. Therefore, to provide clarity in responsibility, He gives clear direction regarding whom He considers the responsible person (the spiritual authority) in each type of situation—the husband in a marriage, the father in the family, the man (the head) in the home, the ordained leaders in the church, the schoolteachers/principal in the school setting, etc. That way everyone can know who God sees as responsible for any mistakes that are made.

Consider that even though Eve took the fruit and ate it first, and then gave it to her husband to eat, God provides us with clarity regarding who He holds responsible for that failure (sin). Wherefore, as by one man [not one woman] sin entered into the world, and death by sin; and so death passed upon all men, for that all have sinned … Nevertheless death reigned from Adam [not from Eve] to Moses, even over them [Adam’s descendants—all of the human race] that had not sinned after the similitude of Adam’s transgression… –Romans 5:12-14.

So, we see that God provides protection and security to all those who are under authority if they stay under that authority. The one who God clearly states as being the authority figure in each relationship will always be the one that God holds responsible for decisions made by that group of people. Just like in the fall in the Garden of Eden, sins of omission and of commission within each family will be primarily held to dad’s account. Whether dad was giving wrong direction to the family or if he was not giving direction at all, it doesn’t matter, he will still be held to account since God sees the man as being the head of his home. (see 1 Corinthians 11:3 and Romans 13:12)

In de afgelopen jaren is er iets waar God in mijn hart aan gewerkt heeft: het gebied van onderdanigheid. Ik wil niet op een verkeerde manier terugkijken, maar ik zie waar ik mijn man tekortgedaan heb in de rol die God mij gegeven heeft om te functioneren als zijn helper, een die geschikt is voor hem. Terwijl ik nadacht over mijn eigen leven, realiseerde ik me hoe belangrijk onze rol is als christelijke vrouwen, in onze huizen en in het leven van onze kinderen.

Ik besef dat onze kinderen hun eigen beslissing zullen moeten nemen als het gaat om het discipelschap van Christus, maar mijn verlangen is dat ik niet de reden ben dat onze kinderen tegen het Woord van God in opstand komen. Wanneer wij onze mannen eren zoals God dat in Zijn Woord heeft geleerd, zal het voorbeeld van ons leven de ongelovigen tot Christus aantrekken. In het vlees zullen we onze mannen niet kunnen eren op een manier die God verheerlijkt, maar met Christus kunnen we alle dingen doen naar Zijn wil.

Ik draag hier een last over omdat ik de afgelopen maanden heb opgemerkt hoeveel onze huizen voortdurend onder aanval staan van de vijand van onze zielen, terwijl hij probeert ons vlees en de wereld te gebruiken. Terwijl ik hierover schrijf, heb ik niet het gevoel dat ik er recht aan doe, dus zal ik slechts enkele van mijn gedachten opschrijven en bidden dat allen die dit artikel lezen worden aangemoedigd in hun huwelijken om hun mannen te eren, te respecteren en lief te hebben.

  • Doch laat de vrouw zien dat zij vresing voor haar man heeft –Efeziërs 5:33.
  • Tevens, gij vrouwen, weest uw eigen mannen onderdanig… –1 Petrus 3:1.
  • Zoals Sara gehoorzaamde aan Abraham, haar heer noemend: wie dochters gij zijt… –1 Petrus 3:6.
  • Vrouwen, onderwerpt u aan uw eigen mannen, als aan de Heere –Efeziërs 5:22.
  • Ik wil u echter laten weten, dat het hoofd van iedere man Christus is; en het hoofd van de vrouw is de man; en het hoofd van Christus is God –1 Korinthiërs 11:3.
  • Laat de vrouw in stilte met alle onderdanigheid leren. Maar ik sta niet toe dat een vrouw onderwijst, noch gezag voert over de man, maar zij moet in stilte zijn. Want eerst werd Adam gevormd, daarna Eva. En Adam werd niet misleid, maar de vrouw, die misleid was, is in overtreding –1 Timoteüs 2:11-14.
  • Als dus de gemeente aan Christus onderdanig is, laat dan ook de vrouwen zich aan hun eigen mannen in alles onderwerpen –Efeziërs 5:24.
  • Laat uw vrouwen zwijgen in de gemeenten: want het is hun niet geoorloofd te spreken; maar zij worden onderdanigheid bevolen, zoals ook de wet zegt –1 Korinthiërs 14:34.

Deze Schriften zijn niet van mij, maar van God. Hij geeft ons Zijn Woord om te lezen en naar te leven omdat dat de enige manier is waarop we vrede en harmonie in onze huizen zullen kunnen hebben. Nog belangrijker: de ENIGE manier waarop we een rein geweten voor God kunnen hebben, is wanneer we in het midden van Zijn wil zijn.

Als we aan onderdanigheid denken, wat komt dan bij ons op? Denken we dat als we ons onderwerpen, we misbruikt zullen worden? Denken we dat we wijzer zijn dan onze mannen? Voor het vlees klinkt dit misschien hard, maar als we ons realiseren dat als we onze mannen niet toestaan te leiden en beslissingen te nemen, we hen slechts verlammen. De realiteit is dat als onze mannen fouten maken, dat oké is omdat wijzelf ook fouten maken. Bovendien, als we opnieuw geboren zijn en met God wandelen, maar onze mannen niet, zal God toch voor ons zorgen. De Schriften leren dat als onze man niet in zijn plaats is, door de vrouw die wandelt volgens de duidelijke leer die God haar in Zijn Woord gegeven heeft, de man gewonnen kan worden door haar gesprek (of door de wijze waarop zij haar leven leidt).

We moeten God toevertrouwen ons hele leven, ook op het gebied van ons huwelijk. God is een God van orde. Denk aan hoe God verlangt dat kinderen de ouders eren en dat ouders hun kinderen niet tot toorn prikkelen; het is niet anders in de relatie tussen man en vrouw. De man moet zijn vrouw liefhebben zoals Christus de gemeente liefheeft, en de vrouw moet haar man vrezen.

In het begin schiep God de man en de vrouw. Hij maakte Adam en zei dat het niet goed was dat de mens alleen bleef; toen schiep Hij de vrouw uit de rib van Adams zijde. Gods hart was in het begin dat man en vrouw één zouden zijn, en samen met God zouden wandelen en Hem verheerlijken. Toen gaven Adam en Eva door toe te geven aan verzoeking, toe aan zonde, en kwam zonde in de wereld. Wanneer wij worstelen in ons huwelijk, word ik eraan herinnerd dat het Eva was die als eerste aan de slang bezweek. Laten wij als vrouwen spoedig ons eigen hart onderzoeken om zeker te zijn dat wij in onze plaats zijn. Wanneer situaties zich voordoen, hoe vaak worden wij als vrouwen in verleiding gebracht te denken dat wij het beter weten en de situatie beter kunnen afhandelen dan onze mannen.

God heeft onze mannen ontworpen om onze beschermer te zijn als we onder hen blijven. Ik realiseer me dat we onvolmaakt zijn, en dat maakt het uitdagender ons aan onze mannen te onderwerpen. Echter, ik geloof dat wanneer we opnieuw geboren zijn door de Geest van God, Zijn liefde in ons ons in staat stelt ons aan onze mannen te onderwerpen. Ik besef ook dat er veel gebroken huizen zijn. Mijn bemoediging aan ieder die in een minder dan ideale situatie verkeert is oprecht te bidden… allereerst voor jezelf dat je onberispelijk kunt wandelen en ook voor je man dat hij zal zijn wat God hem heeft ontworpen om te zijn—niet wat jij denkt dat hij zou moeten zijn. Vaak raken we hierover in verwarring en het veroorzaakt dat we slechte gedachten over onze mannen hebben.

Titus geeft ons zusters duidelijke richting van God. De ouder vrouwen evenzo, dat zij in het leven staan, als moeders; Zij moeten de jonge vrouwen bijbrengen zich sober te gedragen, hun mannen lief te hebben, hun kinderen lief te hebben, discreet, kuis, huishoudelijk, goed, gehoorzaam aan hun eigen mannen, opdat het Woord van God niet lasterlijk gesproken wordt –Titus 2:3-5.

Een andere verleiding waar wij vrouwen mee te maken krijgen, is onze mannen vergelijken met andere mannen. Misschien vertellen we onze mannen dat die andere man niet zo iets zou doen zoals jij het doet, of dat de manier waarop hij iets doet beter is dan de jouwe. Misschien zeggen we deze woorden niet eens, maar onze daden kunnen onze mannen veel vertellen. Gods Woord leert ons gehoorzaam te zijn aan onze eigen mannen, en niet aan een ander. Iedere man is op een andere manier begiftigd, en daarom is iedere vrouw bijzonder geschikt voor haar man. En de HERE God zeide: Het is niet goed dat de mens alleen zij; Ik zal hem een hulp maken die bij hem past –Genesis 2:18.

Dat zij de jonge vrouwen leren sober te zijn, hun mannen lief te hebben, hun kinderen lief te hebben –Titus 2:4. Het woord “liefhebben” in hun mannen lief te hebben betekent “teder en innig gesteld zijn op haar man” in vergelijking met het woord “liefhebben” in hun kinderen lief te hebben dat betekent “een moederlijke genegenheid hebben voor haar kinderen”. Wat voor soort liefde tonen wij onze mannen? Kunnen onze mannen ons vertrouwen dat we alleen hun welzijn voor ogen hebben, of doen we alsof we liefhebben om iets ervoor terug te krijgen? Ware liefde zal vergeven ondanks falen, zelfs wanneer we denken dat de pijn te groot is om te verdragen. Ware liefde zal ons ertoe brengen voor onszelf en onze mannen te bidden wanneer we anders over iets voelen dan zij. Ware liefde zal ons niet doen wanhoopig worden, maar zal ons ertoe brengen God nog meer te zoeken.

Wanneer we in verleiding komen om over de fouten van onze mannen met anderen te spreken, laten we dan niet aan die verleiding toegeven maar voor hen bidden. Woulden we het op prijs stellen als onze mannen over onze fouten met andere mensen spraken? Bid ook om onderscheidingsvermogen om te weten of, en wanneer, je met iemand moet spreken over een zonde waarin je man mogelijk betrokken is. Laten we onze mannen niet terechtwijzen of pesten wanneer moeilijkheden zich voordoen. In plaats daarvan laten we God vragen in ons leven te werken en het probleem aan Hem over te laten en het daar te laten. Onze mannen zijn even menselijk als wij. Als wij soms falen, dan mogen we niet verbaasd zijn dat zij ook soms falen. Ik denk dat wat onze huwelijken volmaakt maakt, is dat we leren elkaar te vergeven en verder te streven om samen één te zijn.

Tevens, gij vrouwen, zijt uw eigen mannen onderdanig; opdat, indien sommigen het Woord niet gehoorzamen, zij zonder het Woord gewonnen worden door de wijze van leven der vrouwen; terwijl zij uw kuise wandel zien met vrees. Zoals Sara gehoorzaamde aan Abraham, haar heer noemend: wie dochters gij zijt, als gij het goede doet en u niet laat vrezelen; Gij mannen, handelt wederszijds wijs met uw vrouwen en geeft hen eer als het zwakkere vat, als mede erfgenamen der genade des levens; opdat uw gebeden niet belemmerd worden –1 Petrus 3:1-2 & 3:6-7.

Eén van de eerste keren dat dit vers voor ons werkelijkheid werd, was toen ons eerste kind ongeveer vijf maanden oud was. We waren een heel eind van huis en hij begon intens te huilen van pijn. We baden voor hem, maar hij huilde nog steeds. We konden niet uitvinden wat er kwaad was, dus brachten we hem naar de Spoedeisende Hulp. Ze zeiden dat hij een oorontsteking had en gaven ons medicijnen. Toch huilde hij nog. We hadden een reis van tien uur naar huis, en hij huilde de hele weg. Nadat we thuis waren gekomen, ontdekten mijn man en ik dat er onopgeloste dingen tussen ons waren. Nadat we onze fouten aan elkaar en aan God hadden bekend, baden we opnieuw voor onze zoon. Meteen nadat we gebeden hadden, stopte onze zoon met huilen. Ik weet dat niet iedere situatie zo afloopt, maar God leerde ons dat we open met elkaar moeten zijn zonder verborgen zonde, zodat onze gebeden niet belemmerd worden.

Enkele vragen die gesteld kunnen worden zijn: Wat zien onze kinderen in onze huizen? Zien zij dat mama hun vader vreest met vreugde of met angst? Zien zij dat mama passend teder is met haar man, zoals door vriendelijke woorden, het zoeken om van de dingen te houden die hij liefheeft, hand in hand lopen, enz. (Ik heb gemerkt dat het moeilijk is om hand in hand met mijn man te lopen als er iets tussen ons staat.) Betwijfelt, daagt of bekritiseert mama wat papa doet?

Terwijl onze eigen kinderen ouder worden en de tienerjaren ingaan, zie ik hoe belangrijk het is dat deze principes in onze huizen worden beleefd. Als wij openlijk de autoriteit van onze man betwijfelen, geloof ik dat we een zaad zaaien in onze kinderen dat zij ook de autoriteit van hun vader zullen betwijfelen. Uiteindelijk, in de tijd waarin wij leven, zien we een generatie die alles betwijfelt van Gods geschapen orde—er is genderverwarring, evolutie en rebellie tegen gezag in het algemeen. Ik heb me vaak afgevraagd of misschien de reden dat we zoveel rebellie zien in onze gewone kerken is omdat Gods orde niet in onze huizen wordt geleefd.

Er was een vriend van ons die zei dat als er één christelijk principe zou zijn dat naar zijn mening de grootste impact op het huis zou hebben, het het principe van hoofdschap zou zijn. We hebben een dierbare vriendin die christen werd voordat haar man dat werd. Ze ging door veel moeilijke tijden, maar bleef haar man liefhebben en vrezen. Ze vastte en bad jarenlang voor haar man. Vandaag zal haar man getuigen dat het vanwege de vrome levenswandel van zijn vrouw was dat hij tot bekering en geloof in Christus werd geleid.

Een ander voorbeeld met een ander resultaat… ik ken een paar dat geen solide huwelijk had. De man was niet in zijn plaats en de vrouw werd bitter, zo bitter zelfs dat ze zei dat toen ze begraven zou worden, ze niet naast haar man begraven wilde worden. Deze bittere houding heeft een verschrikkelijk effect op hun kinderen gehad. Ik vroeg me af of zij niet bitter was geworden, of zij haar kinderen ten minste gespaard zou hebben van de vele hartzeer die zij geleden hebben.

Ik ken ook nog een ander paar waar beiden zwaar mishandeld werden door naaste familie, maar zij kozen ervoor niet bitter te worden. Ze trokken dichter tot God en tot elkaar door die dalen en zij oogsten tot op de dag van vandaag de vruchten van de keuzes die ze gemaakt hebben.

Nog dichter bij huis… ik groeide op in een huis dat geen christelijk huis was. Geen van mijn ouders was wedergeboren. Toen zij God begonnen toe te laten in hun hart, kon ik het zien. Ik kwam thuis van bijeenkomsten en zag mijn vader huilen terwijl hij zijn Bijbel las. Ook, op één avond kwam ik thuis en zag mijn ouders samen aan tafel zitten en zingen. Ik zal getuigen dat dit een enorme invloed op mijn leven had. Ik zag ook mijn eigen moeder verlangen haar plaats in te nemen zoals God haar had ontworpen. Als wij deze aarde verlaten, wat zal ons gezin over ons zeggen? Zullen zij getuigen dat de liefde van God heerste in onze sterfelijke lichamen?

Op een praktisch vlak dacht ik een paar manieren te noteren waarop we kunnen tonen dat we onze mannen liefhebben in daden en niet alleen in woorden.

  • Ze om advies vragen (niet alleen doen wat we zelf denken)
  • Hun favoriete gerechten klaarmaken
  • Het huis ordelijk en netjes houden
  • Bereid zijn en willen onze plannen opzij te zetten om onze mannen te helpen met wat ze nodig hebben
  • Ze bij de deur opvangen met een glimlach (ongeacht hoe slechte dag we gehad mogen hebben)
  • Het huis rustig houden, zelfs met kleine kinderen, wanneer hij rust of wil studeren
  • Onze kinderen juiste manieren leren in hun omgang met elkaar thuis
  • Onze kinderen leren hun vader lief te hebben en te respecteren, zelfs als hij niet altijd perfect is

Een andere uitdaging die ik elke getrouwde zuster wil geven is om iets te bedenken dat je je man kunt vertellen waarover je je door hem gezegend voelt. Probeer dit elke dag twee weken te doen. Het is verbazingwekkend welke uitwerking vriendelijkheid op een huwelijk kan hebben. Misschien lijkt dit voor sommigen als sleur, maar dat is het niet. Ik verwonder me erover dat naarmate we ouder worden, we zoveel hetzelfde denken, soms zelfs elkaars zinnen afmaken. Ik realiseer me dat er nog zoveel meer opgeschreven had kunnen worden. Ik vertrouw erop dat God Zijn Woord ons blijft openen terwijl wij Hem zoeken.

Editor’s Note:

Ik was iemand die jarenlang en in sterke mate worstelde met niet weten hoe zich te onderwerpen en toch dat te willen. Hieronder is mijn poging te delen wat God mij heeft geleerd.

Een van de belangrijkste redenen dat velen worstelen met “onderdanigheid” is dat zij niet echt begrijpen wat God met dat onderwerp bedoelt—zij begrijpen de realiteit van Bijbelse onderdanigheid niet. Meestal weet een persoon wat hij gelooft over een bepaald onderwerp, dus in zijn hoofd wanneer hem gevraagd wordt zich op dat punt te “onderwerpen”, denkt hij dat hem gevraagd wordt zijn persoonlijke overtuiging te compromitteren—of tegen zijn geweten te zondigen.

Het antwoord is tweevoudig.

Ten eerste, als twee mensen het eens zijn over een kwestie, dan is er voor niemand de noodzaak zich te onderwerpen. Dus zich onderwerpen betekent niet noodzakelijk dat de persoon die zich onderwerpt van gedachten verandert; eerder kiest hij ervoor de beslissing van de ander te ondersteunen op basis van het feit dat God zegt dat die persoon degene is die Hij verantwoordelijk houdt voor de beslissingen van die partij—of het nu een koppel, het huis, een school, een kerk, enz. betreft.

Ten tweede, God wist dat wanneer er meer dan één persoon zou zijn die een beslissing moest bespreken, dat het altijd zou betekenen dat de één zich uiteindelijk aan de ander zou onderwerpen. Daarom, om duidelijkheid in verantwoordelijkheid te verschaffen, geeft Hij duidelijke richting betreffende wie Hij als de verantwoordelijke persoon (de geestelijke autoriteit) in elk type situatie beschouwt—de man in een huwelijk, de vader in het gezin, de man (het hoofd) in het huis, de gelegitimeerde leiders in de kerk, de leraren/directeur in de schoolomgeving, enz. Op die manier kan iedereen weten wie God ziet als verantwoordelijk voor eventuele fouten die gemaakt worden.

Overweeg dat hoewel Eva eerst de vrucht nam en at, en daarna haar man gaf om te eten, God ons duidelijkheid geeft over wie Hij verantwoordelijk houdt voor die mislukking (zonde). Daarom, zoals door één mens [niet één vrouw] de zonde in de wereld inging, en door de zonde de dood; en aldus werd de dood over allen, omdat allen gezondigd hebben … Niettemin heerst de dood van Adam [niet van Eva] tot Mozes, zelfs over hen [Adams nakomelingen—de ganse mensheid] die niet gezondigd hadden naar de gelijkenis van Adams overtreding… –Romeinen 5:12-14.

Dus zien we dat God bescherming en zekerheid biedt aan allen die onder gezag staan, als zij onder dat gezag blijven. Degene die God duidelijk stelt als de autoriteitsfiguur in elke relatie zal altijd degene zijn die God verantwoordelijk houdt voor beslissingen gemaakt door die groep mensen. Net als in de val in de Hof van Eden zullen zonden door nalatigheid en daad binnen elk gezin primair aan de vader toegerekend worden. Of vader nu verkeerde leiding gaf aan het gezin of helemaal geen richting gaf, het maakt niet uit, hij zal toch ter verantwoording geroepen worden aangezien God de man ziet als het hoofd van zijn huis. (zie 1 Korinthiërs 11:3 en Romeinen 13:12)

And Peter answered him and said, Lord, if it be thou, bid me come unto thee on the water. And he said, Come. And when Peter was come down out of the ship, he walked on the water, to go to Jesus –Matthew 14:28-29.

Men who follow Jesus are men of faith. Discipleship is not for cowards or the faint of heart, nor is it for those who demand a rationale for acts of obedience. The disciples had spent the day with Jesus. After the feeding of the five thousand Matthew writes that …straightway Jesus constrained his disciples to get into a ship, and to go before him unto the other side, while he sent the multitudes away –Matthew 14:22.

If there was anything that the disciples were familiar with and skilled in, it was sailing the waters of Galilee. This was their territory. Peter and John had fished these waters with their father from their earliest remembrance. But tonight, they were making little headway… the wind was contrary.

And in the fourth watch of the night Jesus went unto them, walking on the sea. And when the disciples saw him walking on the sea, they were troubled, saying, It is a spirit; and they cried out for fear. But straightway Jesus spake unto them, saying, Be of good cheer; it is I; be not afraid –Matthew 14:25-27.

Peter then made this bold appeal …Lord, if it be thou, bid me come unto thee on the water –Matthew 14:28. What was Peter thinking? He had never walked on water. Jesus was not asking him to walk on water. It was not logical. It defied the laws of nature… yet when Jesus said “come”. Peter stepped out of the boat and walked on the water to go to Jesus. That’s right! He was treading on water.

Peter was responding to a clear call from Jesus. Jesus said “come”. It is important that we understand that faith is our response to the clear call of God on our lives. Too often in our ambition to be useful we choose our path and call our ambition “faith” when God may not be in it at all.

If you want to be a man of faith, open your Bible and pray. Ask God to reveal His plan for your life. The Bible contains many commandments that can provide practical direction for our lives. Take God at His Word. Step out in faith and obedience then you will experience the miracle of God’s power in your life.

Peter’s boat was his security. He and his boat had a long relationship. It had served him well for many years. Peter felt right at home in his old bark, although tonight she did not seem to respond well to his masterful seamanship. He had drawn many a draught of fish over her gunwales. Now as he stands on her deck watching Jesus approach, “walking on the water”, he was overcome with a desire to go to Jesus. In reckless abandonment he stepped off her deck …and a miracle happened.

A walk of faith often calls us away from that which is familiar and secure. If we make safety and security our priority—if we limit our actions to carefully calculated risks (limited to that which we can manage and control)—we limit the power of God working in and through us.

Our forefathers in Europe knew that if they embraced the journey of unreserved discipleship, it could be costly. They risked the seizure of their property; many of them lost all that they owned. Since they willingly faced imprisonment and death, we refer to them as heroes of the faith. These were men who were willing to abandon all for the sake of the gospel. Because of their faith we receive the benefits of a godly heritage.

I commend our younger generation of Anabaptist youth for their willingness to make following Jesus a priority. In the past our priority has been to build our security base, be it our farm or business, and then consider mission work as a possibility. That was never Jesus’ model for service. When Jesus sent out his disciples he said. And he said unto them, Take nothing for your journey, neither staves, nor scrip, neither bread, neither money; neither have two coats apiece –Luke 9:3.

Later, after they had returned, Jesus asked them, And he said unto them, When I sent you without purse, and scrip, and shoes, lacked ye any thing? And they said, Nothing –Luke 22:35.

You do not need to go into foreign missions to experience the power of God released in your life. Every act of radical obedience is an act of faith. There are men in our Anabaptist communities who are experiencing moral defeat. If we are going to succumb to a victim mentality (“I can’t help it”), and define moral failure as an addiction, we set ourselves up for ongoing defeat. Men of faith are men of action who take measurable steps of obedience which will lead them to ultimate victory. Moral failure begins with small compromises that end in crushing defeat.

Peter’s actions were not logical. If Peter would have processed his decision using the scientific method, he would not have taken such a risk. Many of the simple commands of Christ have no apparent scientific reasoning. From baptism, to communion, to foot washing, to anointing with oil, these are all acts of faith. The significance and the power of each lies in the doing of it with a heart of obedient faith, not in the thing itself.

So it is with many aspects of the Christian experience. We can analyze a thing endlessly, ultimately resulting in its demise. This happens in many churches. We reason away the woman’s head covering. We reason away the nonconformed lifestyle. We reason away the permanence of marriage. We reason away brotherhood accountability. What we have left has no resemblance to the simple teachings of Jesus. Discipleship calls us to faithful obedience. Jesus and the apostles taught it, so we do it. The blessing and the power lie in the doing of it.

That is what Peter discovered. He walked on water! He did not dip a toe to test the water first. I like to think he leaped from the boat and hit the water with both feet. That would be faith and Peter had faith.

But when he saw the wind boisterous, he was afraid; and beginning to sink, he cried, saying, Lord, save me. And immediately Jesus stretched forth his hand, and caught him, and said unto him, O thou of little faith, wherefore didst thou doubt? And when they were come into the ship, the wind ceased –Matthew 14:30-32.

Peter had faith to walk on water until he began to look around and began to process his situation using the scientific method. This is not to invalidate the scientific method. The scientific method proves the order of creation and the evidence of a creator.

In Hebrews 11 we read that …faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen –Hebrews 11:1.

It is our faith that is the substance and our faith that is the evidence of spiritual realities. Just as the scientific method proves the realities of the created world, so our faith proves spiritual realities.

Boisterous wind and crashing waves produced a fearful, sinking Peter. We sometimes criticize Peter for taking his eyes off of Jesus and sinking into the waves; however, Peter walked on water, I know of no one else who walked on water. When we transition from obedient faith to carnal rationalization, we lose power with God.

Are we suggesting that faith is irrational? No, not at all. As a matter of fact, the first act of faith is to believe that Jesus is the logos. John wrote, In the beginning was the Word [Logos], and the Word [Logos], was with God, and the Word [Logos], was God –John 1:1. It is from the Greek word Logos that we get our English word logic.

Just as there are laws in nature that make the scientific method durable and replicable, so there are spiritual laws that give order and cohesion to our inner man. Jesus is the embodiment of these truths. His teachings are the revelation of these truths and through his death and resurrection these truths have become accessible to all. Jesus promised, Howbeit when he, the Spirit of truth, is come, he will guide you into all truth… –John 16:13.

Men of faith are men who have eyes to see these spiritual realities. Their vision is not limited to the natural world. They understand that there are spiritual realities that have “cause and effect” in our lives that are every bit as powerful as the “cause and effect” that we see about us in the natural world every day.

These realities are only visible to men of faith. Paul wrote, But the natural man receiveth not the things of the Spirit of God: for they are foolishness unto him: neither can he know them, because they are spiritually discerned –1 Corinthians 2:14. Men of faith, are men whose lives are governed by spiritual realities that are incomprehensible to the natural man. If you will be a man of faith, expect to be misunderstood. You are embarking on a journey that will run counter to the world view of many.

As Peter began to sink into the waves he cried out, “Lord, save me”. His plaintive cry revealed an absolute trust in his Lord. Jesus reached out His hand and rescued him. Jesus next words continue to challenge us. He said to Peter, …O thou of little faith, wherefore didst thou doubt? Matthew 14:31. Peter had just walked on water—a feat no man had accomplished before or since, yet Jesus called it “little faith” and asked, “why did you doubt?”.

Jesus said at another time, …If ye have faith as a grain of mustard seed, ye shall say unto this mountain, Remove hence to yonder place; and it shall remove; and nothing shall be impossible unto you –Matthew 17:20.

If Peter’s “little faith” empowered him to walk on water, and if faith as tiny as a grain of mustard seed can remove mountains what does that say of your and my faith?

Perhaps it is evidence that our faith is littler than Peter’s “little faith” and tinier than the tiny grain of mustard seed?! It is also evidence that God honors little faith. What he does not honor is no faith. According to your faith be it unto you. Little faith…walk on water! No faith…sink beneath the waves!

Since Jesus is the “Logos”, He is the master of the natural world and the spirit world. He proved himself to be the Master of the wind and the waves—and when they were come into the ship, the wind ceased –Matthew 14:32. And He proved Himself to be the Master of the spirit world—then they that were in the ship came and worshipped him, saying, Of a truth thou art the Son of God –Matthew 14:33.

We, in our western world, have become so satiated with materialism that we can easily be led to believe that natural realities are the most powerful realities. This materialism assaults us, not just with the abundance of material things, but also with a bombardment of humanistic philosophy. Humanistic philosophy is thinking that is devoid of spiritual reality… that is devoid of faith.

If you, as a man, find yourself sinking in waves of despair… be it financial struggles… be it relational difficulties… moral failure or maybe you find yourself being your own worst critic…may I challenge you to lift your eyes to the one who is Logos. Jesus is the one who is master of your circumstances and the one who would be Lord of your soul. To allow Jesus to be Lord of your soul is to live in faith obedience to the radical teachings of Jesus.

To live in harmony with the natural world we honor the laws of nature. When we are replacing a roof, we respect the law of gravity. When driving a vehicle, we slow down for turns out of respect for the law of inertia. Defy the natural laws and someone gets hurt.

To live in harmony with the spiritual world, we honor the law of Christ. We love our neighbor. We forgive our brother. We keep our marriage vows. We bear …one another’s burdens, and so fulfil the law of Christ –Galatians 6:2.

Men of faith are men who are attune to these spiritual realities and order their lives accordingly.
