וַיַּעַן פֶּטֶרוֹס וַיֹּאמֶר לוֹ, אָדוֹן אִם־אַתָּה אָמַר לִי לָבוֹא אֵלֶיךָ עַל־הַמָּיִם. וַיֹּאמֶר לוֹ, לֵךְ. וּבְרָדוֹתוֹ אֶל־הַסְּפִינָה הָלַךְ עַל־הַמָּיִם לָבֹא אֶל־יֵשׁוּעַ –Matthew 14:28-29.

אנשים ההולכים אחרי ישוע הם אנשים של אמונה. תלמידות אינה למפוחדים או ללב חלש, ולא היא לאלה שדורשים נימוק לכל מעשה של ציות. התלמידים בילו את היום עם ישוע. לאחר האכלת חמשת אלפים Matthew כותב ש…straightway Jesus constrained his disciples to get into a ship, and to go before him unto the other side, while he sent the multitudes away –Matthew 14:22.

אם היה משהו שהתלמידים הכירו ושהיו מיומנים בו, זה שיט על מי הגליל. זה היה תחומם. פטרוס ויוחנן דגו במים האלה עם אביהם מאז זכרונם המוקדם ביותר. אך הלילה הם עשו מעט התקדמות… הרוח הייתה נגדם.

And in the fourth watch of the night Jesus went unto them, walking on the sea. And when the disciples saw him walking on the sea, they were troubled, saying, It is a spirit; and they cried out for fear. But straightway Jesus spake unto them, saying, Be of good cheer; it is I; be not afraid –Matthew 14:25-27.

אז פטרוס נקט בקריאה נועזת זו …Lord, if it be thou, bid me come unto thee on the water –Matthew 14:28. מה חשב פטרוס? הוא מעולם לא הלך על המים. ישוע לא בקש ממנו ללכת על המים. זה לא היה לוגי. זה הפר את חוקי הטבע… ועדיין כשישוע אמר "בוא" פטרוס יצא מהסירה והלך על המים כדי לבוא אל ישוע. נכון! הוא דרך על המים.

פטרוס הגיב לקריאה ברורה מישוע. ישוע אמר "בוא". חשוב שנבין שאמונה היא תגובתנו לקריאה הברורה של אלוהים על חיינו. לעתים קרובות מדי מתוך שאיפה להיות שימושיים אנו בוחרים את דרכנו וקוראים לשאיפה שלנו "אמונה" בעוד שאלוהים אולי כלל לא נמצא בזה.

אם אתה רוצה להיות איש אמונה, פתח את התנ"ך והתפלל. בקש מאלוהים לגלות את תוכניתו לחייך. התנ"ך מכיל מצוות רבות שיכולות להעניק כוון מעשי לחיינו. קבל את אלוהים במילתו. צא באמונה ובציות ואז תחווה את הנס של כוחו של אלוהים בחייך.

סירתו של פטרוס הייתה הביטחון שלו. הוא וסירתו היו בקשר ארוך. היא שירתה אותו שנים רבות. פטרוס הרגיש בבית בסירתו הישנה, אף שבלילה זה היא לא נראתה מגיבה היטב לאמנותו הימית. הוא העלה דג רבים על סיפונה. עכשיו כשהוא עומד על סיפונה וצופה בישוע מתקרב, "הולך על המים", נתפס בו תשוקה ללכת אל ישוע. בהתנפלות רשלנית הוא קפץ מסיפונה… ונס קרה.

הליכה של אמונה לעתים קוראת לנו להתרחק ממה שמוכר ובטוח. אם נציב ביטחון ובטיחות כעדיפותנו — אם נגביל את מעשינו לסיכונים מחושבים בקפידה (מוגבלים למה שאנו יכולים לנהל ולשלוט בו) — אנו מגבילים את כוחו של אלוהים הפועל בנו ובאמצעותנו.

אבותינו באירופה ידעו שאם ייקחו על עצמם את מסע התלמידות ללא הסתייגות, הדבר עלול להיות יקר. הם סיכנו את תפיסת רכושם; רבים מהם איבדו את כל אשר היה להם. מאחר שהתייצבו מרצונם בפני מאסר ומוות, אנו מתייחסים אליהם כאל גיבורי האמונה. אלה היו אנשים שהיו מוכנים לנטוש הכל למען הבשורה. בזכות אמונם אנו נהנים מיתרונות מורשת חסודה.

אני משבח את הדור הצעיר בקהילות האנאבפטיסטיות על נכונותם להפוך את ההליכה אחרי ישוע לעדיפות. בעבר עדיפותנו הייתה לבנות את בסיס הביטחון שלנו, בין אם החווה או העסק, ואז לשקול עבודה מיסיונרית כאפשרות. זו מעולם לא היתה דוגמת השירות של ישוע. כאשר ישוע שלח את תלמידיו הוא אמר. And he said unto them, Take nothing for your journey, neither staves, nor scrip, neither bread, neither money; neither have two coats apiece –Luke 9:3.

Later, after they had returned, Jesus asked them, And he said unto them, When I sent you without purse, and scrip, and shoes, lacked ye any thing? And they said, Nothing –Luke 22:35.

אין צורך לצאת למשימות זרות כדי לחוות את כוחו של אלוהים בחייך. כל מעשה של ציות מהפכני הוא מעשה של אמונה. ישנם אנשים בקהילות האנאבפטיסטיות שלנו החווים תבוסה מוסרית. אם נסגפנו למנטליות קורבן ("אני לא יכול לעזור בזה"), ונגדיר כישלון מוסרי כהתמכרות, אנו מציבים עצמנו לתבוסות מתמשכות. אנשי אמונה הם אנשים של מעשה, שלוקחים צעדים מדידים של ציות שיובילו אותם לניצחון סופי. כישלון מוסרי מתחיל בפשרות קטנות שמסתיימות בתבוסה קשה.

מעשיו של פטרוס לא היו לוגיים. אילו היה פטרוס מעבד את החלטתו בשיטת המדע, הוא לא היה נוקט בסיכון כזה. רבות מהמצוות הפשוטות של המשיח אין להן נימוק מדעי ברור. מן הטבילה, דרך הלחם והיין, שטיפת רגליים, משיחה בשמן — כל אלה מעשי אמונה. משמעותו וכוחו של כל אחד טמונים בעשייתו בלב של אמונה צייתנית, לא בדבר עצמו.

כך גם ברבים מההיבטים של החוויה הנוצרית. נוכל לנתח דבר ללא סוף, ובסופו של דבר להביא לחיסולו. זה קורה בהרבה כנסיות. אנו מבארים מדוע כיסוי ראש האישה מיותר. אנו מצמצמים לחיים לא מתמרדים. אנו מתירים את עמידות הנישואין. אנו משילים את אחריות האחוה. מה שנשאר לנו לא דומה ללימודיה הפשוטים של ישוע. תלמידות קוראת לנו לציות נאמן. ישוע והשליחים לימדו זאת, ולכן אנו עושים זאת. הברכה והכוח טמונים בעשייתו.

זה מה שגילה פטרוס. הוא הלך על המים! הוא לא הטביל אצבע כדי לבדוק את המים תחילה. אני אוהב לדמיין שהוא קפץ מהסירה ונחת על המים בשתי רגליו. זו אמונה ופטרוס היה בעל אמונה.

But when he saw the wind boisterous, he was afraid; and beginning to sink, he cried, saying, Lord, save me. And immediately Jesus stretched forth his hand, and caught him, and said unto him, O thou of little faith, wherefore didst thou doubt? And when they were come into the ship, the wind ceased –Matthew 14:30-32.

לפטורוס הייתה אמונה ללכת על המים עד שהחל להביט סביב והחל לעבד את מצבו בשיטת המדע. הדבר אינו כדי לפגוע בשיטת המדע. שיטת המדע מוכיחה את סדר הבריאה ואת העדות ליוצר.

במכתב אל העברים 11 אנו קוראים ש…faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen –Hebrews 11:1.

האמונה שלנו היא החומר והעדות של מציאויות רוחניות. כפי ששיטת המדע מוכיחה את מציאות עולמנו הבריאה, כך אמונתנו מוכיחה מציאויות רוחניות.

רוח סוערת וגלים שברו פטרוס; הוא הפך לפחדן ושוקע. לעתים אנו מבקרים את פטרוס על כך שהסיר את עיניו מישוע ושקע בגלים; עם זאת, פטרוס הלך על המים — לא ידוע לי על מישהו אחר שהלך על המים. כשאנו עוברים מאמונה צייתנית להסתכלות בשרית ורציונלית, אנו מאבדים כוח עם אלוהים.

האם אנו מציעים כי אמונה היא אי־רציונלית? לא, כלל לא. למעשה, המעשה הראשון של אמונה הוא להאמין שישוע הוא ה-lógos. יוחנן כתב, In the beginning was the Word [Logos], and the Word [Logos], was with God, and the Word [Logos], was God –John 1:1. מהמילה היוונית Logos אנו מקבלים את המילה האנגלית logic.

כפי שיש חוקים בטבע שהופכים את שיטת המדע לעמידה ושחוזרת על עצמה, כך יש חוקים רוחניים שמעניקים סדר וקוהזיה לאדם הפנימי שלנו. ישוע הוא ההתגלמות של האמיתות האלה. תורתו היא גילוי האמיתות האלה ובאמצעות מותו ותחייתו האמיתות האלה הופכות לנגישות לכל. ישוע הבטיח, Howbeit when he, the Spirit of truth, is come, he will guide you into all truth… –John 16:13.

אנשי אמונה הם אנשים שיש להם עיניים לראות את המציאויות הרוחניות האלה. הראייה שלהם אינה מוגבלת לעולם הטבעי. הם מבינים שיש מציאויות רוחניות שיש להן "סיבה ותוצאה" בחיינו שהן לא פחות עוצמתיות מה"סיבה והתוצאה" שאנו רואים בעולם הטבעי סביבנו כל יום.

מציאויות אלה נראות רק לאנשי אמונה. פאולוס כתב, But the natural man receiveth not the things of the Spirit of God: for they are foolishness unto him: neither can he know them, because they are spiritually discerned –1 Corinthians 2:14. אנשי אמונה הם אנשים שחייהם נשלטים על ידי מציאויות רוחניות שהן בלתי נתפסות לאדם הטבעי. אם תרצה להיות איש אמונה, צפה להיות מובן לא נכון. אתה מתחיל מסע שיינגש עם השקפת העולם של רבים.

כשהחל פטרוס לשקוע בגלים קרא: "אדון הושיעני". קריאתו המנוסה חשפה אמון מוחלט במושיעו. ישוע השטיל את ידו והציל אותו. המילים הבאות של ישוע ממשיכות לאתגר אותנו. הוא אמר לפטרוס, …O thou of little faith, wherefore didst thou doubt? Matthew 14:31. פטרוס זה עתה הלך על המים — מפעל שאיש לא עשה לפניו או אחרי — ועדיין ישוע כינה זאת "אמונה מעטה" ושאל, "למה ספקת?".

ישוע אמר עוד באירוע אחר, …If ye have faith as a grain of mustard seed, ye shall say unto this mountain, Remove hence to yonder place; and it shall remove; and nothing shall be impossible unto you –Matthew 17:20.

אם ה"אמונה הקטנה" של פטרוס העניקה לו ללכת על המים, ואם אמונה כגרגר חרדל יכולה להזיז הרים — מה הדבר אומר על אמונתך ועל אמונתי?

אולי זה עדות שהאמונה שלנו קטנה יותר מה"אמונה הקטנה" של פטרוס וזעירה יותר מהגרגר הקטן של חרדל?! זה גם עדות שאלוהים מכבד אמונה קטנה. מה שהוא לא מכבד הוא היעדר אמונה. על־פי אמונתך ייעשה לך. אמונה קטנה… לך על המים! אין אמונה… שקיעה תחת הגלים!

מכיוון שישוע הוא ה"Logos", הוא אדון על העולם הטבעי ועל העולם הרוחני. הוא הוכיח עצמו כאדון על הרוח והגלים — and when they were come into the ship, the wind ceased –Matthew 14:32. והוא הוכיח עצמו כאדון על העולם הרוחני — then they that were in the ship came and worshipped him, saying, Of a truth thou art the Son of God –Matthew 14:33.

אנחנו, בעולם המערבי שלנו, התמלאנו כל כך בחומרנות שאנו נוטים להאמין שקל לנו לראות את המציאויות הטבעיות כחזקות ביותר. חומרנות זו תוקפת אותנו לא רק בשפע החומרי, אלא גם במצור של פילוסופיה הומניסטית. פילוסופיה הומניסטית היא חשיבה חסרת מציאות רוחנית… חסרת אמונה.

אם אתה, כאיש, מוצא את עצמך שוקע בגלי ייאוש… בין אם במאבקים כלכליים… בין אם בקשיים ביחסים… כישלון מוסרי או שאולי אתה השופט החמור על עצמך… האם אוכל לאתגר אותך להרים את עיניך אל אותו שהוא הלוגוס. ישוע הוא זה ששולט בנסיבותיך וזה שיהיה אדון על נפשך. לאפשר לישוע להיות אדון על נפשך פירושו לחיות בציות אמוני ללימודיה הקיצוניים של ישוע.

לחיות בהרמוניה עם העולם הטבעי אנו מקיימים את חוקי הטבע. כשאנו מחליפים גג אנו מכבדים את חוק הכבידה. בנהיגה ברכב אנו מאטים בפניות מתוך כבוד לחוק ההתמדה. להפר את חוקי הטבע ומישהו נפגע.

לחיות בהרמוניה עם העולם הרוחני אנו מקיימים את חוק המשיח. אנו אוהבים את רעינו. אנו סולחים לאחינו. אנו מקיימים את שבועות הנישואין שלנו. אנו נושאים …one another’s burdens, and so fulfil the law of Christ –Galatians 6:2.

אנשי אמונה הם אנשים שמכווננים למציאויות רוחניות אלה ומסדרים את חייהם בהתאם.

This hymn is generally considered to be one of the greatest hymns ever written and is found in nearly every hymnal or book of hymns published today. It was written by a man who was frail in body, but strong in spirit. It was he who coined the phrase, “It is better to wear out than to rust out.” Let us now take a glimpse into the life of this servant of God.

Henry Francis Lyte, the author of this great and noteworthy hymn, was born June 1, 1793, in Ednam, near Kelso, Scotland. At a young age, he was left an orphan and was in comparative poverty. He was educated at Trinity College in Dublin, Ireland. It was there that his gift of poetry began to appear, winning him three prizes. His primary goal with his studies was to become a physician, instead, by the providence of God, he became a minister of the gospel of Jesus Christ.

One day in Cornwall, a fellow clergyman who was on his deathbed, requested that Lyte would come and give him some spiritual comfort. “To their mutual grief, they found themselves [both] groping for the light, veritable blind guides”. As they searched for truth and assurance of salvation, they fixed their faith on Christ, and Lyte came away from that sickroom a changed man, never to be the same again. It is said that it was his encounter with God at the bedside of that dying man that prompted Lyte’s noble hymn, “Jesus, I My Cross Have Taken.” In the year 1823, Henry F. Lyte took charge of a seashore parish, Lower Brixham, in Devonshire, England. It was at that place where he spent the last 23 years of his life toiling as a pastor for the spiritual good of the poor fishing people and the rough seafaring men of that region until his death in the fall of 1847. For all of Henry’s dedication and labor, he received a reward: having a Sunday school of several hundred scholars, as well as “a splendid company of seventy or eighty teachers, personally trained by him.”

Throughout his lifetime, his health was continually threatened by asthma and tuberculosis. Notwithstanding his physical frailties, he worked tirelessly with an established reputation as a poet, musician, and minister. Wherever he went, he was greatly loved and admired by his people. Toward the end of these later years, his health became gradually worse. So it was that during the winter months, he felt compelled to seek a warmer climate in Italy, which is a part of southern Europe.

Though he was greatly weakened by his sickness, on September 4, 1847, as Lyte was about to leave to head southward, he was arrested by an “irresistible desire” to preach once more to his congregation. He dearly loved these people and he had labored among them for so many years. “Against the protest of his amazed friends, he accomplished this purpose, and it is recorded that Lyte nearly had to crawl to the pulpit and his message came as from a dying man.” “O brethren,” he said, as he entered the familiar pulpit for the last time, “I stand here among you today, as alive from the dead, if I may hope to impress it upon you, and induce you to prepare for that solemn hour which must come to all, by a timely appreciation and dependance on the death of Christ.” These final words made a deep impact upon his congregation, after which he closed the service by administering the Lord’s Supper to his weeping people. Later that evening, after the service, he was inspired to “poetical composition” and wrote the eight stanzas of his last and greatest hymn:

Abide with me: fast falls the eventide;
The darkness deepens; Lord, with me abide:
when other helpers fail, and comforts flee,
Help of the helpless, O abide with me.

Swift to its close ebbs out life’s little day;
Earth’s joys grow dim, its glories pass away;
Change and decay in all around I see;
O Thou who changest not, abide with me.

Not a brief glance I beg, a passing word;
But, as Thou dwell’st with Thy disciples, Lord,
Familiar, condescending, patient, free,
Come, not to sojourn, but abide, with me.

Come not in terrors, as the King of kings;
But kind and good, with healing in Thy wings;
Tears for all woes, a heart for every plea;
Come, Friend of sinners, and thus ‘bide with me.

Thou on my head in early youth didst smile;
And, though rebellious and perverse meanwhile,
thou hast not left me, oft as I left thee:
On to the close, O Lord, abide with me.

I need Thy presence every passing hour;
What but Thy grace can foil the tempter’s power?
Who like Thyself my guide and stay can be?
Through cloud and sunshine, O abide with me.

I fear no foe, with Thee at hand to bless:
Ills have no weight, and tears no bitterness.
Where is death’s sting? Where, grave, thy victory?
I triumph still, if Thou abide with me.

Hold Thou Thy cross before my closing eyes;
Shine through the gloom, and point me to the skies;
Heaven’s morning breaks, and earth’s vain shadows flee:
In life, in death, O Lord, abide with me.

This hymn he gave to one of the family members that very night. Leaving the following day, he began his trek to Rome, Italy, hoping to gain some relief from his sickness. Lyte make it as far as Nice, France where his sickness prevented his further travel. He passed away soon after the age of 55, on November 20, 1847. His last words were “Joy! Peace!”

The scene behind this hymn is that of the resurrected Christ Jesus walking on the road to Emmaus with two of His somewhat sad and discouraged disciples. As they neared the end of their seven-mile walk and approached the village where they were going, Jesus …made as though he would have gone further. But they constrained him, saying, Abide with us: for it is toward evening, and the day is far spent. And he went in to tarry with them –Luke 24:28-29.

We can draw a parallel between that scene and Henry F. Lyte’s own experience of drawing toward the close of his earthly journey. Thus, as the disciples besought the risen Lord to abide with them in the close of that ancient day, so was the meaning of this song written in the “shadows of death” to the hymn writer.

Lyte himself composed a tune for this hymn on the same evening that he wrote it, but it never became widely used. However, the tune universally used was written fourteen years later by William Henry Monk, a noted London musician, and editor of the well-known Anglican hymnal, Hymns Ancient and Modern. He included this song in his first edition, which was published in 1861.

In all, William H. Monk composed 50 tunes for the hymnal. It is said that Monk, being “inspired by the beauty of a glorious sunset while yet experiencing a deep personal sorrow,” composed (in only 10 minutes) the tune, Eventide, for the song, “Abide With Me, Fast Falls The Eventide”. William Monk also wrote the music for other familiar hymns such as “Look, Ye Saints! The Sight Is Glorious”, and “The Strife Is O’er”.

To summarize, Henry Lyte experienced many sorrows during his lifetime. Both of his parents died at an early age leaving him an orphan. And his own sickness and frailty caused him to be in ongoing danger of asthma and tuberculosis. Yet, in spite of all his trials, we find in him a resilient spirit to reach out to others; to touch and minister the Gospel to those poor people among whom he lived. “In no other writer,” says Dr. Breed (in the Treasury of Hymn Stories), “are poetry and religion more exquisitely united.”

تُعد هذه الأنشودة عموماً واحدة من أعظم الأناشيد التي كُتبت على الإطلاق وتوجد في كل نشيد تقريباً أو كتاب أناشيد منشور اليوم. كتبها رجل كان ضعيف الجسم، لكنه قوي الروح. هو نفسه صاغ العبارة: «من الأفضل أن تتآكل بالعمل من أن تلتصق بالصدأ». لنلقِ الآن نظرة خاطفة على حياة هذا الخادم لله.

وُلد هنري فرانسيس لايت، مؤلف هذه الأنشودة العظيمة والملحوظة، في الأول من حزيران (يونيو) 1793 في إدنم قرب كيلسو في اسكتلندا. في سن مبكرة تُرك يتيماً وكان في فقر مقارن. تلقى تعليمه في كلية ترينيتي في دبلن بأيرلندا. هناك بدأ موهبة الشعر تظهر لديه، وفاز بثلاث جوائز. كان هدفه الأساسي من دراسته أن يصبح طبيباً، لكن عوضاً عن ذلك، بتدبير الله، أصبح قساً لإنجيل يسوع المسيح.

ذات يوم في كورنوال، طلب منه رجل دين زميل كان على فراش الموت أن يأتي ويمنحه بعض العزاء الروحي. «إلى حزنهما المتبادل، وجدا نفسيهما [كلاهما] يتلمسان النور، مرشدين أعمى حقاً». وبينما كانا يبحثان عن الحق والاطمئنان بالخلاص، وضعا إيمانهما على المسيح، وخرج لايت من تلك الغرفة المريضة رجلاً متغيراً، لا يكون كما كان أبداً. ويقال إن لقائه بالله عند سرير ذلك الرجل المحتضر هو ما دفع لايت إلى نظم أننشوده النبيلة «يا يسوع، قد أخذت صليبي». في سنة 1823، تولى هنري ف. لايت رعاية رعية ساحلية، لوور بريكسهام، في ديفونشير بإنجلترا. هناك قضى آخر 23 سنة من حياته يعمل كراعٍ للخير الروحي للفقراء من أهل الصيد ورجال البحار الخشنين في تلك المنطقة حتى وفاته في خريف عام 1847. لقاء كل تفانٍ وجهد هنري، حصد ثماراً: فقد أدار مدرسة أحد أيام الأحد تضم عدة مئات من التلاميذ، وكذلك «شعبة رائعة من سبعين أو ثمانين معلماً، دربهم شخصياً هو.»

طوال حياته كانت صحته مهددة باستمرار بالربو والسل. ورغم ضعفه الجسدي، عمل بلا كلل وذا سمعة راسخة كشاعر وموسيقي وقس. أينما ذهب كان محبوباً ومعجباً به كثيراً من قبل قومه. نحو نهاية تلك السنوات الأخيرة، تدهورت صحته تدريجياً. فسعى خلال أشهر الشتاء إلى مناخ أدفأ في إيطاليا، التي هي جزء من جنوب أوروبا.

ورغم أنه كان منهكاً بشدة بسبب مرضه، في 4 أيلول (سبتمبر) 1847، حينما كان لايت على وشك المغادرة متجهاً جنوباً، أوقفته «رغبة لا تُقاوم» في الوعظ مرة أخرى لجماعته. كان يحب هؤلاء الناس حباً عظيماً وقد خدم بينهم لسنوات عديدة. «ضد احتجاج أصدقائه المتعجبين، أنجز هذا الهدف، وقد سُجل أن لايت اضطر تقريباً إلى الزحف إلى المنبر وجاءت رسالته كما لو أنها من رجل محتضر.» «يا إخوة»، قال وهو يدخل المنبر المألوف للمرة الأخيرة، «أقف هنا بينكم اليوم، كما لو أنني حيّ من بين الأموات، إن كان لي أمل أن أؤثر فيكم وأن أحضّكم لتستعدوا لذلك الساعة الجليلة التي لا بد أن تأتي على الجميع، بتقدير معقول واعتماد على موت المسيح.» تركت هذه الكلمات الأخيرة أثراً عميقاً في جماعتِه، ثم ختم الخدمة بإدارة سر الرب لشعبه الباكي. في وقت لاحق من تلك الليلة، وبعد الخدمة، أوحى إليه أن «ينظّم شعراً» فكتب مقاطع الأنشودة الثمانية الأخيرة والعظمى:

أبقَ معي: الليل يهطل سريعاً؛
الظلام يزداد عمقاً؛ يا رب، أبقَ معي:
عندما تفشل المساعدات الأخرى، وتهرب العزائم،
يا معين العاجزين، آه، أبقَ معي.

سريعٌ ينحسرُ قليلُ نهارِ الحياة إلى غايته؛
تبهت أفراح الأرض، وتزول أمجادها;
أرى حولي التغير والزوال في كل شيء؛
يا أنت الذي لا تتغير، أبقَ معي.

لا أطلب لمحة عابرة، ولا كلمة مروَّضة؛
بل كما سكنت مع تلاميذك، يا رب،
ألف، متضاءل، صبور، كريم،
تعال، لا لتقيم نُزلاً، بل أبقَ، معي.

لا تأتِ بالرعب، كملك الملوك؛
بل طيبًا وجيدًا، مع شفاء في جناحيك؛
دموعٌ لكل الآلام، وقلبٌ لكل توسّل؛
تعال، صديق الخاطئين، وهكذا «أبقَ معي.»

على رأسي ابتسمت في شبابي المبكر؛
ورغم عصياني وازدرائي فيما مضى،
لم تتركني، كلما تركتك أنا:
حتى النهاية، يا رب، أبقَ معي.

أحتاج حضورك كل ساعة تمر؛
ما الذي سوى نعمتك يرده عن قوة المغوِّي؟
من يكون دليلي وسندي مثلك أنت؟
عبر الغيوم والشمس، آه، أبقَ معي.

لا أخشى خصماً إذا كنت أنت بالقرب لتباركني:
الآلام لا وزن لها، والدموع لا مرارة لها.
أين إبرة الموت؟ أين، أيتها القبر، نصرُك؟
ما زلتُ أنتصر، إن أبقيتَ معي.

ثبت صليبك أمام عيناي الختاميتين؛
أشرق خلال الظلام، وارشدني إلى السماوات؛
فجر السماء يبزغ، وظلال الأرض الباطلة تفرّ:
في الحياة، في الموت، يا رب، أبقَ معي.

وقد أعطى هذه الأنشودة لأحد أفراد العائلة في تلك الليلة نفسها. وفي اليوم التالي بدأ رحلته إلى روما بإيطاليا على أمل أن يجد بعض الراحة من مرضه. وصل لايت إلى نيس في فرنسا حيث منعه مرضه من مواصلة السفر. توفي بعد ذلك بوقت قصير عن عمر يناهز 55 عاماً، في 20 تشرين الثاني (نوفمبر) 1847. كانت كلماته الأخيرة «فرح! سلام!»

المشهد وراء هذه الأنشودة هو للمسيح القائم يسوع يسير في طريق عماوس مع اثنين من تلاميذه الحزينين بعض الشيء والمحبطين. وبينما كانوا يقتربون من نهاية مسيرتهم التي قُدِّرت بسبعة أميال واقتربوا من القرية التي كانوا متجهين إليها، «…تظاهر أنه أراد أن يذهب أبعد. فأقاماه قائلين له: أبقَ معنا لأن النهار قد مضى وقد قرُب المساء. فدخل ليباعد معهم» – لوقا 24:28-29.

يمكننا أن نستخلص موازاة بين ذلك المشهد وتجربة هنري ف. لايت نفسه وهو يقترب من ختام رحلته الأرضية. لذلك، كما التمس التلاميذ من الرب القائم أن يثبت معهم في نهاية ذلك اليوم القديم، هكذا كان معنى هذه الأنشودة التي كُتبت في «ظلال الموت» لكاتب الأنشودة.

قام لايت بنفسه بتلحين لحن لهذه الأنشودة في الليلة نفسها التي كتبها، لكنه لم يصبح مستخدماً على نطاق واسع. ومع ذلك، فإن اللحن المستخدم عالمياً كُتب بعد أربعة عشر عاماً بواسطة ويليام هنري مونك، موسيقي لندن المعروف ومحرر النشيد الأنغليكاني الشهير Hymns Ancient and Modern. أدرج هذا الأغنية في طبعةِه الأولى التي نُشرت عام 1861.

إجمالاً، وضع ويليام هـ. مونك 50 لحناً لهذا الكتاب. ويُقال إن مونك، وقد «ألهمته روعة غروب الشمس بينما كان يعاني في الوقت ذاته من حزن شخصي عميق»، لحن (في عشر دقائق فقط) المقام Eventide لأنشودة «أبقَ معي، الليل يهطل سريعاً». كما كتب ويليام مونك موسيقى أناشيد مألوفة أخرى مثل «انظروا يا قديسيْن! المنظر رائع»، و«انقضت المعركة».

خلاصة القول، عانَى هنري لايت كثيراً أثناء حياته. مات كلا والديه في سن مبكرة فتركاه يتيماً. وسبّب مرضه وضعفه خطر استمرار الإصابة بالربو والسل. ومع ذلك، رغم كل محنِه، نجد فيه روحاً مرنة تمتد إلى الآخرين؛ تلمسهم وتخدم بالإنجيل أولئك الفقراء الذين عاش بينهم. «في لا كاتب آخر»، يقول الدكتور بريد (في Treasury of Hymn Stories)، «يتحد الشعر والدين ببهاء أكثر من اتحادهما فيه.»

“Why don’t we have a cure for cancer yet?” My patient asked me.

I shrugged. “There are lots of different kinds of cancer,” I said. “For some, there are cures, while for others we are still learning how best to treat them.”

“I think,” my patient said with the confidence that he was supposedly sharing a top-secret theory. “I think there actually is a cure for cancer, but the drug companies just don’t want us to know about it.”

I shook my head. “I think we are doing the best we can,” I told him. “We’ve come a long way when it comes to treatment of cancer, but we still have a long way to go.”

Cancer is a scary illness. One Christian man told me that he wasn’t afraid of dying, but if he had a choice, he would choose almost any other way to go than to die of cancer.

More than that, it is something that seems mysterious. More people seem to be getting it, yet no one really knows why.

In this article, I would like to take some time to explore what cancer is, and to discuss cancer screening tests. In the second part (in the next issue) Lord willing, I will discuss some of the treatments available for cancers.

I will mention here that I am a family doctor. I have cared for many patients with cancer, but I am certainly not an oncologist, nor do I know everything about cancer. What I understand, I am willing to share.

What is Cancer?

As with many things, we can trace the beginnings of cancer back to the fall of man in the Garden of Eden. We know that God created humans perfectly. As originally created, not only did they not have cancer, but they also would not have gotten it either.

In order to understand what cancer is, we need to understand how normal tissue and cells behave.

Normal cells live for a period of time and then die. This process is called apoptosis. It makes certain that there is a constant turnover of cells. It also prevents one type of cell from getting “out of line” and beginning to grow in a place where it doesn’t belong.

Every time our cells divide, they copy their DNA into the daughter cells. Usually this happens without error, but occasionally there is an error in the copy process. We call these errors mutations.

Cancer cells are cells that have lost the normal brakes on their behavior. Because of mutations in their DNA, they no longer have a limited life span, nor do they observe the limits of where they belong within the body. Instead, they begin to encroach on surrounding tissues, pulling in additional blood supply and nutrients in the process.

Cancer cells can enlarge locally, or they can spread through the lymphatic system or circulatory system to distant parts of the body. When cancer cells end up in other locations than where they originated, we call it metastases.

The type of cancer is determined by the type of cell that is multiplying out of control. Doctors don’t generally talk about “skin cancer,” even though there are cancers that originate in skin cells. Instead, they classify these cancers into basal cell carcinoma, squamous cell carcinoma, and melanoma—each one referring to a different kind of skin cell. Each one of these skin cancers acts differently. Basal cell carcinoma and squamous cell carcinoma get bigger in a local area and seldom spread elsewhere, while melanoma is very prone to spreading to other parts of the body.

Additionally, how a cancer responds to treatment is going to be based on the type of cell that it comes from, not simply the organ where it originates.

Causes of Mutations…

We do not know how common cancer was in the days before the flood. I would speculate that it was fairly rare.

We know that before the flood, men lived to be very old—often into their 900s. Mutations must have been rare. Their DNA was closer to the original genetic specimen of mankind (and thus, to perfection) than ours is in the 21st century (AD) Therefore, the chance of genes mutating and abnormal genes popping up was much less than it is now.

…Environmental Factors

Beyond that, something must have happened around the time of the flood that increased the rate of mutations. Perhaps there was an increase in radiation levels. Maybe there were genetic changes that gradually caused cancer to show up.

Cancer is not mentioned in the Bible, although it is possible that Hezekiah’s “boil” could have been some kind of cancerous growth. It is also possible that some of the diseases that affected the Philistines when the ark of the covenant was in their land were cancerous tumors.

People began dying at younger ages after the flood and by soon after the time of Abraham, they were seldom living much past their one hundredth year.

Today, we know that things which damage a cell’s copying mechanism and its DNA increase the risk of cancer. The most well-known of these is radiation.

After the atomic bombs were dropped on Hiroshima and Nagasaki, survivors were noted to have significant increases in certain kinds of cancer. Leukemia (cancer of the blood) was the most common type of cancer, followed by cancer of stomach, lung, liver, and breast.

Radiation isn’t something that most people deal with on a regular basis. However, if you work in an x-ray department or if you needed to have radiation to treat some type of cancer, it is possible that you have been exposed to much higher levels of radiation than the general public.

There are plenty of other things that are associated with increases in cancers. Exposure to ultraviolet light increases the risk of skin cancer and is a big reason why doctors recommend sunscreen and protective clothing while enjoying the sunshine to limit ultraviolet exposure.

Finally, there are plenty of chemicals that are present in different types of work that can increase the risk of cancer.

…Unhealthy Foods

Foods that are high in nitrites increase the risk of intestinal cancers. Nitrites are typically present in smoked and cured meats. So, to be healthy, people should limit their intake of these foods to none or at the very least, a very limited percentage of the overall diet.

…Certain Prior Diseases

Another thing to mention is that certain types of infections can increase the risk of cancer. Epstein Barr virus, which causes infectious mononucleosis, has been associated with certain kinds of lymphoma. Hepatitis B and C increase the risk of hepatocellular carcinoma (liver cancer). And Helicobacter pylori infections in the stomach are associated with stomach cancers.

It is important to remember that just because someone has had one of these viruses it will not necessarily cause them to get cancer from that infection. Rather, it simply increases the risk that the person infected will get cancer at some point in the future.

…Unhealthy Habits

One last thing to mention is that certain toxins dramatically increase the risk of cancer. An obvious one is tobacco use, which strongly increases the risk of lung cancer, throat cancer, and even bladder cancer. Alcohol is another risk factor. Alcohol increases the risk of mouth and throat cancers, gastrointestinal cancers, and liver cancer. There really isn’t a safe amount of exposure to either of these toxic agents, but certainly the higher the level of exposure, the worse it is.

Screening for Cancer

There are many tests available that claim to be able to screen for a variety of cancers. Most of them are at least a little effective at identifying cancers at an early stage. However, there are a few problems with some of them which indicate that a certain test is ineffective at truly helping with the screening process.

A good place to start is to simply think about what a perfect screening test would look like. This will help us to see where tests might be beneficial or not.

A perfect screening test is going to have a number of features. First, it will have no false positive or false negative results. In other words, everyone who tests positive with the test will have cancer and those who test negative will not have cancer. Next, the test will identify the cancer at a point early enough in its development that it is easy to treat. The test will be cheap and minimally invasive, and it will require minimal exposure to radiation.

Unfortunately, no test that we currently do for screening totally meets these criteria.

For one thing, many tests produce both false positive and negative tests. These are both problems. The issue with a false negative test is obvious—it leads to someone thinking they don’t have cancer when they really do. A false positive test on the other hand leads to higher anxiety levels along with the cost and dangers from whatever ongoing testing is necessary to let a patient know that they don’t really have cancer.

An example of a bad test, in this respect, is the CEA-125. CEA-125 is a chemical that is made by some types of cancer. Oncologists use this level to track a patient’s response to chemotherapy.

It would make sense that you could use this as a screening test for these cancers, but it simply doesn’t work. Many people have elevated CEA levels, even though they don’t have cancer and on the other side, plenty of GI (gastrointestinal) cancers don’t make this chemical at all. Testing lots of people with CEA-125 testing will lead to more scans and biopsies, but it is doubtful if it would have a significant impact on death rates from cancer.

Another issue has to do with a particular cancer itself. In order for a test to be helpful, the cancer needs to have a long progression through precancerous stages until finally it develops into full-blown cancer.

An example is colon cancer. Most people who develop colon cancer have precancerous polyps several years before they get the cancer. This is why colonoscopies can be effective at preventing the progression to colon cancer.

If a patient has a colonoscopy, the doctor can detect the presence of polyps. More than that, he can remove the polyps through the scope, hopefully stopping the progression to cancer.

One last, related point is that there needs to be some benefit to early detection of cancer. If a new test can detect cancer six months earlier than existing tests, people will live an average of six months longer with the cancer than before, even if nothing else changes.

The question is whether diagnosing the cancer earlier leads to more effective treatment. Can you take it out before it spreads to the lymph glands and thereby completely avoid the need for chemotherapy?

If treatment and response rates are the same regardless of the stage at which you diagnose a cancer, then screening doesn’t really make sense.

The United States Preventive Services Task Force is a volunteer panel of experts that have reviewed the literature on a variety of tests. Based on the studies that have been conducted regarding the available tests, they make recommendations about the various tests and how often to use them.

This panel tends to be more conservative in their recommendations than many cancer societies. For instance, they recommend every other year for the use of mammograms for women between the ages of 50 and 75, as compared to the yearly screening recommended by other groups.

With each recommendation they give a grade of how good the studies are which support that specific recommendation, along with links for those studies. Their recommendations are well researched. This is helpful for low-risk people trying to decide what testing to do. If someone has a high risk because of family history or exposures, their recommendations are less helpful.

Cancer Challenges

People often discuss cancer as though it was a single entity. As before mentioned, cancer is not just one thing. Skin cancer behaves differently from lymphoma, which in turn behaves differently from sarcomas. The chance that there will ever be a single treatment for all cancer—the “Cure for Cancer” which people talk about, is unlikely.

An even bigger challenge when dealing with cancer cells is that they are very similar to our normal cells. Basically, we are trying to poison the cancer just a little more than the rest of our normal tissues. There are a number of different treatments that are currently available. In Part 2, we will address some of the different options available today and some others that may become available in the future.

Final Thoughts

There are a few things that come to mind when contemplating the subject of cancer.

We do not need to live in fear or make choices out of fear. Fear thou not; for I am with thee: be not dismayed; for I am thy God: I will strengthen thee; yea, I will help thee; yea, I will uphold thee with the right hand of my righteousness –Isaiah 41:10.

I don’t think that we should fatalistically allow anything to happen that might, simply because it is “God’s will.” We need to make wise choices, then having done so, we should not live in a state of anxiety.

Therefore take no thought, saying, What shall we eat? or, What shall we drink? or, Wherewithal shall we be clothed? (For after all these things do the Gentiles seek:) for your heavenly Father knoweth that ye have need of all these things. But seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you. Take therefore no thought for the morrow: for the morrow shall take thought for the things of itself. Sufficient unto the day is the evil thereof –Matthew 6:31-34.

Finally, if we can, through wise decisions, prevent a certain cancer from forming or spreading, that seems like a reasonable goal. None of us will live forever in this body, but if we can die of something other than cancer, that seems like a good goal too. May God give us wisdom to care for the body which He has given us.

“हमारे पास अभी तक कैंसर का इलाज क्यों नहीं है?” मेरे रोगी ने मुझसे पूछा।

मैंने कंधे उचका दिए। “कैंसर के कई अलग-अलग प्रकार होते हैं,” मैंने कहा। “कुछ के लिए इलाज होते हैं, जबकि अन्य के लिए हम अभी भी यह सीख रहे हैं कि उन्हें सबसे अच्छा कैसे उपचारित किया जाए।”

“मुझे लगता है,” मेरे रोगी ने वैसे विश्वास के साथ कहा जैसे वह कोई शीर्ष-गुप्त सिद्धांत साझा कर रहा हो। “मुझे लगता है कि असल में कैंसर का इलाज है, पर ड्रग कंपनियाँ बस हमें उसके बारे में नहीं बताना चाहतीं।”

मैंने सिर हिलाया। “मुझे लगता है हम अपनी तरफ से बेहतरीन कर रहे हैं,” मैंने उसे बताया। “कैंसर के उपचार के मामले में हमने लंबा सफर तय किया है, पर अभी भी हमारे सामने बहुत काम बाकी है।”

कैंसर एक भयानक बीमारी है। एक ईसाई पुरुष ने मुझे बताया कि वह मरने से नहीं डरता, पर अगर उसे चुनाव करना हो तो वह कैंसर से मरने के अलावा शायद ही किसी अन्य तरीके को पसंद करेगा।

उससे भी बढ़कर, यह कुछ ऐसा है जो रहस्यमय लगती है। अधिक लोग इसे पाते दिख रहे हैं, फिर भी कोई वास्तव में नहीं जानता क्यों।

इस लेख में, मैं कुछ समय लेकर यह बताना चाहूँगा कि कैंसर क्या है, और कैंसर स्क्रीनिंग परीक्षणों पर चर्चा करना चाहूँगा। दूसरे भाग में (अगले अंक में), प्रभु की इच्छा हो तो, मैं कुछ कैंसर उपचारों पर चर्चा करूँगा।

यहाँ मैं यह उल्लेख करूँगा कि मैं एक फैमिली डॉक्टर हूँ। मैंने कई कैंसर रोगियों की देखभाल की है, पर मैं निश्चित रूप से ऑन्कोलॉजिस्ट नहीं हूँ, और न ही मैं कैंसर के बारे में सब कुछ जानता हूँ। जो मैं समझता हूँ, उसे मैं साझा करने को तैयार हूँ।

कैंसर क्या है?

कई चीजों की तरह, हम कैंसर की शुरुआत को मानव के पतन तक, एडेन् के बगीचे में वापस trace कर सकते हैं। हम जानते हैं कि परमेश्वर ने मनुष्यों को परिपूर्ण रूप से बनाया था। मूल रूप से बनाए जाने पर, न केवल उन्हें कैंसर नहीं था, बल्कि वे इसे प्राप्त भी नहीं करते थे।

कैंसर क्या है यह समझने के लिए, हमें यह समझना होगा कि सामान्य ऊतक और कोशिकाएँ कैसे व्यवहार करती हैं।

सामान्य कोशिकाएँ एक अवधि तक जीवित रहती हैं और फिर मर जाती हैं। इस प्रक्रिया को एपोप्टोसिस कहा जाता है। यह सुनिश्चित करता है कि कोशिकाओं का निरंतर नवीकरण होता रहे। यह यह भी रोकता है कि किसी प्रकार की कोशिका “सीमा से बाहर” होकर उस स्थान पर बढ़ने लगे जहाँ वह नहीं होनी चाहिए।

हर बार जब हमारी कोशिकाएँ विभाजित होती हैं, वे अपनी DNA की प्रतिलिपि बेटा कोशिकाओं में बनाती हैं। आमतौर पर यह त्रुटि के बिना होता है, पर कभी-कभी प्रतिलिपि प्रक्रिया में त्रुटि हो जाती है। हम इन त्रुटियों को म्यूटेशन कहते हैं।

कैंसर कोशिकाएँ वे कोशिकाएँ हैं जिन्होंने अपने व्यवहार पर सामान्य ब्रेक खो दिए हैं। उनके DNA में म्यूटेशन के कारण, अब उनकी सीमित आयु नहीं रहती, न ही वे शरीर के भीतर जहाँ वे होने चाहिए वहाँ की सीमाओं का पालन करती हैं।इसके बजाय, वे आसपास के ऊतकों पर आक्रमण करने लगती हैं, और इस प्रक्रिया में अतिरिक्त रक्त आपूर्ति और पोषक तत्व खींचने लगती हैं।

कैंसर कोशिकाएँ स्थानीय रूप से बढ़ सकती हैं, या वे लिम्फैटिक सिस्टम या परिसंचरण प्रणाली के माध्यम से शरीर के दूरस्थ भागों तक फैल सकती हैं। जब कैंसर कोशिकाएँ उस स्थान के अलावा किसी अन्य स्थान पर पहुँच जाती हैं जहाँ वे उत्पन्न हुई थीं, तो इसे मेटास्टेसिस कहा जाता है।

कैंसर का प्रकार उस कोशिका के प्रकार से निर्धारित होता है जो अनियंत्रित रूप से विभाजित हो रही है। डॉक्टर आमतौर पर “त्वचा कैंसर” इस प्रकार बात नहीं करते, यद्यपि त्वचा कोशिकाओं से उत्पन्न होने वाले कैंसर होते हैं। इसके बजाय, वे इन कैंसरों को बेसल सेल कार्सिनोमा, स्क्वैमस सेल कार्सिनोमा, और मेलेनोमा के रूप में वर्गीकृत करते हैं—प्रत्येक एक अलग प्रकार की त्वचा कोशिका को सूचित करता है। इन तीनों त्वचा के कैंसरों का व्यवहार अलग-अलग होता है। बेसल सेल कार्सिनोमा और स्क्वैमस सेल कार्सिनोमा स्थानीय क्षेत्र में बढ़ते हैं और शायद ही कहीं और फैलते हैं, जबकि मेलेनोमा अन्य हिस्सों में फैलने के लिए अत्यधिक प्रवण है।

इसके अतिरिक्त, किसी कैंसर का उपचार के प्रति कैसे प्रतिक्रिया होगी यह इस बात पर आधारित होगा कि वह किस प्रकार की कोशिका से आया है, न कि केवल उस अंग पर जहाँ से वह उत्पन्न हुआ।

म्यूटेशन के कारण...

हमें यह नहीं पता कि बाढ़ से पहले के दिनों में कैंसर कितना आम था। मैं अनुमान लगाऊँगा कि यह काफी दुर्लभ था।

हम जानते हैं कि बाढ़ से पहले मनुष्य बहुत लंबी आयु जीते थे—अक्सर 900 वर्ष तक। म्यूटेशन शायद दुर्लभ थे। उनका DNA मानवता के मूल आनुवंशिक नमूने (और इस प्रकार, परिपूर्णता) के निकट था जितना 21st सदी (AD) में हमारा है। इसलिए, जीनों के म्यूटेट करने और असामान्य जीनों के उत्पन्न होने की संभावना अब की तुलना में बहुत कम थी।

...पर्यावरणीय कारक

उसके आगे, कुछ ऐसा बाढ़ के समय के आसपास हुआ होगा जिसने म्यूटेशनों की दर बढ़ा दी। संभव है कि विकिरण स्तरों में वृद्धि हुई हो। शायद आनुवंशिक परिवर्तन हुए जो धीरे-धीरे कैंसर के प्रकट होने का कारण बने।

कैंसर बाइबिल में उल्लेखित नहीं है, यद्यपि यह संभव है कि हिज़किय्याह का “फोड़ा” किसी प्रकार का कैंसरयुक्त ऊदय रहा हो। यह भी संभव है कि जब धर्मगृह का ताबूत फ़िलीस्तियों के देश में था तब उन्होंने जिन रोगों का अनुभव किया वे कैंसरयुक्त ट्यूमर रहे हों।

बाढ़ के बाद लोग कम उम्र में मरने लगे और अब्राहम के समय के बाद जल्दी ही वे सौ वर्ष से अधिक जीवित काफी कम रहते थे।

आज, हम जानते हैं कि जो चीजें किसी कोशिका की प्रतिलिपि बनाने की प्रणाली और उसके DNA को नुकसान पहुँचाती हैं वे कैंसर का जोखिम बढ़ाती हैं। इनमें सबसे अधिक जाना-माना विकिरण है।

जब हिरोशिमा और नाघासाकी पर परमाणु बम गिराए गए, सर्वाइवरों में कुछ प्रकार के कैंसरों में उल्लेखनीय वृद्धि देखी गई। ल्यूकेमिया (रक्त का कैंसर) सबसे सामान्य प्रकार था, इसके बाद पेट, फेफड़े, जिगर, और स्तन के कैंसर आए।

विकिरण ऐसी चीज़ नहीं है जिससे अधिकांश लोग नियमित रूप से निपटते हों। हालाँकि, यदि आप एक्स-रे विभाग में काम करते हैं या आपको किसी प्रकार के कैंसर के उपचार के लिए विकिरण देनी पड़ी है, तो संभव है कि आप सामान्य जनता की तुलना में बहुत अधिक विकिरण के संपर्क में रहे हों।

कैंसर वृद्धि से जुड़े और भी कई तत्व हैं। अल्ट्रावायलेट प्रकाश के संपर्क में आना त्वचा कैंसर का जोखिम बढ़ाता है और यही एक बड़ा कारण है कि डॉक्टर सूर्य का आनंद लेते समय अल्ट्रावायलेट के संपर्क को सीमित करने के लिए सनस्क्रीन और सुरक्षात्मक कपड़ों की सलाह देते हैं।

अंत में, विभिन्न प्रकार के कार्यों में मौजूद कई रसायन कैंसर का जोखिम बढ़ा सकते हैं।

...अस्वस्थ खाद्य पदार्थ

नाइट्राइट्स से भरपूर खाद्य पदार्थ आंत के कैंसर का जोखिम बढ़ाते हैं। नाइट्राइट्स सामान्यतः स्मोक्ड और क्योर किए हुए मांस में पाए जाते हैं। इसलिए, स्वस्थ रहने के लिए लोगों को इन खाद्य पदार्थों का सेवन शून्य या कम से कम, कुल आहार का बहुत सीमित प्रतिशत रखना चाहिए।

...कुछ पूर्व रोग

एक और बात यह है कि कुछ प्रकार के संक्रमण कैंसर का जोखिम बढ़ा सकते हैं। एपस्टीन बार वायरस, जो संक्रामक मोनोनेयूक्लियोसिस का कारण बनता है, कुछ प्रकार के लिम्फोमा से जुड़ा हुआ है। हेपेटाइटिस बी और सी हेपाटोसेलुलर कार्सिनोमा (यकृत कैंसर) का जोखिम बढ़ाते हैं। और Helicobacter pylori संक्रमण पेट के कैंसर से जुड़े हैं।

यह याद रखना महत्वपूर्ण है कि सिर्फ इसलिए कि किसी व्यक्ति को इन में से किसी वायरस का संक्रमण हुआ होगा, इसका यह अर्थ नहीं कि वह निश्चित रूप से उसी संक्रमण से कैंसर हो जाएगा। बल्कि, यह केवल उस व्यक्ति में भविष्य में कैंसर होने की संभावना को बढ़ा देता है।

...अस्वस्थ आदतें

एक अंतिम बात यह है कि कुछ विषाक्त पदार्थ कैंसर का जोखिम नाटकीय रूप से बढ़ा देते हैं। एक स्पष्ट उदाहरण तंबाकू का उपयोग है, जो फेफड़े के कैंसर, गले के कैंसर, और यहां तक कि मूत्राशय के कैंसर के जोखिम को बहुत बढ़ाता है। शराब एक और जोखिम कारक है। शराब मुँह और गले के कैंसर, जठरांत्र संबंधी कैंसर, और यकृत कैंसर का जोखिम बढ़ाती है। इन विषाक्त एजेंटों के संदर्भ में वास्तव में कोई सुरक्षित मात्रा नहीं है, पर निश्चित रूप से जितना अधिक संपर्क होगा, उतना ही अधिक हानिकारक होगा।

कैंसर के लिए स्क्रीनिंग

कई परीक्षण उपलब्ध हैं जो विभिन्न प्रकार के कैंसर के लिए स्क्रीन करने का दावा करते हैं। इनमें से अधिकांश कम-से-कम कुछ हद तक शुरुआती चरण में कैंसर की पहचान करने में प्रभावी होते हैं। हालांकि, कुछ परीक्षणों के साथ कुछ समस्याएँ हैं जो संकेत देती हैं कि कोई विशेष परीक्षण स्क्रीनिंग प्रक्रिया में वास्तव में मददगार नहीं है।

शुरू करने के लिए एक अच्छा स्थान यह सोचना है कि एक आदर्श स्क्रीनिंग परीक्षण कैसा दिखेगा। यह हमें यह देखने में मदद करेगा कि परीक्षण लाभकारी हैं या नहीं।

एक आदर्श स्क्रीनिंग परीक्षण में कई विशेषताएँ होंगी। पहले, इसमें कोई झूठा सकारात्मक या झूठा नकारात्मक परिणाम नहीं होगा। दूसरे शब्दों में, जो कोई भी परीक्षण में सकारात्मक निकलेगा, उसे कैंसर होगा और जो नकारात्मक निकलेगा, उसे कैंसर नहीं होगा। अगला, परीक्षण कैंसर को उसके विकास के उस बिंदु पर पहचान लेगा जहाँ उसे उपचार करना आसान हो। परीक्षण सस्ता और कम आक्रामक होगा, और इसमें विकिरण का न्यूनतम एक्सपोजर होगा।

दुर्भाग्यवश, वर्तमान में स्क्रीनिंग के लिए जो भी परीक्षण हम करते हैं, वे इन मानदंडों को पूरी तरह से पूरा नहीं करते।

एक बात यह है कि कई परीक्षण झूठे सकारात्मक और नकारात्मक दोनों परिणाम देते हैं। ये दोनों समस्याएँ हैं। झूठा नकारात्मक परीक्षण स्पष्ट है—यह किसी को यह सोचने पर मजबूर करता है कि उसके पास कैंसर नहीं है जबकि वास्तव में है। झूठा सकारात्मक परीक्षण दूसरी ओर उच्च चिंता के स्तर के साथ-साथ आगे के परीक्षणों की लागत और खतरों की ओर ले जाता है जो यह पुष्टि करने के लिए आवश्यक होते हैं कि रोगी के पास वास्तव में कैंसर नहीं है।

इस संदर्भ में एक खराब परीक्षण का उदाहरण CEA-125 है। CEA-125 एक रासायनिक है जो कुछ प्रकार के कैंसर बनाते हैं। ऑनकोलॉजिस्ट इसका स्तर कीमोथेरेपी के प्रति रोगी की प्रतिक्रिया को ट्रैक करने के लिए उपयोग करते हैं।

यह समझ में आता है कि आप इसे इन कैंसरों के लिए एक स्क्रीनिंग परीक्षण के रूप में इस्तेमाल कर सकते हैं, पर यह बस काम नहीं करता। कई लोगों में CEA स्तर ऊँचा होता है, जबकि उनके पास कैंसर नहीं होता और दूसरी ओर, बहुत से GI (गैस्ट्रोइंटेस्टाइनल) कैंसर यह रसायन बिल्कुल नहीं बनाते। बहुत से लोगों की CEA-125 टेस्टिंग करने पर अधिक स्कैन और बायोप्सियाँ होंगी, पर यह संदेह है कि इसका कैंसर से मौत दरों पर कोई महत्वपूर्ण प्रभाव होगा।

एक और मुद्दा किसी विशेष कैंसर से जुड़ा हुआ है। किसी परीक्षण के उपयोगी होने के लिए, कैंसर का पूर्व-कैंसरous अवस्थाओं के माध्यम से लंबा प्रसार होना चाहिए जब तक कि अंततः यह पूर्ण-रूप से विकसित कैंसर न बन जाए।

उदाहरण कोलन कैंसर है। अधिकांश लोग जो कोलन कैंसर विकसित करते हैं उनके पास कैंसर से कई साल पहले पूर्व-कैंसरous पॉलीप्स होते हैं। यही कारण है कि कोलोस्कोपी कोलन कैंसर तक प्रगति को रोकने में प्रभावी हो सकती है।

यदि कोई रोगी कोलोस्कोपी करवाता है, तो डॉक्टर पॉलीप्स की उपस्थिति का पता लगा सकता है। उससे बढ़कर, वह स्कोप के माध्यम से पॉलीप्स को हटा सकता है, उम्मीद है कि इससे कैंसर तक प्रगति रुक जाएगी।

एक अंतिम, संबंधित बिंदु यह है कि प्रारंभिक पहचान का कुछ लाभ होना चाहिए। यदि कोई नया परीक्षण कैंसर का पता मौजूदा परीक्षणों की तुलना में छह महीने पहले लगा लेता है, तो लोग औसतन कैंसर के साथ पहले की तुलना में छह महीने अधिक जीएँगे, भले ही अन्य कुछ भी न बदले।

प्रश्न यह है कि क्या कैंसर का जल्दी निदान अधिक प्रभावी उपचार की ओर ले जाता है। क्या आप इसे लिम्फ ग्रंथियों तक फैलने से पहले निकाल सकते हैं और इस तरह रसायन चिकित्सा की आवश्यकता से पूरी तरह बच सकते हैं?

यदि उपचार और प्रतिक्रिया दरें उस चरण की परवाह किए बिना वही हैं जिस चरण पर आप कैंसर का निदान करते हैं, तो स्क्रीनिंग का वास्तव में कोई तर्क नहीं बनता।

यूनाइटेड स्टेट्स प्रिवेंटिव सर्विसेज टास्क फोर्स एक स्वयंसेवी विशेषज्ञ पैनल है जिसने विभिन्न परीक्षणों पर साहित्य की समीक्षा की है। उपलब्ध परीक्षणों के बारे में किए गए अध्ययनों के आधार पर, वे विभिन्न परीक्षणों और उन्हें कितनी बार उपयोग करने के बारे में सिफारिशें करते हैं।

यह पैनल कई कैंसर समाजों की तुलना में अपनी सिफारिशों में अधिक रूढ़िवादी होने की प्रवृत्ति रखता है। उदाहरण के लिए, वे 50 से 75 वर्ष की उम्र की महिलाओं के लिए मैमोग्राम के उपयोग के लिए हर दूसरे वर्ष की सिफारिश करते हैं, जबकि अन्य समूह वार्षिक स्क्रीनिंग की सलाह देते हैं।

प्रत्येक सिफारिश के साथ वे उस विशेष सिफारिश का समर्थन करने वाले अध्ययनों की गुणवत्ता का ग्रेड देते हैं, साथ ही उन अध्ययनों के लिंक भी देते हैं। उनकी सिफारिशें अच्छी तरह शोधित हैं। यह कम-जोखिम वाले लोगों के लिए क्या परीक्षण करने का निर्णय लेने में मददगार है। यदि किसी व्यक्ति का परिवारिक इतिहास या एक्सपोज़र के कारण उच्च जोखिम है, तो उनकी सिफारिशें कम सहायक होती हैं।

कैंसर की चुनौतियाँ

लोग अक्सर कैंसर की चर्चा ऐसे करते हैं जैसे यह एक ही इकाई हो। जैसा पहले उल्लेख किया गया, कैंसर केवल एक चीज़ नहीं है। त्वचा कैंसर का व्यवहार लिम्फोमा से अलग है, जो अपनी ओर से सारकॉमा से अलग व्यवहार करता है। इस बात की संभावना कि कभी सभी कैंसरों के लिए एक ही उपचार—लोगों द्वारा बात किए जाने वाला “कैंसर का इलाज”—मिलेगा, कम ही है।

कैंसर कोशिकाओं से निपटने में एक और बड़ी चुनौती यह है कि वे हमारी सामान्य कोशिकाओं के बहुत समान होती हैं। मूल रूप से, हम कोशिश कर रहे हैं कैंसर को थोड़ी अधिक जहर देना बनिस्बत हमारी सामान्य ऊतकों के। वर्तमान में कई अलग-अलग उपचार उपलब्ध हैं। भाग 2 में, हम आज उपलब्ध विभिन्न विकल्पों और कुछ अन्य जो भविष्य में उपलब्ध हो सकते हैं, उन पर चर्चा करेंगे।

अंतिम विचार

कैंसर के विषय पर विचिन्तन करते समय कुछ बातें मेरे मन में आती हैं।

हमें भय के कारण जीने या भय से प्रेरित होकर निर्णय लेने की ज़रूरत नहीं है। डर मत; क्योंकि मैं तुम्हारे साथ हूँ: घबराओ मत; क्योंकि मैं तुम्हारा परमेश्वर हूँ: मैं तुझे दृढ़ करूँगा; हाँ, मैं तुझे सहायक बनूँगा; हाँ, मैं अपनी धार्मिकता के दाहिने हाथ से तुझको संभालूँगा –Isaiah 41:10.

मुझे नहीं लगता कि हमें भाग्यवश किसी भी चीज़ को ऐसा होने देना चाहिए क्योंकि वह “परमेश्वर की इच्छा” है। हमें बुद्धिमानी से निर्णय लेने चाहिए, और फिर ऐसा करने के बाद हमें चिंता की स्थिति में नहीं जीना चाहिए।

सो निश्चिन्त हो जाओ, कहकर, हम क्या खाएँगे? या हम क्या पियेंगे? या हम किससे वस्त्र पहिनेंगे? (इन सब बातों के लिए विदेशी लोग तड़पते हैं:) तुम्हारा स्वर्गीय पिता जानता है कि तुम्हें इन सब चीज़ों की ज़रूरत है। परन्तु पहले परमेश्वर का राज्य और उसकी धार्मिकता खोजो; और ये सब चीज़ें तुम्हें भी दी जाएँगी। अतः कल की चिंता मत करो: क्योंकि कल अपनी बातें स्वयं करेगी। प्रतिदिन के लिये अपने बुरे की मात्रा पर्याप्त है –Matthew 6:31-34.

अंत में, यदि हम बुद्धिमानी भरे निर्णयों के द्वारा किसी निश्चित कैंसर के बनकर या फैलने से रोक सकें, तो वह एक तर्कसंगत लक्ष्य लगता है। हम में से कोई भी इस शरीर में सदा जीवित नहीं रहेगा, पर यदि हम किसी ऐसे कारण से मर सकते हैं जो कैंसर न हो, तो वह भी एक अच्छा लक्ष्य लगता है। परमेश्वर हमें उस शरीर की देखभाल करने की बुद्धि दे जो उसने हमें दी है।

And there arose a great storm of wind, and the waves beat into the ship, so that it was now full. And he was in the hinder part of the ship, asleep on a pillow: and they awake him, and say unto him, Master, carest thou not that we perish? And he arose, and rebuked the wind, and said unto the sea, Peace, be still. And the wind ceased, and there was a great calm. And he said unto them, Why are ye so fearful? how is it that ye have no faith? And they feared exceedingly, and said one to another, What manner of man is this, that even the wind and the sea obey him? Mark 4:37-41

Many times, I have read this passage and wondered what we are to derive from it. It seems to be a story that generates more questions than it solves. We often like to think of Jesus as the relational form of the Godhead; a sort of go-between, between us and the Almighty God. But here, in our scriptural passage, His behavior is almost unthinkable in human terms. How could Christ sleep in such a storm, much less in a boat filling with water? We can believe that He is Master of the wind and seas, and they must bow at His command, but does He expect us to do the same? Would our compassionate Christ expect us to be calm and fearless in such dire straits? Is all exhibition of fear the fruit of our lack of faith? These probing questions are disturbing, for we all would hope that our faith in Him is strong enough to secure our salvation, yet experience has taught us that our own walk through the troublesome pastures of life has produced nothing more noble than the harrowing bleating of the disciples.

Why are ye so fearful? How is it that ye have no faith? The questions seem almost out of place coming from our Saviour, almost as though He is not as patient and longsuffering as we had hoped. But Christ has placed a definitive expectation upon His disciples that is not beyond their attainment. Was He calling on them to rebuke the storm themselves? Should they have awakened Him sooner? Did he expect them to quietly row on in confident assurance? The Scripture here supplies us with few answers, but we do know that there is an abiding lesson here concerning fear and faith.

Storms are a common part of life, and no major dilemma is pleasant. While Paul sailed toward Rome, they experienced a time …when neither sun nor stars in many days appeared, and no small tempest lay on us, all hope that we should be saved was then taken away –Acts 27:20. In the midst of a cloudy and hopeless situation there is one bell that continues to toll clear and bright: There is a peace that can be apprehended even in the most dreadful circumstances. Paul had spent a precarious …night and a day I have been in the deep –2 Corinthians 11:25, yet he did not demand the wind and sea to submit to his authority. Rather, he states that in the midst of the storm …there stood by me this night the angel of God, whose I am, and whom I serve, Saying, Fear not, Paul… –Acts 27:23-24. This is a scene similar to the peril being endured by the disciples (in our text for today) yet we see a different outcome. Paul was comforted and commended while the disciples received rebuke.

While bobbing about in the clutches of a potential watery grave, the disciples cried out: …Master, carest thou not that we perish? –Mark 4:38. How natural it is for us all to thrust our frustration and blame upon another. To think that some apathetic person is shirking their responsibility is very disheartening. In like fashion …the shipmaster came to him [Jonah], and said unto him, What meanest thou, O sleeper? arise, call upon thy God, if so be that God will think upon us, that we perish not –Jonah 1:6.

There seems to be an edge to the shipmaster’s rebuke very similar to the disciple’s response to the sleeping Jesus. Christ finds no pleasure in allowing trouble to visit us, but there seems to be no other veritable vehicle of grace wherewith His peace can flood our souls. If there first be no valley, how shall we value the mountaintop? If there be no thorns, how shall we enjoy the rose? If there first be no storm, how shall we appreciate the calm? Paul suffered the same despair being …pressed out of measure, above strength, insomuch that we despaired even of life –2 Corinthians 1:8. Yet he carried within his breast a visionary anchor for his soul.

For he commandeth, and raiseth the stormy wind, which lifteth up the waves thereof. They mount up to the heaven, they go down again to the depths: their soul is melted because of trouble. They reel to and fro, and stagger like a drunken man, and are at their wits’ end. Then they cry unto the LORD in their trouble, and he bringeth them out of their distresses. He maketh the storm a calm, so that the waves thereof are still. Then are they glad because they be quiet; so he bringeth them unto their desired haven –Psalm 107:25-30.

The Desired Haven…

Somehow, we have embraced the thought that the desired haven of rest is an earthly euphoric utopia void of any storms. The shipmaster in charge of guiding the vessel en route to Rome thought that …the haven was not commodious to winter in … supposing that they had obtained their purpose… –Acts 27:12-13, so he set sail at the first hint of approval from the soft south wind. But the haven Christ promotes is a harbor that is free from fretful fear and fledgling faith. This is a peace … not as the world giveth, give I unto you. Let not your heart be troubled, neither let it be afraid –John 14:27. This rest is ours to be had just by sailing with Christ and trusting Him to guide us through each storm.

The tenacious storms of adversity can arise without warning as quickly as …a tempestuous wind, called Euroclydon –Acts 27:14. These tempestuous winds carry an amazing audacity to jolt any relationship. To feel tense and alert in the midst of stressful situations is but human nature. Our central medulla gland unleashes a powerful hormone called adrenaline into our system, our muscles become tense, our mind focuses, so that we are aroused and prepared for fight or flight. This is not necessarily anxiety but a natural response. As humans, we have a divine capacity to reason in the midst of extreme passion and pressure. The disciples did not know what Jesus would do. They only knew that this situation was out of control. Here is where they made their major mistake. Christ knew Who was in control. Paul knew Who was in control. Even Jonah knew why the tempest had arisen. Our faith is bound to fail when anxiety escalates, and we think we must control the raging trials about us. We may have a noble agenda and a sincere heart and still find our faltering faith frazzled. We mistakenly marvel that God sits in heaven and does nothing. We faithfully launch our prayers upward, but the heavens seem brazenly silent. We would expect that from worshippers of Baal, Buddha, and from backsliders. But it is not supposed to happen to people with strong convictions—people who are born again, attend church regularly, read their Bible, and pray on a daily basis. We must reconsider that God is not so concerned about our environmental peace, but rather that our inner soul arrives safe and sound at His haven of rest.

When we are happy, we jubilantly claim that rest, even though we have no sense of truly needing Him. His insertions into our lives often seem like interruptions. But when times get desperate and we have exhausted all our resources, we lean hard upon Him. In that excruciating hour, He often tests our sincerity and offers us nothing … nothing but silence. Christ, sleeping in our boat. Sleeping… right when we need him the most. And then the question, Why are ye so fearful? How is it that ye have no faith? Frankly, this seems hard to me—even harsh—and entirely out of character with what I would normally expect from Jesus. But the question must be answered, for it is necessary if we wish to enter His haven of rest. The winds obey Him, but they don’t obey us … or do they? We obviously cannot control the weather, our environment, our situations, or the people around us. Yet these externals are not the root cause of our anxiety. It is our own faulty premonitions that pound our soul and prevent us from entering the portal of peace. The winds that whip our vessel into a fearful frenzy are not driven from without but unleashed from within. This anxiety rides on the waves of unbelief, while Christ continues in His divine slumber, waiting until we recognize the source of our anxiety and call out in faith. These four strong winds are roused at the slightest provocation when we are…

…Preserving our Person

If we are healthy, and if things are going well in our family and finances, we may be prone to misinterpret our circumstances. It is a mistake to believe that easy sailing is a mark of God’s favor, and that trouble is a sign of His displeasure. All good and perfect gifts come from God, but a debilitating storm can fall under that category as well. Our personal surroundings are temporal while our soul is eternal. God will frequently expend our personal comforts in order to expand our faith. But great fear arises when our person is demoted. Many of our phobias arise in the absence of actual danger.

  1. The acrophobic person has a fear of heights and is afraid he will fall from the heights of any platform though it is secure and guarded well. Even if countless others have successfully stood there, he is miserably trapped in this fear, not because he is in danger, but because he has grossly overestimated his likelihood of falling and refuses to believe the truth.
  2. The zoophobic lives in fear of animals, creating images in his mind of being clawed to death or disemboweled.
  3. The claustrophobic is afraid of small, tight places, while the agoraphobic fears open places.
  4. Arachibutyrophobia is the fear of getting peanut butter stuck to the roof of your mouth.

In the face of his fear, the phobic may experience a racing heart, heavy breathing, dry mouth, perspiration, dizziness, or light-headedness. Thus, their phobias become real to them. While most will excuse their personal glitch, the truth remains that this anxiety is unfounded. When we excuse and cater to the preservation of our person, fear is inevitable. The disciples feared that they were perishing, and Christ asked them why. Is it not better …to depart, and to be with Christ; which is far better –Philippians 1:23. If we can trust Christ with our life, can we not trust him with our death?

For whosoever will save his life shall lose it; but whosoever shall lose his life for my sake and the gospel’s, the same shall save it –Mark 8:35.

…Protecting our Property

Outwardly, the life of Christ was one of the most troubled lives that was ever lived. Foxes had their dens and the birds had their nests while He lay His pillow in the back of a rocking boat groaning under tempest and tumult of the incessant waves breaking over it. But His inner haven was a sea of glass. This was partially due to the fact that He had no property to protect. Even the boat was borrowed. “Much coin, much care” states the ancient proverb, and anxiety rises when wealth falls. And one of the company said unto him, Master, speak to my brother, that he divide the inheritance with me –Luke 12:13. Jesus refused to side with him. Instead, He spoke to the covetous heart that was causing the anxiety. If Christ gives us wealth, we do not need to feel guilty. If He takes it, we do not need to feel anxiety. In the midst of the storm, we are exhorted …to be of good cheer: for there shall be no loss of any man’s life among you, but of the ship –Acts 27:22. This was ministered as healing balm to the bedraggled sailors, but to those who feel inclined to protect their property it is a sordid saga. When the rich young ruler was offered salvation in exchange for his earthly collection of trinkets, …he went away sorrowful: for he had great possessions –Matthew 19:22. Those of us who become anxious at the loss of our wealth are no less foolish.

…Perfecting our Plan

We set out on a course. Maybe we change jobs, enter into a relationship, or embark upon some new avenue of ministry. We have launched out in faith and before we know it, we are struggling. The winds and waves of ordinary life seem to be working against us. We have expectations that are not being met and it seems that Christ is not doing His part. It is not Christ, but rather it is our expectation that is the cause of our anxiety. We expect much from our investments and it is discouraging to see our efforts go for naught. Martha’s pulse quickened at the lack of help she was receiving in the kitchen. Her frustration rose while her well-planned meal remained unfinished. Her complaint is no less accusing than the disciples’ while rowing in the sea. …Lord, dost thou not care that my sister hath left me to serve alone? bid her therefore that she help me –Luke 10:40. Her anxiety was not caused by Mary’s neglect nor Christ’s indifference. Her sister was docked at the haven of rest while Martha battled the tumultuous emotions within her heart. So does the perfectionist create his own storm when his unfulfilled vision falls short of his expectations. But Christ is more concerned about faith-filled bosoms than water-filled boats.

…Pleasing all People

The Scriptures have taught us well to love our neighbor as ourselves, but that does not insinuate that we must strive and aim for their approval. It feels wonderful to be liked. It is painful to be rejected. Thus, many souls spend their waking hours seeking the approval of others. They must dress like, act like, talk like, and live like their peers. These live a life laden with stressful waves of anxiety. A flurry of “what ifs” arrive with each new acquaintance. There is no ship more fragile than a relationship. No matter how great a sacrifice we make to be loved, we will eventually encounter a disappointing squall sucking us down to the depths of despair. When our best efforts fail us and our best friends derail us, we must bring our battered vessel to the haven of rest. Inconvenient, unfortunate, unpleasant, and annoying relationships will always exist. We shall do much better to make excuses for others’ poor behavior than for our own. When we can rebuke the winds that arise within our own minds, we will immediately find ourselves at the desired haven.

There remaineth therefore a rest to the people of God. For he that is entered into his rest, he also hath ceased from his own works, as God did from his. Let us labour therefore to enter into that rest… –Hebrews 4:9-11.

큰 바람이 일어나 파도가 배에 부딪쳐 배에 물이 가득한지라, 예수께서 배의 뒷부분에서 베개에 엎드려 주무시더니 저희가 깨우며 이르되 선생이여 우리가 망하리니 상관이 없으시나이까 하니 예수께서 일어나 바람을 꾸짖으시며 바다더러 이르시되 잠잠하라 고요하라 하시니 바람이 그치고 매우 큰 잔잔함이 있더라. 이에 이르시되 어찌하여 이렇게 무서워하느냐 어찌하여 너희에게 믿음이 없느냐 저희가 몹시 두려워하여 서로 말하되 이 사람은 어떠한 사람이기에 바람과 바다도 순종하는가 하니라. 마가복음 4:37-41

나는 이 본문을 여러 번 읽으며 여기서 무엇을 얻어야 할지 궁리해 왔다. 이 이야기는 풀어주는 것보다 더 많은 질문을 낳는 것처럼 보인다. 우리는 종종 예수님을 삼위일체의 친화적인 면, 곧 우리와 전능하신 하나님 사이의 중개자 같은 분으로 생각하고 싶어 한다. 그러나 여기 성경 본문에서 그분의 행동은 인간적 잣대로는 도저히 생각하기 어려운 것이다. 어떻게 그리스도께서 그런 폭풍 중에, 더구나 물이 배에 차는 가운데서 잠을 주무실 수 있는가? 우리가 그분이 바람과 바다의 주인이어 명령하시면 복종한다고 믿을 수는 있지만, 그분이 우리에게도 똑같이 기대하시는가? 자비로운 그리스도께서 그런 절체절명의 위기에서 우리에게 차분하고 두려움이 없기를 바라실까? 모든 두려움의 표시는 우리의 믿음 부족의 열매인가? 이러한 물음들은 불안하게 한다. 우리 모두 그분에 대한 믿음이 우리의 구원을 확보하기에 충분히 강하길 바라지만, 삶의 어려운 목초지를 걷는 우리의 경험은 제자들의 괴로운 울음소리 이상을 산출한 적이 거의 없다.

어찌하여 이렇게 무서워하느냐 어찌하여 너희에게 믿음이 없느냐—이 질문들은 구세주께서 하시기에는 다소 어울리지 않는 것처럼 보인다. 마치 우리가 기대했던 것만큼 인내하시지 않는 분처럼 느껴지기도 한다. 그러나 그리스도는 제자들에게 도달 불가능한 기대를 두신 것이 아니다. 그분은 제자들에게 폭풍을 스스로 꾸짖으라 하셨는가? 더 일찍 깨우라 기대하셨는가? 조용히 노를 저어 자신 있게 계속하라 기대하셨는가? 여기 성경은 몇 마디 답만을 제공하지만, 두려움과 믿음에 관해 지속되는 교훈이 있음을 우리는 안다.

폭풍은 인생의 흔한 일부이며 어떤 중대한 곤경도 즐거운 것은 아니다. 바울이 로마로 항해할 때 그들은 …며칠 동안 해나 별이 보이지 아니하며 큰 풍랑이 우리에게 덮치니 우리가 구원을 얻을 소망이 전부 끊어졌더니 –사도행전 27:20. 흐리고 희망이 끊긴 가운데서도 한 가지 맑고 분명하게 울리는 종소리가 있다. 가장 끔찍한 상황 가운데서도 붙잡을 수 있는 평강이 있다는 것이다. 바울은 …하루와 밤을 깊은 바다에서 지내었고 –고린도후서 11:25라는 불안한 체험을 했으나 바람과 바다를 자기 권세로 굴복시키라 요구하지 않았다. 오히려 그는 그 폭풍 중에 …이 밤에 내 곁에 하나님의 사자가 서서 내가 누구의 것이며 누구를 섬기는 줄을 말하며 이르되 바울아 두려워하지 말라… –사도행전 27:23-24.고 말한다. 이것은 오늘 본문에서 제자들이 겪는 위험과 유사한 장면이지만 결과는 달랐다. 바울은 위로와 칭찬을 받았으나 제자들은 꾸짖음을 받았다.

잠깐 물의 무덤에 빠질 위기에 놓여 있었던 제자들이 외쳐 이르되 …선생이여 우리가 망하리니 상관이 없으시나이까 –마가복음 4:38.라고 하였다. 우리 모두가 분노와 책임을 타인에게 전가하는 것이 얼마나 자연스러운가를 알 수 있다. 어떤 무관심한 사람이 책임을 회피한다고 생각하는 것은 매우 낙담스럽다. 같은 방식으로 …선장이 그에게 이르되 네가 무슨 일을 하는 것이냐 잠자는 자여 일어나 네 하나님께 구하라 혹시 하나님이 우리를 생각하사 우리가 망하지 아니하게 하실까 하니 –요나 1:6.

선장의 꾸짖음의 어조에는 잠든 요나에 대한 꾸짖음과 매우 유사한 날카로움이 있는 듯하다. 그리스도께서 우리에게 환난을 허락하시는 것을 기뻐하시는 것은 아니지만, 그분의 평강이 우리의 영혼에 넘치게 할 수 있는 다른 진실한 수단이 없는 것 같다. 먼저 골짜기가 있어야 우리가 산꼭대기를 소중히 여길 수 있지 않겠는가? 먼저 가시가 있어야 우리가 장미를 기쁘게 누릴 수 있지 않겠는가? 먼저 폭풍이 있어야 그 잔잔함을 감사히 여길 수 있지 않겠는가? 바울도 …측량할 수 없이 눌리고 능력을 넘어서서 사는 것까지 절망하였고 –고린도후서 1:8. 같은 절망을 겪었으나 그는 가슴 속에 영혼의 환상적 닻을 지니고 있었다.

이는 그가 명하사 바람을 일으키게 하시며 그 물결을 높이시나니 저희가 하늘로 오르고 다시 깊은 곳으로 내려가고 그 환난으로 인하여 그 영혼이 녹는다. 주리며 비틀거리며 취한 사람 같이 비틀거려 정신이 어둡다. 이에 그들이 환난 중에 여호와께 부르짖으매 그가 그의 환난에서 면하게 하시며 그 풍랑을 잔잔케 하사 그 물결이 잔잔하여지게 하시매 저희가 기뻐하니 여호와가 저희를 자기 원하던 피난처로 인도하셨도다 –시편 107:25-30.

바라던 피난처…

어쩐지 우리는 바라던 쉼터가 어떤 폭풍이 없는 지상의 유토피아라는 생각을 받아들여 왔다. 로마로 향하던 배를 인도하던 선장은 …그 항구가 겨울을 나기에 편한 곳이 못 될 줄을 생각하고 … 저희가 목적을 이룬 줄로 생각하여 –사도행전 27:12-13 항해를 시작했는데, 온화한 남풍의 암시에 첫 징후가 보이자 출항한 것이다. 그러나 그리스도께서 권하시는 피난처는 근심 많은 두려움과 초보적인 믿음으로부터 자유로운 항구다. 이는 세상이 주는 것과 같지 아니한 평강을 내가 너희에게 주노니 너희는 마음에 근심하지도 말고 두려워하지도 말라 –요한복음 14:27. 이 쉼은 그리스도와 함께 항해하며 각 폭풍을 통과하도록 그분께서 인도하실 것을 신뢰함으로써 얻는 것이다.

시련의 끈질긴 폭풍은 경고 없이 갑자기 …유라클리돈이라는 심히 급하고 심한 바람 –사도행전 27:14.처럼 일어날 수 있다. 이러한 격심한 바람들은 어떤 관계든 동요시키는 놀라운 대담성을 지녔다. 스트레스 상황에서 긴장하고 경계하는 것은 인간 본성이다. 우리의 중추 신경계는 아드레날린이라는 강력한 호르몬을 체내로 방출시키며 근육은 긴장하고 정신은 집중되어 싸움이나 도피에 대비하게 된다. 이것은 반드시 불안은 아니며 자연스러운 반응이다. 인간으로서 우리는 극도의 열정과 압박 가운데서도 이성적으로 판단할 수 있는 신성을 부여받았다. 제자들은 예수께서 무엇을 하실지 알지 못했다. 그들은 다만 이 상황이 통제 불능임을 알았을 뿐이다. 여기서 그들은 중대한 실수를 범했다. 그리스도는 누가 주관하시는지 아셨다. 바울도 누가 주관하시는지 알았다. 요나조차 왜 폭풍이 일어났는지 알았다. 불안이 증폭되어 우리가 치러야 할 시련을 우리가 통제해야 한다고 생각할 때 우리의 믿음은 실패하게 마련이다. 우리는 고귀한 의도와 진실한 마음을 가졌을지라도 흔들리는 믿음으로 지쳐버릴 수 있다. 우리는 하나님이 하늘에 앉아 아무 일도 하지 않는다고 잘못 놀라지만, 우리의 기도가 충실히 올라가도 하늘은 대담하게 침묵하는 듯 보인다. 우리는 우상 숭배자들이나 배교자들에게서 그런 일을 기대할 수 있지만, 거듭나 교회에 규칙적으로 출석하고 성경을 읽고 날마다 기도하는 신실한 사람들에게 그런 일이 있어서는 안 된다. 우리는 하나님이 우리의 환경적 평화에 그렇게 관심을 두시는 것이 아니라, 우리의 내적 영혼이 그분의 쉼터에 안전하게 도달하는지를 더 염려하심을 다시 생각해야 한다.

우리가 행복할 때 우리는 그 쉼을 기쁜 마음으로 주장하지만, 실제로는 그분이 진정으로 필요하다고 느끼지 않을 때가 많다. 그분의 개입은 종종 방해처럼 느껴진다. 그러나 때가 절박하고 우리가 모든 자원을 다 소진하면 우리는 그분께 간절히 의지한다. 그 고통스러운 시간에 그분은 종종 우리의 성실함을 시험하시고 아무것도 제공하지 않으신다… 아무 것도 아닌 침묵만을. 배 안에서 잠자시는 그리스도. 우리가 가장 필요로 할 때 바로 그때 주무신다. 그리고 물으신다, 어찌하여 이렇게 무서워하느냐? 어찌하여 너희에게 믿음이 없느냐? 솔직히 말해 이것은 나에게 힘들고 심지어 냉정하게 느껴지며 보통 내가 예수께 기대하는 성품과는 다소 동떨어진다. 그러나 그 질문에는 답해야만 한다. 그 질문에 답하는 것이 그분의 쉼터에 들어가기 위해 필요하기 때문이다. 바람은 그분에게 순종하지만 우리에게는 순종하지 않는다… 혹은 순종하는가? 우리는 분명히 날씨나 환경, 상황 또는 주변 사람들을 통제할 수 없다. 그러나 이런 외적 요인들이 우리의 불안의 근본 원인은 아니다. 우리의 불안은 우리 자신의 그릇된 예감에서 비롯되어 우리의 영혼을 두드리며 평강의 문으로 들어가는 것을 막는다. 배를 공포로 몰아넣는 바람들은 밖에서 몰려오는 것이 아니라 내면에서 분출된다. 이 불안은 불신의 파도 위를 타고 다니며, 그리스도는 계속하여 신성한 잠에 있으시다가 우리가 불안의 근원을 깨닫고 믿음으로 소리칠 때까지 기다리신다. 이러한 네 가지 강한 바람은 우리가 조금만 자극을 받아도 일어난다—우리가…

…자기 보존을 유지하려 함

건강하고 가정과 재정이 순조로우면 우리는 상황을 잘못 해석하기 쉬울 수 있다. 순항이 하나님의 호의의 표지이고 환난이 그분의 불쾌의 신호라고 믿는 것은 잘못이다. 모든 선하고 온전한 은사는 하나님께로부터 오지만 쇠약하게 하는 폭풍도 그 범주에 들 수 있다. 우리의 개인적 환경은 일시적이지만 우리의 영혼은 영원하다. 하나님은 종종 우리의 개인적 편의를 소모하여 우리의 믿음을 확장하신다. 그러나 우리의 인격이 격하될 때 큰 두려움이 일어난다. 많은 공포증은 실제 위험이 부재한 가운데 발생한다.

  1. 고소공포증이 있는 사람은 높은 곳에서 떨어질 것이라는 두려움을 가지고, 그 장소가 안전하고 잘 보호되어 있어도 떨어질 가능성을 과대평가하여 괴로워한다. 수많은 다른 사람들이 그곳에 성공적으로 섰다 해도 그는 이 두려움에 갇혀 있으며, 이는 그가 위험에 처했기 때문이 아니라 떨어질 가능성을 심하게 과대평가하고 진실을 믿기 거부하기 때문이다.
  2. 동물공포증은 동물에 대한 두려움 속에서 살며, 찢겨 죽거나 내장이 드러날 것이라는 장면을 마음속에 만들어낸다.
  3. 폐쇄공포증은 좁고 작은 장소를 두려워하고, 광장공포증은 넓은 곳을 두려워한다.
  4. 아라치부티로포비아는 땅콩버터가 입천장에 붙는 것을 두려워하는 공포증이다.

공포증 대상과 맞섰을 때 그 사람은 심장이 빨리 뛰고 숨이 거칠어지며 입이 마르고 땀이 나며 어지럽거나 현기증을 느낄 수 있다. 따라서 그들의 공포증은 그들에게 현실이 된다. 대부분은 자신의 결함을 변명하지만 진실은 이 불안이 근거 없다는 것이다. 우리가 자기 보존을 변명하고 그것을 채워주면 두려움은 필연적이다. 제자들은 자신들이 멸망할 것이라 두려워했으며 예수님은 그들에게 왜 그러하냐고 물으셨다. …떠나는 것이 차라리 낫고 그리스도와 함께 있는 것이 더욱 좋다 –빌립보서 1:23가 아니겠는가. 우리가 삶을 그리스도께 맡길 수 있다면 죽음도 맡기지 못하겠는가?

무릇 자기 생명을 구하려 하는 자는 잃을 것이요 나와 복음을 위하여 자기 생명을 잃는 자는 찾으리라 –마가복음 8:35.

…재산을 지키려 함

외형상 그리스도의 삶은 기록된 바대로 가장 고난이 많은 삶 중 하나였다. 여우는 굴이 있고 공중의 새는 둥지가 있거늘 그는 흔들리는 배의 뒤편에 베개를 놓고 눕고 끊임없이 부딪치는 파도 아래에서 신음하였다. 그러나 그의 내적 안식처는 유리 같은 바다였다. 이는 부분적으로 그가 보호할 재산이 없었기 때문이다. 심지어 배도 빌린 것이었다. “돈이 많으면 걱정도 많다”라는 옛 속담처럼 부가 떨어지면 불안이 증가한다. …무리 중에 한 사람이 이르되 선생님이여 내 형에게 유산을 나눠 주라 하소서 –누가복음 12:13. 예수께서는 그 편을 들어주지 않으셨다. 대신 그분은 불안을 일으키는 탐욕스러운 마음에게 말씀하셨다. 그리스도께서 우리에게 재물을 주시면 우리는 죄책감을 느낄 필요가 없다. 그가 재물을 거두시면 우리는 불안할 필요가 없다. 폭풍 속에서 우리는 권면을 받는다: …담대하라. 너희 중 어떤 사람의 생명은 잃지 아니하리라 단지 배뿐이리라 –사도행전 27:22. 이것은 지친 선원들에게는 치료의 향유로 봉사했지만 재산을 지키려는 사람들에게는 불쾌한 이야기다. 부자 청년이 그의 지상 소유를 대가로 구원을 제안받았을 때 …그가 큰 재산이 있으므로 근심하며 가니라 –마태복음 19:22. 재산을 잃음에 불안해하는 우리도 어리석음을 면치 못한다.

…계획을 완성하려 함

우리는 어떤 항로를 설정한다. 직장을 바꾸거나 관계를 시작하거나 어떤 사역의 새 길을 떠날 수 있다. 우리는 믿음으로 출발했고 어느새 우리는 고군분투하고 있다. 일상 생활의 바람과 파도가 우리를 거스르는 것처럼 보인다. 우리의 기대가 충족되지 않고 그리스도께서 제 역할을 하지 않는 것처럼 느껴진다. 문제가 그리스도에 있는 것이 아니라 우리의 기대가 불안의 원인이다. 우리는 투자에 많은 것을 기대하고 우리의 노력이 헛되이 가는 것을 보고 낙담한다. 마르다는 부엌에서 도움을 받지 못함에 맥박이 빨라졌다. 잘 계획된 식사가 끝나지 않자 그녀의 좌절감이 일어났다. 그녀의 불만은 바다에서 노를 젓던 제자들의 불평만큼이나 책임을 묻는 것이었다. …주여 내 누이가 나를 혼자 두고 섬기게 하였으니 나보고 그에게 말하여 도와주게 하소서 –누가복음 10:40. 그녀의 불안은 마리아의 소홀함이나 그리스도의 무관심 때문에 생긴 것이 아니었다. 그녀의 자매는 이미 쉼터에 도착해 있었고 마르다는 마음속의 격렬한 감정과 싸우고 있었다. 완벽주의자는 자신의 이루지 못한 비전이 기대에 미치지 못할 때 스스로 폭풍을 일으킨다. 그러나 그리스도는 물에 찬 배보다 믿음으로 가득한 가슴을 더 염려하신다.

…남을 기쁘게 하려 함

성경은 이웃을 자기 자신처럼 사랑하라 가르치지만, 그것이 우리가 반드시 다른 사람의 승낙을 얻기 위해 애써야 한다는 뜻은 아니다. 좋아하는 사람으로 보이는 것은 기분이 좋다. 거부당하는 것은 고통스럽다. 그래서 많은 영혼들이 깨어 있는 시간 내내 타인의 승인을 구한다. 그들은 동료들과 같이 입고, 같이 행동하고, 같이 말하고, 같이 살려고 한다. 이런 사람들은 스트레스의 파도로 가득한 삶을 산다. 새로운 지인마다 온갖 “만약에”라는 생각들이 밀려온다. 관계만큼 깨지기 쉬운 배는 없다. 사랑받기 위해 아무리 큰 희생을 하더라도 결국 우리를 절망의 나락으로 끌어내리는 실망스러운 폭풍을 만나게 된다. 우리의 최선이 실패하고 가장 친한 친구가 우리를 탈선시킬 때 우리는 상처 입은 배를 쉼터로 가져가야 한다. 불편하고, 불행하고, 불유쾌하고, 성가신 관계는 항상 존재할 것이다. 우리는 타인의 잘못된 행동을 변명하는 것이 우리 자신의 잘못을 변명하는 것보다 훨씬 낫다. 우리의 마음 속에서 일어나는 바람을 꾸짖을 수 있을 때 우리는 즉시 바라던 피난처에 있음을 발견할 것이다.

그러므로 하나님의 백성에게는 쉬는 것이 남아 있도다. 혹 쉬는 데 들어간 자는 또한 자기 일을 그치었은즉 하나님의 하심과 같이 하였느니라. 그러므로 우리가 저 안으로 들어가기를 힘쓰자… –히브리서 4:9-11.
